case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 30.09.2007 passed by the High Court Division in Writ petition No. 438 of 2006)
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J. Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 1408 of 2009 and 1161 of 2012 against the judgment and order dated 30.09.2007 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 438 of 2006 making the Rule absolute and the Contempt Petition No.4 of 2013 taken up for analogous hearing are being disposed of by this single judgment and order.

2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the present respondent Nos.1 and 2, as petitioners, filed Writ Petition No. 438 of 2006 before the High Court Division stating, inter alia, that the writ petitioner No.1 is a Non-Government University (IUBAT) recognized and registered under the Non-Government University Act, 1992 (Act No.34 of 1992) in August, 1993 and the writ petitioner No.2 is the Founder and Vice-Chancellor of the writ petitioner No.1 University; that upon recommendation of the Ministry of Education the writ respondent No. 1 RAJUK by memo dated 13.12.1994 allotted 15 bighas of land to the writ petitioner No.1-IUBAT; that as the land was beyond the flood control dam and under water and undeveloped the writ petitioner No.1 by letter dated 29.12.1994 requested the RAJUK to reduce the price taking into account the development cost, but RAJUK expressed its inability to reconsider the price and kept the price of developed land and demanded the same 0 price for undeveloped land and rescheduled the time for payment by memo dated 05.09.1995 and that the last installment was to be paid on 30.09.1999; that the writ-petitioner No.1 IUBAT informed the Ministry of Education that permanent location of IUBAT Campus would be at Plot No.4, Sector No.10, Uttara Model Town, Dhaka-1230; that IUBAT started its classes and official functioning at the said address from January, 2004 and IUBAT has no office at its previous address at House No.135, Road No. 9/A, Dhanmondi R/A, Dhaka-1209; that the IUBAT paid Tk.89,01,699/- being the first installment on 30.09.1995; that on 29.12.1995 IUBAT wrote to RAJUK requesting for the supply of the site plan and lease deed against payment of requisite charges and accordingly RAJUK supplied the site plan with approval date shown as on 07.08.1994.

3. The writ petitioners further stated that instead of giving possession of 15 bighas of land, RAJUK gave possession of only 13 bighs 13 kathas 10 chattaks of land; that the land in question is disputed and is subject to litigation being Title Suit No.162 of 1996 and Misc. Appeal No.148 of 1996 filed by one Golam Azam and others; that on 22.05.1996 the IUBAT wrote to RAJUK for the construction of Embankment. Drive Road which is the approach road to Plot No.4 along with other roads on the south and northern sides as well as provision of utilities and the IUBAT also made a prayer to RAJUK for filing up the land by letter dated 01.06.1996; that Local Government and Engineering Division (LGED) on 07.03.1996 gave an estimate of the east of earth filling and thereafter RAJUK entered into a lease agreement; that IUBAT by letter dated 01.09.1996 asked for the shortfall in land but RAJUK replied by memo dated 17.10.1996 stating that no extra land could be given because of non-availability of further land adjacent to the allotted plot; the IUBAT again applied by letter dated 27.11.1996 for allotment of extra-land to meet statutory requirements, that on 03.03.1997 RAJUK Board approved the allotment of shortfall in land and by letter dated 11.05.1997 RAJUK allotted the shortfall of two bighas and odd land on condition that after payment of the price lease deed would be executed; that the Lease Deed Form was supplied to IUBAT along with revised lay out plan on Plot No.4 on 28.05.1997; that on 28.06.1997 IUBAT wrote to RAJUK that there was still shortfall in land after measurement whereupon RAJUK wrote on 11.08.1998 to its Uttara field Office to examine the problem of measurement at the field level and in the meantime IUBAT paid Tk. 48,000/- for sanction of building plan and by memo dated 15.07.1998 RAJUK approved the building plan (Annexure-H-6); that RAJUK without giving any reason cancelled the allotment of shortfall land by memo dated 23.09.1998 and in the meantime the land has been registered in the name of IUBAT; that RAJUK by letter dated 14.02.1999 (Annexure-J) demanded payment of all installments regarding the registered land by 31.03.1999 although the last installment at least was not due at that particular point of time and RAJUK refused to grant permission to deposit the second installment and RAJUK threatened to take legal action. This being mala fide the writ petitioners sent a notice of demand of justice but to no avail; that the writ-petitioner Nos.1 and 2 challenged the cancellation of the shortfall and the threatened cancellation of the lease in Writ Petition No.925 of 1999 whereupon a Division Bench of the High Court Division, by the judgment and order dated 21.04.1999 made the Rule absolute and declared memo dated 23.09.1998 canceling allotment of shortfall land and the demand to pay all installments at a time threatening punitive action as intimated by RAJUK vide memo dated 14.02.1999 are illegal and without lawful authority and allowed the writ-petitioners-IUBAT to pay the installments in different times without any interest subject to payment of the same within the period fixed by the Court.

4. The present respondent No.4 preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1546 of 2002 before this Division challenging the aforesaid judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 925 of 1999 wherein this Division dismissed the leave petition on merit with observation.

5. The writ petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 (IUBAT) approached RAJUK vide letters dated 14.12.2002 and 22.12.2003 requesting   to give permission to make payment of the second and the third installments respectively within the stipulated time but the RAJUK refused to accept the same. After dismissal of the leave petition when the writ-petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 requested RAJUK vide letters dated 22.12.2004 and 17.12.2005 to give permission to make payment of the fourth and the fifth installments respectively, RAJUK declined to give any permission. All on a sudden the writ-petitioners came to know that RAJUK had, already cancelled allotment of several plots allotted to different institutions including their land being Plot No. 4, Sector No. 10, Uttara Model Town, Dhaka-1230 pursuant to the decision taken in a meeting held in the Ministry of 1 Home Affairs on 18.12.2005. Earlier on 22.11.2004 RAJUK forcibly entered into the lUBAT Campus with a group of workers and cut down several bamboos and further during Eid holidays on 12.11.2004 the Member (Estate) of RAJUK along with the ADC (Revenue) , Dhaka, a contingent of Police Force and about 500 workers entered into the IUBAT Campus at Uttara breaking down the boundary wall and destroyed temporary constructions with CI sheet roofing built for laboratories of different Departments of the University. After the approval of the building plan by RAJUK the first phase of construction of the academic cum-administrative building of the University as per RAJUK approved plan has been completed and the building has a foundation of 15 (fifteen) floors for future expansion and IUBAT has spent an approximate amount of Tk. 14 (fourteen) crores for the construction so far and that IUBAT shifted its campus to the present address in December, 2004 and started classes therein from January, 2005. IUBAT has a number of resident faculty members from different countries like Canada and United Kingdom and it has earned a lot of fame for providing education of international standard. IUBAT is a full member of the Association of Commonwealth University (ACU). In the meeting held on 10.07.2007 Tabligue Jamat was given 109.01 acres of land out of RAJUK's acquired land of 169.28 acres of land. The quantum of land allotted to Tabligue Jamat is 109.01 plus 12.78 acres, in total 121.79 acres of land.

6. A Division Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order dated 30.09.2007 passed in Writ Petition No. 438 of 2006 made the Rule absolute.

7. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order pissed by the High Court Division the writ respondents preferred the instant Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1408 of 2009 before this Court. However, the third party petitioners, being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, preferred the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1161 of 2012 before this Division.

8. A devoted follower of Tabligue Jamat who is also involved in the management of "Bishwa Istema Ground" (Bishaw Istema Math) and an Advocate of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, High Court Division, being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division preferred the instant Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal stating, inter alia, that due to world wide impact of Bishaw Istema it has become a necessary to expand its area and as such the Government took initiative to allot more land for Bishaw Istema and accordingly some allotments made earlier with regard to lands in the western side of the Turag river including the writ petitioners' plot were cancelled vide RAJUK memo dated 09.01.2006 with assurance to the allottee to grant alternative plot on emergency basis; that the writ petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 preferred Writ Petition No. 438 of 2006 challenging the 9. cancellation of allotment; that RAJUK contested the Rule in that writ petition but did not file any affidavit-in-opposition; that a copy of the notice was sent to Ahale Sura Tabligue Jamat, Kakrail, Dhaka but the learned Advocate for the respondent RAJUK failed to give any cogent reason for canceling plot of IUBAT; that because of global importance of Bishaw Istema the Muslims from all over the world are corning to Bangladesh and it has become impossible to manage it at the eastern side of Turag River as a result of which the Government has decided to allot some lands from the western side of the said river after canceling existing allotments and at the same time it has decided to allot equal quantum of and on emergency basis to the affected allottees; that accordingly, allotments were made but due to pendency of the writ petition and an order of stay, injunction and status-quo, the case of the writ petitioners cannot be considered or alternative plot; that for maintaining law and order situation during Bishaw Istema the western side of Turag River is very much essential and as such the Ministry of Home Affairs at its meeting held on 18.12.2005 made some recommendations vide its Minute No. 19(ka) and accordingly, RAJUK in its General Meeting No.16 of 2005 decided to cancel previous allotments; that the Divisional Commissioner of Dhaka Division made a report regarding lands at the western side of the River Turag on 16.05.2007 wherein it was recommended that RAJUK should take immediate measures to file an appeal against the judgment passed in writ petition but no step was taken by RAJUK; that RAJUK vide its Board Meeting No. 05 of 2007 decided to allot an institutional plot measuring 5 acres in favour of the American International University, vide its minute No.85; that the "Bishaw Istema Math" is situated at the eastern side of the Turag River for holding namaz but for lack of space the people are being compelled to stand in front of the Imam for prayer in the Western side of the river which is contrary to Sariah and canons of Islamic laws and regulations but the "Mimbor" cannot be shifted to the western side of the River due to existence of the present establishment and boundary walls of the writ-petitioner No.1 and therefore, for the sake of millions of people it is necessary to take possession of the land occupied by the writ petitioner-University; that Bishaw Istema is not only important as a religious event but also a very important source of earning foreign currencies, since thousands of foreigners from all over the world regularly come to Bangladesh for joining Bishaw Istema; that the IUBAT can easily transfer their campus after getting alternative plot, therefore they will have no occasion to sustain any loss and injury; that the Rule issued in the writ petition ought to have been discharged for the ends of justice; that although a copy of the impugned notice of cancellation of allotment was served upon the Ahlay Sura Tabligue Jamat, Kakrail, Dhaka yet they were not made parties in the writ petition and it is curious enough that the basis of the order of cancellation of allotment was not revealed before the High Court Division causing great difficulties, irreparable loss and injury to pious Muslims and therefore the present petitioners herein seek permission to file the instant Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal; that the American International University was also allotted an alternative plot; that other than these two institutions none of the other allottes raised any objection considering the welfare of the millions of people and reputation of the country and in particular welfare of the Muslims from all over the world; that the matter involves great public interest and as such the petitioners are appearing as the 3rd party petitioners affected by the impugned judgment and order not for their own benefit but in the public interest for the benefit of the people at large.

9. Mr. Mahbuhey Alam, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner-RAJUK in C.P No.1408 of 2009 on 14.09.2012 has submitted that the writ petitioner-respondent No.1 is not prejudiced by the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division inasmuch as the respondent No. 1 was given alternative plots and as such the impugned judgment and order is not sustainable in law and leave should be granted. Then he has submitted that about 30 lacs Muslims from all over of the world have been assembling at "Tongi Bishaw Istema Math" and most of the people have been using the Approach Road from Tongi-Ashulia Embankment Road to the west bank of the Turag River for going to the other side of the river in the "Bishaw Istema Math" but because of encroachment and obstruction by the respondent No.1 people who are coming to join Bishaw Istema cannot use the Approach Road (passage) from Tongi-Ashulia Embankment Road towards the west bank of the Turag River and thereby the Musallies of the Bishaw Istema have been suffering very badly and because of this encroachment Musallies of the Bishaw Istema of Tabligue Jamat have to use an alternative road to go to the "Bishaw Istema Math" from the Tongi-Ashulia Embankment Road taking a diversion road of more than 1 kilometre in length. Mr. Mahbubey Alam has finally submitted that to avoid difficulty and in the interest of the public the highest authority of the Government in various Ministries decided to use the Approach Road (passage) from Tongi-Ashulia Embankment Road to the west bank of the Turag River towards the "Bishaw Istema Math" and to cancel the allotments given to different institutions and to give alternative plot to the writ petitioners-respondents and others since public interest prevailed over individual interest and as such leave should be granted in the instant case.

10. Mr. Rafique-ul-Huq with Dr. M. Zahir and Mr. N. Amir-ul-Islam, the learned Senior Advocates appearing on behalf of the respondents has made submissions defending the judgment. Dr. Zahir has submitted that cancellation of allotment of plots in favour of the respondent No.1 was made without lawful authority. On 03.12.2012 Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners in C.P. No.1408 of 2009 has submitted that because of his personal embarrassment he has decided to withdrew himself to represent the petitioners and that RAJUK would appoint another Advocate who would make necessary submissions on the next date of hearing. However, subsequently, Mr. A.F.M. Mesbahuddin, the learned Senior Advocate, having appeared with fresh power on behalf of the petitioner in C.P. No.1408 of 2009 submitted that he has received instruction from his client not to press the leave petition in view of RAJUK decision in its Meeting No. 01/2013 wherein it was decided that the cancellation of allotment of plots shall not be applicable to IUBAT which is an "institution" and not a "person". At this stage the Court wanted to know from Mr. Mesbahuddin, the learned Senior Advocate what prompted RAJUK to change their decision in respect of the cancellation of allotment of the disputed plot and this Court by its order dated 12.1 2.2012 directed the Chairman, RAJUK to appear in person before this Court on 24.01.2013 to apprise the Court as to the latest stand of RAJUK in the matter. In compliance with the order of the Court the Chairman, RAJUK appeared-in-person before the Court on 24.01.2013 with an Affidavit-in-compliance of the Court's order dated 12.12.2012 referring to the resolution of 01/2013. General Meeting of RAJUK wherein it was decided that since the allotment of the disputed plot was cancelled by order of the Home Ministry and that subsequently the Home Ministry decided that cancellation of plot would not be applicable to IUBAT and consequently RAJUK has agreed to withdraw the order of cancellation of allotment of land being plot No.4 in favour of IUBAT.

11. However, Mr. Sheikh Fazle Noor-Taposh, the learned Advocate for the third party-petitioner in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1161 of 2012 has submitted that the impugned judgment and order emphasized on the point that the learned Advocate on behalf of RAJUK could not show any cogent reason for cancellation of the allotment of plot of the writ petitioner respondent but the real fact is that it was cancelled for allotting the same in favour of Tabligue Jamat for facilitating the people in general and the Musallies of "Bishaw Istema" and as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division suffers from non-application of mind and the same is liable to be interfered with for the ends of justice. Then Mr. Fazle Noor-Taposh has submitted that the "Mimbor" for holding namaz is situated on the east bank (eastern side) of the Turag River but for lack of space the people are being compelled to stand in front of the Imam for prayer, which is contrary to Sariah and canons of Islamic Law and that "Mimbor" cannot be shifted to the west bank of the River due to existence of the present respondent No. 1's establishment and boundary walls which were constructed illegally and therefore for the sake of public interest and to help millions of people it is necessary to recover  the land occupied by the IUBAT for the use of the Tabligue Jamat Mr. Taposh has further submitted that Bishaw Istema is not only important as a religious event but also the second largest congregation of the Muslims from all over the world after the holy Hazz and therefore, to mange such a huge congregation and to facilitate the local and the foreign Musallies a clear entrance (approach road) and exit route from the Tongi-Ashulia Embankment Road to the west bank of the Turag River towards the "Bishaw Istema Math" is desperately required and that to give accommodation to the foreign Musallies the land in question is urgently required on which the reputation of the country largely depends and the inconvenience, if any, to be sustained by the IUBAT is comparatively lower than the difficulty faced by the Government in managing the affairs of Bishaw Istema on the East Bank of the Turag River keeping in view of the country' s reputation and solidarity with the Muslim Ummah. He has submitted that the respondent No.1-University can easily transfer their campus to Purbachal after getting alternative plot from RAJUK who has already expressea it's decision to allot the same in Purbachal and that the respondents will have no occasion to sustain any loss and injury and as such the Rule issued in the writ petition ought to have been discharged for ends of justice. Then referring to Article 104 of the Constitution he has submitted that the Appellate Division have the power to issue such directions orders, decrees or writs as may be necessary for doing complete justice in any cause or matter pending before it and the present case is such an unique one which deserves exercise of such power in the public interest for the welfare of the Muslim Community all over the world. He has further submitted that because of the change of portfolio of the immediate past Minister for Home Affairs in the Government the policy of Government cannot be changed. He has finally submitted that since in the instant case an Inter-Ministerial Committee headed by the Home Minister had decided to cancel the allotment of plots in favour of the respondent No.1 and others and accordingly the allotment of the respondent's land was cancelled as such the present incumbent Minister for Home Affairs is not competent to withdraw the order of cancellation in the absence of the other functionaries of the state.

12. During the course of hearing Mr. Sheikh Fazls Noor-Taposh, the learned Advocate for the petitioners in Leave Petition No.1161 of 2012 has submitted that since the respondent No.1 encroached and obstructed the 100-feet Approach Road (passage) from Tongi Ashulia Embankment Road to the west bank of the Turag river which had been constructed and left open for the use of the people in general and the Musallies of Bishwa Istema, the respondents be directed to remove the obstruction demolishing the wall and other structures if any, for facilitating the people in general and the Musallies to use the Approach Road (passage) from Tongi-Ashulia Embankment Road to the west hank of the Turag River towards the "Bishaw Istema Math".

13. After hearing both the parties this Division by an order dated 12.12.2012 directed the respondents not to obstruct the 100-feet Approach Road (passage) from Tongi-Ashulia Embankment Road to the bank of the Turag River towards the "Bishaw Istema Math".

14. Subsequently, on 24.01.2013 the petitioners of the Leave Petition No.1161 of 2012 filed a Contempt Petition under Article 108 of the Constitution for drawing up proceedings for Contempt of Court against the respondent Nos.1-2 who are the Vice-Chancellor and Registrar of the IUBAT-writ-petitioners. The petitioner filed the contempt petition, stating, inter alia, that they filed the Leave Petition No. 1161 of 2012 against the judgment and order dated 30.09.2007 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 438 of 2006; that this leave petition is being heard analogously with the Leave Petition No. 1408 of 2009 by this Division; that during the hearing of these leave petitions on 12.12.2012 this Division was pleased to direct the authorities of International University of Business, Agriculture and Technology (IUBAT) not to obstruct the use of 100-feet wide Approach Road (passage) of RAJUK situated to the west bank of the Turag river within Dhaka District, which is presently under the illegal occupation of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 for the use of the people in general and the Musallies of the Bishwa Istema of Tabligue Jamat and keep it open till 24.01.2013; that the said order was: passed by this Division in presence of the respondents and their learned Advocates; that the respondents not only violated the order passed by this Division but also made construction and carried out repairing works willfully during the aforesaid period which is evident from the photographs taken on 18.01.2013 marked as Annexure-A to the Contempt Petition; that the sketch map prepared by some Civil Engineers and Architects with regard to the Approach Road in question, is in consonance with the final survey conducted in presence of the contemner No. 1 for allotting land of IUBAT has been attached along with the aforesaid final survey report dated 19.05.1996; that the contemners in their application for acceptance of supplementary paper book dated 23.01.2013 denied any existence of 100 feet wide road in question in the RAJUK layout plan at its paragraph No. 4 regarding which this Division passed its order dated 12.12.2012; that their statements are evidence of their commission of contempt which entails taking of strict measures for the ends of justice; that the respondent Nos. 1and 2 willfully flouted the order dated 12.12.2012 passed by this Divisions in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 1161 of 2012 and 1408 of 2009 showing disregard and disrespect to this Division, the order of the Apex Court of the country, cannot be disregarded or undermined in any way and the same renders strict measures to ensure rule of law and high standing of the judiciary and thereby to enhance confidence of the people both at home and abroad upon the judiciary and administration of justice in Bangladesh; that the petitioner No.1 tried to take shelter of the local administration and filed a G.D. Entry before the concerned Police Station, namely, Uttara West Police Station informing about the non-compliance of the said order passed by this Division on 12.12.2012 but the same was not accepted by the Officer-in-Charge of that police station for reasons best known to him; that if the contemnors cannot be taken to task the dignity of this Court will be at stake and the people's confidence upon the Court will greatly be shaken.

15. Accordingly, this Court issued Rule calling upon the respondent Nos.1 and 2 to show cause as to why proceedings of contempt shall not be drawn against them for violation of the order dated 12.12.2012 passed by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos.1161 of 2012 and 1408 of 2009 directing the authorities of the International University of Business, Agriculture and Technology (IUBAT) not to obstruct the use of 100 feet passage of 1 RAJUK situated to the west bank of the Turag river at Tongi within Dhaka District now under their occupation by the Bishaw Istema Musallies and keep it open till 24.01.213.

16. However, Mr. Nurul Huda, the Chairman, RAJUK appeared in person before this Court on 24.01.2013 and stated that in view of letter dated 14.11.2012 issued by the. Ministry of Horne Affairs, the RAJUK decided to withdraw the order of cancellation of the allotment of plot in favour of the IUBAT authority subject to payment of all dues with interest by the IUBAT authority. In support of his statement   he has submitted RAJUK's Memo dated 21 .01.2013 which is as follows: -

রাজধানী উন্নয়ন কর্তৃপক্ষ (জোনাল অফিস)

উপ-পরিচালক (এস্টেট-২) এর কার্যালয়

উত্তরা, ঢাকা-১২৩০।

বিষয়ঃ IUBAT এর অনুকূলে বরাদ্দকৃত উত্তরা আবাসিক এলাকার ১০নং সেক্টরের এ্যামব্যাম্কমেন্ট রোডের ০৪ নং প্লটের বরাদ্দ বাতিল আদেশ প্রত্যাহার প্রসঙ্গে।

কর্তৃপক্ষের ০১/২০১৩তম সাধারণ সভার সিদ্ধান্ত। উপর্যুক্ত বিষয় ও সূত্রের প্রেক্ষিতে আদিষ্ট হয়ে জানানো যাচ্ছে যে, স্বরাষ্ট্র মন্ত্রণালয়ের নির্দেশে প্লটটি বাতিল করা হয়েছিল। বর্তমানে স্বরাষ্ট্র মন্ত্রণালয় হতে জানিয়েছে যে বর্তমানে স্বরাষ্ট্র মন্ত্রণালয় হতে জানিয়েছে যে তাদের এ সিদ্ধান্ত IUBAT এর জন্য প্রযোজ্য হবে না। সার্বিক বিষয়ে পর্যালোচনা সাধারণ সভায় নিম্নোক্ত সিদ্ধান্তে উপনীত হন।

রাজউকের সকল পাওনা সুদসহ IUBAT কর্তৃক প্রদান সাপেক্ষে বরাদ্দ বাতিল আদেশ প্রত্যাহার করতে রা্জউক সম্মত থাকবে।

উপর্যুক্ত বিষয়টি মহামান্য আদালতকে অবগত করার জন্য IUBAT এর লোকেশন ম্যাপও এতদসঙ্গে সংযুক্ত করা হলো।

22. The report dated 16.05.2007 in respect of the lands of the west bank of the Turag river Annexure-4 to the Leave Petition No.1161 of 2012 submitted by a committee headed by the Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka recommended to the following effect:

যদিও বিগত ৪০ বৎসর যাবৎ ইজতেমায় আগত দেশী-বিদেশী মেহমানগন নদীর উভয় পাড়ের জমি একইভাবে ব্যবহার করে আসছে, কিন্তু ইজতেমা অনুষ্ঠানের পরবর্তী সময়ে এই জমিগুলো আবারো বেদখলে চলে যায়-যা আদৌ কাম্য নয়। অন্যদিকে ইজতেমা ময়দানের কাঠামোগত উন্নয়ন ও অন্যান্য সুযোগ-সুবিধা বৃদ্ধি পাওয়ায় ভবিষ্যতে মুসল্লীগণের সংখ্যা দিন দিনই বৃদ্ধি পাওয়ায় অবিষ্যতে মুসল্লীগণের সংখ্যা দিন দিনই বৃদ্ধি পেতে থাকবে একথা অনস্বীকার্য। ফলশ্রুতিতে এখন হতেই ইজতেমা ময়দানের পরিসর সম্প্রসারণের পরিকল্পনা গ্রহণ করা জরুরী। এক্ষেত্রে ইজতেমা মাঠ সংলগ্ন চতুর্পাশ্বের সরকারী জমি ইজতেমা মাঠের আওতাভুক্ত করার কোন বিকল্প নেই। তবে ইজতেমা ব্যবস্থাপনার সুবিধার্থে বিষয়গুলো স্থায়ী নিষ্পত্তি হওয়া প্রয়োজন। ----------

বিশ্ব ইজতেমা কর্তৃপক্ষের পক্ষ থেকে জানান হয় যে, সাম্প্রতিককালে ইজতেমার বিশ্বের ৭০ টি থেকে ৯০ টি দেশের ৬-১০ হাজার মোমেনসহ ৫০ লক্ষ লোকের সমাগম হয়ে থাকে। বিশ্ব ইজতেমা ও সারা বছরব্যাপী বিভিন্ন দাওয়াতী মজমার গুরুত্ব উপলব্ধি করে বিগত ৪০ বছর যাবত বিভিন্ন সরকার টংগী ময়দানের জমি তাবলীগ জামাতের অনুকূলে বরাদ্দ প্রদানের প্রতিশ্রুতি দিয়ে আসছে। ১৯৯৫ রাজউক তুরাগের পূর্ব তীরের ১৬০ একর জমি তাবলীগ জামাতকে ব্যবহারের অনুমতি দেয়। কিন্তু ২০০৫ সালে ‘রাজউক’ কতিপয় ব্যক্তি ও প্রতিষ্ঠানকে তুরাগের পশ্চিম পাড়ের প্রায় ৪০ বিঘা জমি (যা দীর্ঘদিন যাবৎ তাবলীগের কাজে ব্যবহৃত হয়ে আসছে) বরাদ্দ দেয়া পরবর্তীতে স্বরাষ্ট্র মন্ত্রণালয়ের নেতৃত্বে সরকারের যে ৭০/৮০ টি বিভাগ/ সংস্থা প্রতি বৎসর ইজতেমার আয়োজন ও অন্যান্য সমাবেশ অনুষ্ঠানে সহায়তা দিয়ে থাকে, তাদের সর্বসম্মত সিদ্ধান্ত ও সুপারিশের পরিপ্রেক্ষিতে ‘রাজউক’ উক্ত বরাদ্দ বাতিল করেু (বরা্দ্দ প্রাপকদের বিকল্প জমি বরাদ্দের প্রতিশ্রুতি দিয়ে) উক্ত জমি তাবলীগ জামায়াতের ব্যবহারের জন্য সিদ্ধান্ত নেয়। কিন্তু পুরো জমির দখল তাবলীগ জামাত এখনও পায়নি।

বিগত ২৫/০২/০৭ তারিখ স্বরাষ্ট্র মন্ত্রণালয়ের অনুষ্ঠিত আন্তঃমন্ত্রণালয়, বিভাগ/সংস্থার ইজতেমা সংক্রান্ত মূল্যায়ন সভায় সর্বসম্মতক্রমে প্রস্তাব করা হয়েছে যে, তুরাগ নদীর পূর্ব, পশ্চিম ও দক্ষিণ পাড়ের জমি যা ইতোমধ্যে ইজতেমার জন্য ব্যবহার হয়ে আসছে তা অবিলম্বে তাবলীগ জামাতের অনুকূলে স্থায়ীভাবে বরাদ্দ দেয়া হোক এবং আগামী ইজতেমা থেকে সুমলীমের স্থান সংবুলানের জন্য ইজতেমা মেম্বার ও কিছু থিত্তা (জিলা ভিত্তিক অবস্থান স্থল) তুরাগের পশ্চিম পাড়ে আশুলিয়া সড়ক সংলগ্ন জায়গায় স্থানান্তরিত করা হোক। এ প্রস্তাব বাস্তবায়নের জন্য ঢাকা বিভাগীয় কমিশনারের নেতৃত্বে একটি আন্তঃবিভাগীয়/ সংস্থা কমিটি গঠন করে আগামী ইজতেমার পূর্বে তা বাস্তবায়নের দায়িত্ব দেয়া হয়েছে।”

23. It appears that in view of the decision of a meeting of 70/80 Departments / Divisions of different Ministries of the Government headed by the Ministry of Home Affairs, the RAJUK cancelled the allotment of plots in favour of different institutions including the respondent No.1-University in order to facilitate the public at large and the Musallies of the Bishaw Istema of Tabligue Jamat to use the land. In an Inter-Ministerial Meeting held in the Ministry of Home Affairs on 25.02.2007 it was resolved that the land situated to the east, west and south bank of the Turag river which has been used by the Musallies of Tabligue Jamat should be permanently allotted to Tabligue Jamat and the Mimbor of the Istema and some of the khitta (District wise tents) be transferred to the West bank of the Turag river adjacent to the Tongi-Ashulia embankment Road. An Inter-Departmental Committee headed by the Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka was constituted to take necessary steps before the next Bishaw Istema. In the report dated 16.05,2007 amongst others the following observations were made:

“যদিও IUBAT এবং আহছানিয়া মিশন হাসপাতালের মধ্যবর্তী প্লটটি ইজতেমার মাঠে প্রবেশ ও প্রস্তানের একটি সহজ সংযোগ সড়ক হিসাবে স্বীকৃত কিন্তু কিছু অংশ IUBAT এর দখলে থাকায় এবং তা নিয়ে মহামান্য আদালতের মামলা অনিষ্পন্ন থাকায় সড়কটির কোন স্থায়ী রুপ দেয়া যাচ্ছে না। কিন্তু ইজতেমায় সমাগত সুসল্লীদের যাতায়াতের সুবিধার্থে এই রাস্তাটির একটি স্থায়ী নিষ্পত্তি হওয়া প্রয়োজন।”

26. From the foregoing discussions we find that admittedly the RAJUK allotted land of the east bank of the Turag River to Tabligue Jamat as "Bishaw Istema Math" and according to the lay out plan admittedly there was a 100-feet approach road from Tongi-Ashulia Embankment Road to the west hank of the Turag River towards the "Bishaw Istema Math". It appears from the materials on record that subsequently the approach road (entrance) was occupied illegally by the respondent-University (IUBAT). Though possession of the additional land has not been handed over to the IUBAT for not making full payment of the price of the same. Even from the surveyor's report of RAJUK dated 02.12.2012 it has transpired that 13 bighas 13 kathas 13 chataks and 5 square feet of land was handed over to the respondent University and subsequently,  an additional amount of 2 bighas and odds lands was allotted to the respondent University. But possession of the additional plot of land was not handed over to them for not full payment of the price. We also find that considering the importance of the Road the then Minister of Home Affairs who happened to be the Local Member of the Parliament by her letter  dated 19.05.2009 stated that the earth work of the link road from the Embankment road of sector 10 to the west bank of the Turag river had been completed by RAJUK.

27. But the construction of concrete work of the said road had not been made by RAJUK for which the Musallies of Bishaw Istema have to suffer untold difficulties for rain during Bishaw Istema. Accordingly, she has requested the Chairman, RAJUK to complete the concrete work of the Approach Road (passage) from Tongi-Ashulia Embankment Road to the west bank of the Turag river towards the 'Bishaw Istema Math" for the use of the people in general and the Musallies of Bishaw Istema.

28. Earlier by repeated reminders, the IUBAT requested RAJUK for allotment of 1 bigha and 6 katas of land to make up a total 15 bighas to fulfill the maximum stationary requirement of land for Non-Government University. But RAJUK by memo dated 17.10.1996 refused to allot on the ground that “উপরোক্ত প্লটের পার্শ্বে বরাদ্দকৃত অতিরিক্ত খন্ড জমি না থাকায় বরাদ্দের কোন অবকাশ নাই।” However, the IUBAT got allotment of additional land of 2 bighas 9 kathas 10 chataks 20 squire feet from  RAJUK by memo dated 11,01.1997 on condition that “বরাদ্দকৃত জমির মূল্য প্রতি বিঘা টাঃ ১৬,০০,০০০/- (টাকা ষোল লক্ষ) মাত্র হারে টাঃ ৩৯,৭২,২২৩/- (টাকা উনচল্লিশ লক্ষ বাহাত্তর হাজার দুইশত তেইশ) মাত্র আগামী ৩০.০৬.৯৭ইং তারিখের মধ্যে সোনালী ব্যাংকে, রা্জউক ভবন শাখা, ঢাকায় এককালীন জমা করিয়া জমাকৃত টাকার ব্যাংক রশিদ রাজউকের এস্টেট শাখায় দাখিল করিতে হইবে। উক্ত সময়সীমার মধ্যে জমির মূল্য পরিশোধে ব্যর্থ হইলে আর কোন বর্দ্ধিত সময় প্রদান করা হইবে না এবং বরাদ্দ পত্র বাতিল করা হইবে।” In default of payment the allotment of additional land was cancelled. However, at the instance of IUBAT in Writ Petition No. 925 of 1999 the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 21.04.2002 declared the cancellation of allotment of additional land and demand to pay all installments at a time as communicated by RAJUK letter dated 14.02.1999 as illegal and without lawful authority. The appellate Division by judgment and order dated 27.10.2004 passed in Civil Petition for Leave, to Appeal No.1546 of 2002 affirmed the aforesaid judgment and order of the High Court Division. However, the IUBAT could not make the full payment of the price of the land. Considering the acute shortage of land of the Bishaw Istema Math of the Tabligue Jamat, the allotment of several plots allotted to different institutions including the petitioner's land in plot No. 4 of Sector 10, Uttara Model Town was cancelled by memo dated 09.01.2006 issued by the RAJUK. However, the IUBAT successfully challenged the aforesaid cancellation in Writ Petition No. 438 of 2006 wherein a Division Bench of the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 30.09.2007 made the Rule absolute declaring the order of cancellation of allotment of plot No. 4 without lawful authority. We have to dispose Civil Petition No. 1408 of 2009 and C.P. No. 1161 of 2011 which have arisen out of the impugned judgment and order dated 30.09.2007. The very existence of the 100 feet Approach Road is evident by the statements made in the application dated 08.02.2007 on behalf of the writ petitioner for restoration of status quo ante, Supplementary Affidavit dated 11.02.2007 on behalf of the writ petitioner IUBAT, application dated 02.04.2007 on behalf of the writ petitioner for a direction on writ respondent No.6 not to disturb the possession of the writ petitioner in the university premises, application dated 22.01.2007 on behalf of the writ petitioner for injunction and restoration of status quo ante. But according to the IUBAT the 100 feet Approach Road was forcibly made open by the RAJUK officials with the help of police and the Musallies of Tabligue Jamat. But this is a disputed question of fact which can he not proved in writ jurisdiction. However, the very existence of the 100 feet Approach Road between plot No.3 and plot No.4 can easily, be seen front the original layout plan.

<u>29. On perusal of the original layout plan dated 28.02.1994 of RAJUK, Survey report of RAJUK dated 19.05.1996, the report dated 16.05.2007 of the Committee beaded by the Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka in respect of the recovery of the west bank land of RAJUK by evicting illegal occupants there from, minutes of the meeting dated 19.06.2009 under the Chairmanship of the Deputy Commissioner, Gazipur and minutes of different meetings of RAJUK it transpires that there is a 100 feet Approach Road (passage) from the Tongi Ashulia Embankment Road to the west bank of the Turag river towards the "Bishaw Istema Math" in between the plot No. 4 allotted to the IUBAT and Plot 3 allotted to the Ahsania Mission Cancer Hospital. The very existence of the side road has been admitted by IUBAT stating that the layout for the side road is national". From the minutes of the meetings of the RAJUK, the Gazipur District Administration, the Dhaka District Administration and the high powered Istema Management Committee, we find that the approach road was illegally occupied by the IUBAT. These authorities in their meetings expressed concern and resolved to recover the 100 feet approach road (passage) from the illegal occupation of IUBAT. From the materials on record it is obvious that the 'respondent-University trespassed/ encroached into the 100 feet Approach 71 Road (passage) which has been in use for long 40 years by the people in general, Musallies of Bishaw 'sterna, the Government officials and the Senior people who are involved in holding of Bishaw Istema off the "Bishaw Istema Math" which is situated the east bank of the Turag river. It is true that the petitioners in Civil Petition No.1161 of 2012 could not appear before the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 438 of 2006 because they were not impleaded. Against the a impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division RAJUK preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1408 of 2009. But at a belated stage because of change of the Home Minister, the Ministry of Home Affairs by their letter dated 14.11.2012 informed the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works endorsing a copy to the RAJUK stating that the decision dated 18.12.2012 is not applicable to the case of IUBAT which is not a "person". It is true that RAJUK being the petitioner had been diligently pursuing the Leave Petition No.1408 of 2009 since 2009 but for the reasons best known to them they have decided to withdraw their leave petition. But public interest demands that they should not have decided to that extent. However, the third party-petitioners on behalf of the people in general and the Musallies of the Bishaw Istema in particular   decided to prefer Civil Petition No.1161 of 2012 challenging the impugned judgment and order dated 30.09.2007 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 438 of 2006. The leave petitioners being interested in the affairs of the Bishaw Istema of Tabligue Jamat are competent enough to maintain the leave petition. We find merit in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners in Leave Petition No.1161 of 2012. It has also been argued on behalf of the respondents that the leas deed was executed and registered in favour of the respondent University for the whole 15 bighas of land including the land which was marked in the layout plan as the Approach Road from the Tongi Ashulia Embankment Road to the west bank of the Turag river towards the "Bishaw Istema Math". Mr. M. Amirul Islam and Dr. Zahir have contended that there is a six storied building on the premises of the University, Library, Cafeteria and other establishments on the disputed land so it would be very harsh to dislodge the respondent-University from the disputed land wherein they had spent more than Tk.14 crores in the development and construction of the University Building. Here we are confronted with two conflicting public interests, on the one hand, the rights of the people in general and the Musallies of the "Bishaw Istema Math" to use the land as prayer ground and Approach Road and on the other hand the rights of the owners of the Non-Government University to use the land in question for the use of the University which is imparting education to the students and thereby disseminating knowledge. When thee is a conflict between two kinds of public interests the Court has a duty to assess the gravity of the two interests and find out the way in which direction the balance yields to locate the larger public interest. Generally, it is a difficult task to find out the larger public interest. But in the instant case it has been noticed that the IUBAT prevailed upon the RAJUK to get allotment of additional land of two bighas nine kathas ten chattaks twenty square feet of land vide RAJUK's Memo dated 11.05.1997 (Annexure-H). Clause 3 of the Allotment letter dated 11.05.1997 reads as under:</u>

<u>১। জমির মূল্য পরিশোধের পর দখলী গ্রহনের তারিখ হইতে ৯০(নব্বই) দিনের মধ্যে রাজউকের আরোপিত শর্তাবলী সন্নিবেশীত স্টানডার্ড লীজ ডিড ফরমে লীজ দলিল সম্পাদন ও রেজিষ্ট্রী করিয়া দিতে হইবে।</u>

<u>২। --------------------------</u>

<u>“৩। রাজউক প্রয়োজন বোধে নগর পরিকল্পনার আলোকে এলাকায় সুবিন্যাস লে আউট প্লান পরিবর্তনের অধিকার সংরক্ষন করিবে। ইহাতে কোন ওজর আপত্তি উথ্যাপন করা চলিবে না।” It appears that by granting the allotment of the additional land the RAJUK deprived the people in general and the Musallies of the Tabligue Jamat from-the use of the Approach Road. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, we are required to dispense justice between the rights of the people in general and the Musallies from both home and abroad and on the other hand the rights of the owner of the Non-Government University which is imparting education the students and thereby disseminating knowledge.</u>

<u>30. It is to be noted that according to the Final Survey Report dated 19.05.1996 of RAJUK the IUBAT received 13 bighas 13 kathas 10 chattaks and 5 square feet area of land instead of 15 bighas of allotted land, Thus there was a shortage of one bigha, 6 kathas, 5 chattaks, 40 square feet of land. The IUBAT had made repeated representations including Memo dated 01.01.1996 to allot additional land of one bigha and six kathas. But in fact IUBAT got allotment of 2 bighas and odds land which is much more quantity then the statutory requirement of 15 bighas of land for the campus of a Non-Government University. In the facts and circumstances of the case, we invoke Article 104 of the Constitution to exercise the extra-ordinary power of this Division to issue such directions or orders in the cause or matter pending before it for doing complete justice to the respective parties, In that view of the Matter we direct Goth the RAJUK and the IUBAT to keep open 40 feet Approach Road instead of the original 100 feet wide road from the Tongi Ashulia Embankment Road to the west bank of the Turag river towards the Tongi Istema Math by demolishing wall and or other structures, if any, from the Southern side of the allotted plot No. 4 thereby modifying the layout Plan of the area within two months from the date of the receipt of a copy of this judgment and order. If the respondent-IUBAT fails to comply with the order expeditiously then BAJUK is further directed to demolish any obstruction or structures to keep open the Approach Road in accordance with law. In the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the opinion that allotment of the additional land including the Approach Road (passage) in favour of the respondent-University in contravention of the original Layout Plan of 1994 is without lawful authority. Admittedly the contention of the petitioner of Leave Petition No. 1161 of 2012 is corroborated by the final survey report dated 19.05.1996 issued by the RAJUK. Here, we are concerned with two conflicting public interests.</u>

<u>31. Firstly, the public interest in respect of right to use of the Approach Road (passage) from Tongi-Ashulia Embankment Road to the west bank of the Turag river towards the "Bishaw Istema Math" and secondly, the establishment of the university (IUBAT) on the allotted land and encroachment on the Approach Road by IUBAT in getting allotment of additional land defying the need of the people in general and the Musallies of the "Bishaw Istemas Math" of the Tabligue Jamat in particular. We are of the view that the public interest would be best served if the people in general and the Musallies of Bighaw Istema of Tabligue Jamat are allowed to use a 40 feet wide Approach Road (passage) instead of 100 feet wide Approach Road (to the southern side of Plot No.4 between Plot No.4 and Plot No.3) from the Ashulia Embankment Road to the west bank of the Turag River towards the Bishaw Istema Math. Considering the inconvenience of the students and the authority of the IUBAT, we are not inclined to uphold the order of cancellation of the allotment of land made in favour of the University or dislodge the university from Plot No.4 to an alternative site. However, considering the gravity of the situation and this being a matter of great public importance concerning the right of the people in general and the Musallies from home and abroad who are meeting in the huge congregation of Bishaw Istema twice in every year for the last 40 years to perform their prayer in the Bishaw Istema Math and therefore, invoking the power of complete justice this Division is of the opinion that in the interest  of justice a 40 feet wide Approach Road (passage) should be kept open for the people in general and the Musallies of the Bishaw Istema of the Tabligue Jamat in particular.  Accordingly, the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 be directed to demolish the wall and other structures which had been constructed on the land of the original 100 feet wide Approach Road (passage) for keeping open a 40 feet wide Approach Road for the use of the people in general and the Musallies of Bishaw Istema of the Tabligue Jamat which has been in use for more than 40 years. Leaving the land of 40 feet wide Approach Road open and uninterrupted the rest of the land of the additional allotment and land of Plot No. 4 in modified plan should be used and possessed by the respondent-University which shall be deemed to have satisfied the statutory requirement of land of the University campus.</u>

32. In view of the above discussions and findings we are of the view that interest of justice would be best served if the respondents be directed to hand over the 40 feet wide Approach Road (between plot No.4 and Plot No.3) keeping it open and uninterrupted for the use of the people in general and the Musallies of Bishaw Istema of Tabligue Jamat in the west bank of Turag river towards the Bishaw Istema Math.

33. For the foregoing reasons, we do thereby direct the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 to restore the 40 feet wide Approach Road from the Tongi-Ashulia Embankment Road to the west bank of the Turag River towards the "Bishaw Istema Math" by demolishing and or breaking the wall and or other structures, if any, on the Approach Road adjacent to the southern side of IUBAT (Plot No. 4) and keep the said road open and uninterrupted and hand over the same to RAJUK for the use of the people in general and the Musallies of the Tabligue Jamat within 2 months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment and order. In the event of any failure to comply with the order of this Division the RAJUK is directed by this order of mandamus to demolish the wall, and other structures, if any, on the land of the 40 feet wide Approach Road and make it ready, open and uninterrupted for the use of the people in general and Musallies of Bishaw Istema Tabligue Jamat in particular.

34. Further, the respondent Nos. 1 to 3 are directed to pay outstanding installments, if any, to RAJUK within 2 months from the date of the receipt of a copy of the judgment.

<u>35. The unconditional apology tendered by the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 are accepted and they are warned to be cautious in future while dealing with such order of this Court.</u>

36. With the above observations and directions the leave petitions and the contempt petition are disposed of.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Surendra Kumar Sinha, CJ.:- Delay in filling the petition is condoned. 

2. This petition is directed from a judgment of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.271 of 2003. By this judgment the High Court Division made the rule absolute and directed the writ respondent to implement the order dated 15.04.1999 passed by the Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka in G.R. Case No.1425 of 1997 releasing gold bars and ornaments seized from the possession of the petitioner. 
3. We have perused the order in G.R. Case No.1425 of 1997, the police report, the pleadings in Writ Petition No.271 of 2003 and the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. Admittedly, the respondent-Md. Mozibur Rahman was carrying 42 gold bars each weighting ten tolas and 76.50 grms of ornaments on 26.07.1997 through Hazrat Shahjalal Airport. He was a passenger coming from Singapore by Biman Bangladesh Airlines. He did not declare the gold bars and when he was crossing the green channel, the Customs Authority suspected him and on search the gold bars were recovered.

4. Though a charge sheet has been submitted against him, he was acquitted by the learned Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. Since smuggled gold were recovered from his possession, a departmental proceeding under the Customs Act was drawn up and the Customs Authority confiscated the gold bars and sold the gold bars. The High Court Division set-aside the said order and directed to hand over the possession of the gold bars. 

5. On perusal of the materials, we find a clear case of smuggling has been committed by the respondent any event, the respondent cannot take back the gold bars and also avoid the criminal proceedings. He was illegally acquitted by the Magistrate. Even after such acquittal, the Customs Authority has power to dispose of its departmental proceedings and if it is found that the gold bars have been smuggled into Bangladesh, it can confiscate the same. The High Court Division on a misconception of law has directed to release the gold in failing to notice that the respondent did not declare the gold to the Customs Authority. He was taking away the gold by deceitful means and therefore, all the ingredients of smuggling are present in this case. 

6. Mr. Abdul Matin Khashru, learned Counsel however, submits that the respondent Md. Mozibur Rahman has been fighting for the gold since 1997 and if he is again put on trial for smuggling, ends of justice will be defeated. Learned Counsel submits that he has instructions from his client that he will not claim the ownership of the gold bars provided no direction is given for prosecuting the respondent on the charge of smuggling of gold. In view of the submission of the learned Counsel, we set-aside the judgment of the High Court Division and maintain the order of confiscation of the gold bars. However, on consideration of the sufferings of the respondent Md. Mozibur Rahman, we are not inclined to direct for further prosecution in respect of the offence for smuggling. 

7. This petition is accordingly disposed of with the above observations and direction.

End.
