full_judgment:
Mr. A.N.M. Bashir Ullah J:- This Rule, on an application under Section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure (in short, the Code) at the instance of the defendant No.56 of the suit was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 24.09.2013 passed by the Additional District Judge, 1' Court, Comilla in Civil Revision No.87 of 2010 affirming those dated 18.08.2010 passed by the Assistant Judge, Debiddar, Comilla in Title Suit No.1042 of 2008 rejecting an application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code for the rejection of the plaint should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in short, is that the present opposite party  No.1 Charu Mia as plaintiff filed the above noted suit against 98 defendants naming the present petitioner Md. Shahjahan Bhuiyan in serial No.56 for partition of the suit land claiming 0.6650 acres of land out of 8.38 acres of partitionable land. The defendant No.56 appearing in the suit filing written statement controverted the claim of the plaintiff and also filed another application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code for rejection of the plaint averring inter alia that the entire suit property is wakf property but the plaintiff tactfully canceling the said fact raised his claim for the suit land. The suit is barred under Section 102 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962. The defendant No.56 was made defendant in his personal capacity leaving his legal status as Motowalli of Khan Bahadur Afzalur Rahman Wakf Estate (in short, the Wakf Estate). The plaintiff cannot maintain the suit without seeking decree that the suit land is not wakf property. 

3. It was also averred in the prayer that the suit is hit by the principle of res judicata as Title Suit No.153 of 1976, thereafter, Title Suit Nos.357 of 1984, 47 of 1993 and 9 of 1995 were filed by the plaintiff or by his men claiming the said land as of their own and those suits were decided against the plaintiffs. 

4. The plaint of Title Suit No.357 of 1984 was rejected on 16.01.1989 and plaint of Title Suit No.47 of 1993 was rejected on 08.02.1994 and later on another Title Suit being No.9 of 1995 was also filed for the partition of the suit land. The plaint of the said suit was also rejected on 25.02.1996. Thereafter, against which Title Appeal No.25 of 1996 was filed and the same was also dismissed and as against the judgment of the Title Appeal No.25 of 1995, Civil Revision No.1592 of 1999 was filed in this Court but the Rule of the revision was discharged on 31.05.2007 and the plaintiff moved to the Appellate Division through Civil Petition for Leave to. Appeal No.1263 of 2007 and the same has been decided against the plaintiff on 22.05.2008. 

5. The plaintiff without noticing and stating all the above facts and its result filed the present suit suppressing the relevant facts. Thus, the defendant No.56 prays for rejection of the plaint. 

6. The trial Court upon hearing of both the parties in details rejected the prayer filed by the defendant No.56 holding inter alia, that any suit against the order of the Waqf Administrator in the civil Court is hit or barred under Section 102 of the Waqf Ordinance1962 but the present suit has not been filed challenging any order of the Wakf Administrator. As such, the suit is not barred under Section 102 of the Waqf Ordinance. 
The trial Court also held that the suit is not barred by principle of res-judicata as no suit between the parties previously have been decided finally on the selfsame issue. 

6A. The defendant No.56 as against the said judgment and order of the trial Court below dated 18.08.2010 preferred Civil Revision No.87 of 2010 in the Court of District Judge, Comilla which has been ultimately heard by the Additional District Judge, 1' Court, Comilla who by his judgment and order dated 24.09.2013 affirmed the judgment of the trial Court below. The defendant-petitioner being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and order of the revisional Court below moved this Court and sought leave for filing of this revisional application and accordingly leave was granted and Rule was issued. 

6B. The Rule is contested by the plaintiff-opposite party No.1. 

6C. Mr. Md. Abdus Salam Mondal, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-petitioner supporting the Rule and opposing the judgment of the Courts below submits that 8.38 acres of land appertains to C.S. Khatian Nos.490 and 477 corresponding to hal Khatian Nos1558 and 540 is a Wakf Estate which is known as Khan Bahadur Afzalur Rahman Wakf Estate and within this Wakf Estate there is a mosque and dargah which is locally known as "Utkhara Dargah Share at Debiddar, Comilla. The wakf was created and maintained before operation as wakf by user and the present defendant No.56 was appointed as regular motowalli from 1998 but before 1998 he was official motowalli also of the wakf estate and the wakf estate was enrolled through. Enrolment Case No.9095 and from the time immemorial, the local people have been trying to grab the wakf land in this or that way and as part of the said ill device by this time 4 regular suits have been filed so far save and except the present suit. Those are Title Suit Nos.153 of 1976, 357 of'1984, 47 of 1993 and 9 of 1995 but none of the suit has been decided in favour of the plaintiff so far and against the wakf estate. But even then the plaintiff knowing all the fact and figures regarding the former suits has filed the present test suit again concealing all the facts relating t.0 the suit land. The plaintiff did not make the defendant No.56 as the motowalli of the Wakf Estate. The defendant No.56 after filing of the written statement filed a separate petition under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code for rejection of the plaint mainly on two grounds that the suit is barred by the principle of res judicata and also the suit is barred under Section 102 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962. 

7. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that before filing of the present suit at least 4 persons took vigorous attempt to get the suit land by the former suits but they could not be succeeded and all the former suits were dismissed or the plaint was rejected as the suit land is wakf estate. So the present suit is not maintainable 4nd the plaint is liable to be rejected but both the Courts below committed serious error of law and facts in not rejecting the plaint of the plaintiff. 

8. He next submits that the suit land is a wakf land even before the C.S. record of right and the same has been enrolled through enrollment case (in short, the E.C.) No.9095 and enrolment of a wakf estate is a .formal order from the Administrator of Wakf as to the notification about the wakf estate which was made on 16.02.1998. If the plaintiff disagrees with the said notification dated 16.02.1998 the plaintiff should have filed objection challenging the enrolment of the wakf estate before the Wakf Administration under Section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962 and if his objection is not accepted by the Wakf Administrator he has a right to file a suit challenging the order of the Wakf Administrator under Section 35 of the Ordinance but the present suit is barred under Section 102 of the Ordinance. Section 102 of the Ordinance provides that no decision or order of the Wakf Administrator shall be questioned in any suit or other proceeding in any Court except the provision of this Ordinance. Since the Ordinance has made an avenue that anybody disagrees with the decision of the Wakf Administrator as to the enrollment of any property as Wakf Property he is to file objection before the wakf Administrator and thereafter he reserves the right to file the suit before the civil Court against the order of the Wakf Administrator but the plaintiff without challenging the enrollment of the suit land as wakf land before the Wakf Administrator cannot file a regular suit in the civil Court to get any decree in any form for the wakf property. So, the trial Court as well as the first revisional Court below measurably failed to appreciate the facts and law of the case as well as the provisions of Section 102 of the Waqf Ordinance. So, the judgment of the Courts below is not sustainable in law. 

9. Mr. Md. Shahadat Tanveer Amin, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No.1 supporting the judgment of the Courts below and assailing the arguments made so far by the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that both the Courts below rightly found that the suit is not barred by the principle of res judicata as between the selfsame party on the selfsame issue no suit was finally decided till now. Though somebody else had filed suits on different dates but none of the suit has been decided finally. So, there was no any application of principle of res judicata as laid down in Section 11 of the Code. 

10. He next submits that the 1' revisional Court below rightly held that the plaintiff did not challenge any order of the Wakf Administrator, So, the suit is not barred by under Section 102 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962. 

He also submits that the 1" revisional Court below in his elaborate discussions observed that the person who are interested to consider the suit land as wakf land did not claim the entire 8.38 acres of land as wakf land. Rather they have claimed the land as wakf land on various figures on different times. As such, the revisional Court also held that the plaintiff has been praying for a saham only for 0.6650 acres of land. Since the entire land has not been claimed as wakf land by any quarter so the plaintiff might have prayed for those small portion of the land within the suit lands. 

11. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite party also submits that a plaint can be rejected relying on the facts end statement of the plaint itself and not taking any fact either from the written statement or from an application filed by the parties and in support of his such contention he refers the case of Abdul Malek Sawdagar Vs. Md. Mahbubey Alam and others 57 DLR(AD) 18 and also refers the case of Syed Shah Mohammad Osman Ghani Vs. Bangladesh, through Secretary, Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development and others 39 DLR 451. 

12. I have considered the above submissions and the arguments of the learned Advocates of both the parties with profound attention and have gone through the materials on record. 

13. From the plain reading of the plaint it appears that nowhere of the plaint the plaintiff had articulated any fact regarding the enrolment of the suit land as wakf land. The plaintiff is almost silent regarding the attachment of the suit land with the Wakf Administrator although the plaintiff made Md. Shahjahan Bhuiyan, son of late Abdul Majid Bhuiyan as defendant. No. 56 who happens to be the Motowalli of the wakf properties. The defendant No. 56 appearing in the suit filed petition under Order VII rule 11 of the Code seeking the rejection of the plaint on two grounds. 

14. The 1st ground is that the suit is barred by the principle of res judicata as before the present suit, Title Suit No.153 of 1976 was filed in the 1st Court of Munsif, Comilla. Thereafter, Title Suit No.357 of 1984 was filed in the Court of 2nd Sub-Judge, Comilla and the plaint of which was rejected on 16.01.1989. And a 3rd suit for the suit land was also filed being No.47 of 1993 and the A plaint of which was also rejected on 08.02.1994. The 4th suit for the suit land being No.9 of 1995 was also filed claiming partition of the suit land. The plaint of which was rejected on 25.02.1996 against which Title Appeal No.25 of 1996 was preferred and against the judgment dated 25.02.1996 and the appeal was decided against the plaintiff of that suit thereafter the plaintiff of that suit preferred Civil Revision No.1592 of 1999 in this Court and the same has been decided by this Court on 31.05.2007 affirming the judgments of the Courts below against which Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal being No.1263 of 2007 was filed but the same was also rejected on 22.05.2008. So, for the reasons stated above the present suit is also barred under the principle of res judicata. 

15. The 2nd ground taken by the defendant No.56 for rejection of the plaint is that the suit land has been enrolled as wakf land as such the plaintiff cannot file any suit for the wakf land. If he wants to change the character of the suit land he should have filed. the case before Wakf Administrator under Section 50 of the Ordinance and thereafter if he feels aggrieved by the decision of the Wakf Administrator he is entitled to file the suit in the civil Court under Section 35 of the Ordinance. But without filing of the case before the Wakf Administrator, the plaintiff cannot file any suit to change the character of the wakf land in this or that way. 

16. Now, on the date of hearing of this Rule I invited the learned Advocate for the petitioner to show any judgment of the civil Court between the parties for the present suit which has been decided finally but he ultimately could not show any judgment of any suit which has been mentioned earlier in the judgment. Although there appears 4 suits to have been filed in respect of the suit land but none of the suit was decided finally between the parties for the suit land. The gist of the principle of res judicata as laid down in Section 11 of the Code is that by the same parties in a former suit the issue which is involved in the latest suit has been heard and finally decided by a competent Court: But the defendant-petitioner could not show any judgment or could not place any material to show that between the same parties any suit has been decided finally. So without having much discussions it can safely be said that the suit of the plaintiff 
was not barred by the principle of res judicata. 

17 The 2nd ground taken by the defendant-petitioner in the petition for rejection of 
plaint runs as follows: 
	
	“স্বত্ব দখল বিহীন বাদী নানারুপ মিথ্যা, তঞ্চকী ও বানোয়াট উক্তিতে সত্য গোপনাক্রমে এই মোকদ্দমা আনায়ন করায় তাহা খারিজ হইবে।” 

From the judgment of the Courts below it appears to me that the Courts below did not consider this point of the defendant rather they came to an easy conclusion that no order of the Wakf Administrator has been challenged in the suit land and as such the suit is not barred under Section 102 of the Waqf Ordinance, 1962. In fact, the Courts below did not apply their judicial mind properly in order to investigate this point raised by the defendant No.56. 

18. As I have told it earlier that the plaintiff had filed a suit as if he has no knowledge about the character of the suit land. As such there is no any reflection that either the entire suit land or its part is wakf property or not. The plaint is going to show that the plaintiff sought a saham for 0.6650 acres of land out of total partible 8.38 acres of land which appertains to have been recorded in C.S. Khatian Nos.490 and 477. 

19. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite party No.1 very strongly argued before me that the suit land was recorded in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiff in C.S. record of right and pursuant to the C.S. record of right in S.A. record the suit land has been recorded in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiff and in support of his such contention he referred those khatians filed during the hearing through affidavit-in-reply. 

20. On the other hand the petitioner during the hearing of this Rule filing supplementary affidavit with some papers showed that 8.38 acres of land appertains to C.S. Khatian Nos.490 and 477 corresponding to S.A. Khatian Nos.558 and 540 have been enrolled as wakf property in the name and style of Khan Bahadur Afzalur Rahman Wakf Estate, Comilla through enrollment Case No.9095 and in this connection the Memo No.1023(1), Comilla dated 16.02.1998 issued by the office of the Wakf Administrator is very much relevant to note here. Thus it is evident from the said memo dated 16.02.1998 that the entire 8.38 acres of land which is the suit land also has been enrolled as wakf property. 

21. The plaintiff without admitting the suit land as wakf property filed the present suit for partition seeking a saham as noted earlier. In my consideration the law is almost settled on this point that if any property is enrolled as wakf property and if anybody is aggrieved by the said enrollment he is entitled to challenge the character of the suit land as wakf land before the Wakf Administrator under Section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance and if for any reason he could not be satisfied of the decisions of the Wakf Administrator he is also entitled to file a suit challenging the order of the Wakf Administrator under Section 35 of the Ordinance and in my consideration nobody can without the taking the re-course of the Wakf Administrator under Section 50 of the Ordinance can file case in the civil Court directly for declaration of his status or for any other relief regarding the wakf land and in that view of the matter the suit appears to be a pre matured suit. 

22. Now, if I concede all the arguments of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite party No.1 that the suit land has been recorded both in the C.S. and S.A. record of right in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiff and they have title and arguable case in their favour but even then he is to follow the law of the land to get the appropriate relief and this view has also taken by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, in the case of Syed Masud All and others Vs. Md. Asmatullah and others 32 DLR(AD) 39 wherein it has been held in the following manner: 

"The interpretation that we have given on Section 50, therefore, brings us to the conclusion that if a dispute as to the wakf character of a property is raised either before or at the time of enrolment of after the enrolment, the jurisdiction to decide the wakf character is that of the Administrator. The wakf Ordinance being a special statute provides a special procedure to be followed. The cognizance of the civil Court is to that extent excluded. The exclusion is again enacted in Section 102 of the Ordinance, which is as under”

102. Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Ordinance no decision or order of the Administrator shall be questioned in any suit or other proceeding in any Court." 

It provides that "except as otherwise provided in this Ordinance no decision or order of the Administrator shall be questioned in any suit or other proceeding in any Court." (Para 14 of the Judgment). 

23. From the above noted decision of the Appellate Division it appears that if there is any dispute as to the wakf character of a property either before or at the time of enrollment or after the enrolment the jurisdiction to decide the wakf character is that of the Wakf Administrator. In my consideration the suit property has been enrolled as wakf property, now if the plaintiff finds any disagreement with the enrolment he has the right to challenge the same before the Wakf Administrator under Section 50 of the Ordinance but before going to the Wakf Administrator under Section 50 he cannot file the suit in the civil Court as the same is barred under Section 102 of the Waqf Ordinance. 

24. In this Rule the learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 1 referring the decision of Abdul Malek Sawdagar Vs. Md. Mahbubey Alam and others 57 DLR(AD) 18 submits that whether the plaint is liable to be rejected as being barred by law must be considered from the statement made in the plaint itself and not from the written statement or any other materials other than that has been presented in the plaint. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that though the defendant petitioner filed the application in the trial Court for rejection of the plaint on two grounds that the suit is barred by res judicata and the suit is not maintainable in the civil Court as the suit land is 'a wakf land and now they are not pressing the 1st ground for rejection of the plaint. So the decision of the 57 DLR is not applicable in this Rule and he also referring the case of Rashida Begum Vs. Nurussofa and others reported in 24 BLD(AD) 223 submits that rejection of plaint now is not confined under Section VII Rule 11 of the Code only and in an appropriate case while the proceeding itself is the abuse of the process of the Court, the Court having recourse of Section 151 will be competent to reject the plaint or striking out the part of the relief prayed for, Ongoing to the reported case it appears that the Appellate Division held in the following ways: 

"The law is more or less settled that matter of rejection of plaint is not confined to the provision of Order 11 Rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure, In a fit or appropriate case i.e, while the proceeding initial is an abuse of the process of the Court or a contrive to achieve something which the party failed upon proceeding under the law provided for or in any other case akin to cases as mentioned above the Court taking recourse of the provision of Section 151 would be competent to reject the plaint or strike out part of the relief prayed for or sought in a subsequent suit." (Para 13 of the Judgment) 

Now having regards to the decision noted above it appears to me that the ingredients for rejection of plaint may not be available in the plaint itself but in appropriate case when from the hearing and materials placed by the parties it appears that by filing of a suit and concealing there important and related facts for the suit land the plaintiff has been trying to cause fraud upon the laws of the countries also upon others in such a case the plaint should be rejected under Section 151 of the Code and having regards to the above findings I am of the view that the plaintiff under the grab of a partition suit in fact has been trying to establish that the suit land is not wakf property but in order to achieve this goal by the plaintiff, he is to take the recourse of the remedy as available in Section 50 of the Waqf Ordinance. Thereafter, for any reason if he could not be satisfied of the decision of the Wakf Administrator he is at liberty to come again in the civil Court under Section 35 of the Ordinance. As such, I find that the Courts below committed error of law in not rejecting the plaint that the suit was not maintainable for the bar of Section 102 of the Ordinance read with Section 50 of the same Ordinance.

25. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The plaint of Title Suit No.1042 of 2008 filed in the Court of Assistant Judge, Debiddar, Comilla is hereby rejected. 

26, Let a copy of this judgment and order be sent to the Court concerned for information and necessary action. 

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 29.11.2007 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal in Appeal No. 75 of 2001)
full_judgment:
Md. Muzammel Hossain CJ. This appeal by leave is directed against the judgment and order dated 29.11.2007 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka in Appeal No. 75 of 2001 dismissing the appeal upon affirming the judgment and order dated 26.04.2001 passed by the Administrative Tribunal, Bogra in A.T. Case No. 85 of 2000 dismissing the case.

2. The appellant as petitioner filed A.T. Case No. 85 of 2000 before the Administrative Tribunal, Bogra stating, interalia, that the appellant is a Freedom Fighter and in the competitive examination in 1974 he became fit in the quota of Freedom Fighters and joined the Bangladesh Bank in the post of Examiner Grade-2: that he was promoted to the post of C/N Examiner Grade-1 in 1978 and he was promoted to the post of Assistant Treasurer in 1982 ; that thereafter he was promoted to the post of "Officer Cash" in 1985 and Assistant Manager Cash in 1997; that while he was serving as such he was asked to show cause on 09.03.1999 by the General Manager, Motijheel Office, alleging that "number less and not signed by the Governor 22 notes of 500 Taka denomination was received from two packets of notes cancelled by the appellant on 17.12.1998; that the appellant in reply denied the allegation ; that the authority appointed an enquiry committee on 17.05.1999; that the committee submitted report on 30.06.1999; that then General Manager (Administration), Bangladesh Bank, Principal Office, Dhaka framed charge against the appellant on 19.09.1999; and thereafter denying the allegation the appellant gave reply to the charge on 05.10.1999; that thereafter the appellant was dismissed from service by an order dated 09.12.1999 passed by the respondent No. 4; that the appellant preferred appeal against the aforesaid order to the Governor of Bangladesh Bank on 24.01.2000 and the appeal was rejected on 05.06.2000; that the appellant filled the case before the Administrative Tribunal on 23.11.2000 for setting aside the order of dismissal

3. The respondent No. 4 contested the case by filing a written objection praying for rejection of the petition stating, interalia, that the application filed before the Administrative Tribunal was barred by limitation that the appellant was dismissed from his service on 09.12.1999 after proper enquiry and giving him sufficient time to appear before the Inquiry Officer; that thereafter the appellant filed an application to the Governor of the Bangladesh Bank on 24.01.2000 for reinstating him in the service and that the said application was rejected on 05.06.2000 and the said order was communicated to him on 05.07.2000 ; that since the case was filed before the Administrative Tribunal beyond the period of limitation; the same is liable to be dismissed.

4. The learned Member, Administrative Tribunal, Bogra by the judgment and order dated 26.04.2001 dismissed the case.

5. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order dated 26.04.2001, the appellant preferred an appeal being A.A.T. Appeal No. 75 of 2001 before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka. The Administrative Appellate Tribunal , Dhaka after hearing both the parties by impugned judgment and order dated 29.11.2007 dismissed the appeal affirming those passed by the Administrative Tribunal Bogra in A.T. Case No. 85 of 2000.

6. The present appellant being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and order passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka preferred the instant appeal with leave of this Court.

7. Leave was granted to consider the submissions that the petitioner-appellant was dismissed from service on 09.12.1999 whereupon he filed a representation before the Higher Administrative Authority and that was rejected on 05.06.2000 and thereafter on 23.11.2000 the petitioner appellant filed the case before the Administrative Tribunal i.e. within 6 months from the date of the decision by the Higher Administrative Authority and as such both the Tribunal below erred in law in holding that the case is barred by limitation.

8. Mr. Abdur Rob Chowdhury, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that both the Tribunals misread the provision of Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 as amended by the Administrative Tribunals (Amendment) Act, 1992 and illegally declared that the A.T. Case is not maintainable and as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka is liable to be set aside. He then submits that the Administrative Appellate Tribunal committed an error of law in not taking into consideration that the Administrative Tribunal misread the Administrative Tribunals (Amendment) Act, 1997 and Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980 and illegally dismissed the said A.T. Case. He finally submits that the petitioner-appellant was dismissed from his service on 09.12.1999 and thereafter he filed a representation before the Higher Administrative Authority and that was rejected on 05.06.2000 and then on 23.11.2000 the petitioner-appellant filed the case before the Administrative Tribunal i.e. within 6 months from the date of the decision by the Higher Administrative Authority and as such both the Tribunals below erred in law in holding   that the case is barred by law of limitation and the appeal is liable to be allowed.

9. Mr. Shamim Khaled Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondents submits that according to second   proviso to Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 as amended by the amending Act XXIV of 1997 which came into force on 19.11.1997 the appellant was required to wait for a decision on his departmental appeal for two months i.e. upto 24.03.2000 and he was required to come to the Administrative Tribunals for relief against his dismissal within 6 months. He then submits that the appellant was required to file application before the Administrative Tribunal within 24.09.2000 according t. second proviso to Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 as amended but he filed the application before the Administrative Tribunal on 23.11.2000 i.e. long after the expiry of the period of limitation. He submits that although according to the last proviso to Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 as amended the application before the Administrative Tribunal would have been within time but limitation provided for in the last proviso to Section 4(2) of the said Act is not available to the applicant because the period of limitation in the second proviso to the aforesaid section is the governing provision compared to the last proviso to the said section as per interpolation of the statuary period. He finally submits that the application filed by the appellant before the Administrative Tribunal was hopelessly barred by limitation and the Member of the Administrative Tribunal and the Administrative Appellant Tribunal rightly decided the limitation question against the appellant and as such the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

10. We have heard the learned Counsel for both parties and perused the impugned judgment and order to the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka and also other materials available on record. It appears that the appellant preferred departmental appeal on 24.01.2000 and the appeal was rejected on 05.06.2000 and the A.T. Case was filed on 23.11.2000 for setting aside the order of dismissal. In this context it is pertinent to quote Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980 as amended by the Administrative Tribunals (Amendment) Act, 1997 which provides as under:

"A person in the service of the Republic or of any statutory public authority may make an application to an Administrative Tribunal under sub-section   (1), if he is aggrieved by any order or decision in respect of the terms and conditions of his service including pension rights or by any action taken in relation to him as a person in the service of the Republic or of any statutory public authority.

Provided that no application in respect of an order, decision or action which can be set aside, varied or modified by a Higher Administrative Authority under any law for the time being in force relating to the terms and conditions of the service of the Republic or of any statutory public authority or the discipline of that service can be made to the Administrative Tribunal until such Higher Authority has taken a decision on the matter;

Provided further that, where no decision on an appeal or application for review in respect of an order, decision or action referred to in the preceding proviso has been taken by the higher administrative authority within a period of two months from the date on which the appeal or application was preferred or made, it shall, on the expiry of such period, be deemed, for the purpose of making an application to the Administrative Tribunals under this section, that such higher authority has disallowed the appeal or the application;

Provided further that no such application shall be entertained by the Administrative Tribunal unless it is made within six months from the date of making or taking of the order, decision or action concerned or making of the decision on the matter by the higher administrative authority, as the case may be."

<u>11. It appears that a new second proviso has been inserted after proviso No. 1 in Sub-Section (2) of Section, 4 by the Administrative Tribunals (Amendment) Act 1997 (Act No. 24 of 1997). According to the said amended provision of Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act the appeal pending before the Higher Administrative Authority shall be deemed to have been disallowed by the authority after the expiry of two months from the date of submissions of the departmental appeal and accordingly the appellant ought to have filed the A.T. Case within six months after the expiry of said two months before the Administrative Tribunal but he did not do so and as such the case before the Administrative Tribunal was barred by limitation.</u>

<u>12. In Civil Petition for leave to appeal No. 1454 of 2008, Bangladesh Supreme Court Digest -2009, Volume-XII, Page.10 the fact was that the petitioner was dismissed from service on 24.01.1995. He preferred departmental appeal on 08.02.1915 and it was rejected on 14.01.2001. In the meantime the Administrative Tribunals Amendment Act, 1997 (Act No. XXIV of 1997) came into force on 19.11.1997 whereby new 2nd proviso to section 4(2) of the Act was introduced. This Division approved the view taken by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal that as the amending Act came into force on 19.11.1997 the appeal to the higher authority by the petitioner deemed to have been rejected on 19.01.1998 i.e. before 19.07.1998 but he filed the A.T. Case on 04.06.2001 long after the statutory period of limitation. Therefore, the Administrative Tribunal Case was hopelessly barred by limitation under section 4(2) of the A.T. Act, 1980.</u>

<u>13. In Abul Bashar Vs. Invesment Corporation of Bangladesh and another, 20 BLD (AD) 294 the fact was that the petitioner was an Assistant General Manager of the Investment Corporation of Bangladesh. In exercise of powers under Regulation 56(2) the Investment; Corporation of Bangladesh (Officers and Employees) Service Regulations, 1993 the Investment Corporation of Bangladesh terminated the service of the petitioner, as Assistant General Manager of the Corporation on 23 April 1995. The petitioner challenged the order of termination in Writ Petition No. 921 of 1995. The petitioner   was summarily rejected on 3 May 1995. The thereafter made a civil petition for leave to Appeal before the Appellate Division which was also summarily rejected on 13 December 1995. Being unsuccessful, the petitioner filed case No. 242 of 1995 before the Administrative Tribunal, Dhaka, on 31 December 1995, which was beyond time. He, however, sought to have the benefit of section 14 of the Limitation Act on the ground that the time spent for prosecution of the writ petition and the civil petition for leave to appeal should be excluded in computation of the period of limitation prescribed under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980. This Division held that it is clear from the wording of the second proviso Now that is third after the amendment of 1997) to subsection (2) of section 4 of the Administrative Tribunals Act that the legislative intendment behind this provision is to exclude the proceedings governed by the Administrative Tribunals Act from the operation of the benefit conferred by sub-section (2) of section 29 of the Limitation Act, 1908 and while computing the period of limitation in filing an application before the Administrative Tribunal a person can not have the benefit of section 14 of the Limitation Act, 1908. This judgment justifies that limitation in regard to cases under Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 has to be calculated applying the procedures described in the Act itself and there is very little scope, if not no scope in deviate from the strict rule of limitation embodied in the Act while dealing with Administrative Tribunals cases.</u>

14. From the above discussions and findings we are of the view that both the Tribunals below having considered the materials on record rightly arrived at a correct decision in the matter. Accordingly we do not find any illegality in the impugned judgment and order passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal in affirming those passed by the Administrative Tribunal.

15. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and order dated 29.11.2007 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka in A.A.T. Appeal No. 75 of 2001 is hereby affirmed.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 20th of April, 2008 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka, in A. A. T. Appeal No. 62 of 2003)
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J. This civil appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 20.04.2008 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka in A.A.T. Appeal No.62 of 2003 allowing the appeal, thereby setting aside the judgment and order dated 12.10.2002 passed by the Administrative Tribunal, Dhaka, in A.T. Case No. 24 of 2000.

2. Facts of the case, in brief, are that while the appellant was working as an Inspector of Police under the respondent No. 4, Superintendent of Police, Jhalakathi, he was proceeded against on 16.08.1998 by respondent No.3 on charges of misconduct, inefficiency, negligence of duty and corruption under the provisions of Police Officers (Special Provisions) Ordinance, 1976 and was asked to show cause as to why he would not be dismissed from service.

3. The appellant submitted his explanation to the show cause notice denying all the allegations. Thereafter, the authority issued a second show cause notice on 17.09.1998 calling upon him to show cause as to why he would not be reduced to his previous lower post (Sub-Inspector). The appellant again submitted his reply to the second show cause notice on 27.09.1998. The respondents without considering the reply passed the order dated 06.10.1998 inflicting punishment by reducing the appellant to lower post of Sub-Inspector for two years.

4. Thereafter, the appellant preferred a departmental appeal to respondent No. 1 who upheld the above order of punishment reducing him to the post of Sub-Inspector for ever vide his order dated 12.08.1999 (communicated on 24.08.1999).

5. Against the orders dated 06.10.1998 and 12.08.1999, the appellant preferred A.T. Case No. 24 of 2000 before the Administrative Tribunal, Dhaka on 08.02.2000, which upon hearing the parties by its order dated 12.10.2002 allowed the case of the appellant declaring the order of punishment as illegal, void, without jurisdiction and is of no legal effect with a direction to reinstate the appellant to his previous post, that is Inspector of Police from the date of his reduction to the lower post and to grant him arrear salary and other attending benefits.

6. Being aggrieved by the order of the Administrative Tribunal, the respondents preferred A.A.T. Appeal No. 62 of 2003 before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka, which upon hearing the parties concerned, was allowed. Hence, the petitioner filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1297 of 2008.

7. Leave was granted to consider the following submissions of the learned advocate appearing for the petitioner:

"I. The order of the Administrative Tribunal, Dhaka, was pronounced on 12.10.2002 and against the said order, appeal was preferred before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka, on 23.04.2003 that means after expiry of 6 months. According to section 6 (2) and 6 (2A) of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980, appeal against the impugned judgment, order or decision passed by the Administrative Tribunal must be filed in all circumstances not later than 6 months from the date of the impugned order or judgment. But having violated the mandatory provisions of sections of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980, appeal was preferred before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka, against the order dated 12.10.2002 passed by the Administrative Tribunal, Dhaka and as such the judgment and order dated 24.04.2008 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka, has occasioned failure of justice.

II. The Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka, observed that the Administrative Tribunal case was filed by the petitioner beyond the statutory period of limitation as laid down in the second proviso of section 4(2) of the said Act, 1980. But the said observation of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka, is not correct. Because the petitioner filed the administrative tribunal case on 08.02.2000 that is within 6 months from the appeal order dated 12.08.1999 passed by the respondent No.1. As the petitioner challenged the appeal order and the Tribunal also set aside the appeal order dated 12.08.1999 and so the application before the Administrative Tribunal was within time and considering these facts and circumstances of the case the judgment and order dated 20.04.2008 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka, has occasioned failure of justice; and

III. The petitioner who was the Inspector of Police was a second class Gazetted Officer. But it appears from the impugned order and other connected documents on record that the authority did not consult with the Public Service Commission before passing the impugned order of reduction to lower rank which is a major penalty. So, on this score the impugned order of punishment is not tenable in law. But the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka without considering the said aspect passed the impugned judgment merely on point of limitation and as such the same has occasioned failure of justice.

8. Mr. Nurul Amin, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant sub-mined in line with the grounds of appeal and further expanded his arguments stating that the finding of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal that the case filed before the Administrative Tribunal was barred by limitation is erroneous, since the petitioner's appeal was decided on 12.08.1999 and the case before the Administrative Tribunal was filed on 08.2.2000 which is within the period of limitation. He also submitted that the order passed by the appellate authority reducing the appellant's rank to a lower post for ever is also unconscionable and illegal. Moreover, he submitted, the appellate   authority did not decide upon the appellant's appeal within time and as such the final order passed by the appellate authority, by which his punishment was enhanced, is of no legal effect. The learned Advocate further submitted that the appeal filed by the Government before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal was beyond the period of six months allowed under section 6(2A) of the Act. He submitted that, therefore, the judgment and order of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal is itself without jurisdiction and illegal, and hence, liable to be set aside.

9. Mr. Biswajit Deb Nath, learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the respondents submitted that clearly the appellant's application before the Administrative Tribunal was barred by limitation since he was required by law to file the application within a period of eight months from the date of preferring appeal before the appellate authority, since according to the second proviso of section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act (the Act, 1980) the appeal was deemed to have been disallowed after two months of filing that appeal. In support of his contention he has referred to a decision of this Division in the case of Md. Nazimuddin vs Government of Bangladesh and ors reported in 17 BLC (AD)10.

10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgment and order as well as the evidence and materials on record.

11. It appears that by the order of the authority dated 06.10.1998 the appellant was demoted to his lower rank for a period of two years, against which he filed appeal before the authority, namely the Government, on 13.10.1998. The appellate authority by order dated 12.08.1999 demoted the appellant to his lower rank for ever. The appellant then filed a case before the Administrative Tribunal on 08.02.2000 challenging both the orders dated 06.10.1998 and 12.08.1999. However, the requirement of the law as enunciated in the second proviso to section 4(2)of the Act, 1980 is that the case before Administrative Tribunal must be presented within six months of the decision of the appellate authority, and if the authority does not make a decision on the employees appeal within two months of the appeal being filed, it will be deemed to have been disallowed and the case before the Administrative Tribunal must be filed within a period of six months therefrom, i.e. within eight months from the date of filing the appeal.

12. In the facts of the instant case, it appears that the appellant filed his appeal before the appellate authority on 13.10.1998, and therefore, on 13.12.1998 his appeal would be deemed to have been disallowed and the appellant was required by law to file his case before the Administrative Tribunal by 12.06.1999. The records show that the appellant filed the case before the Administrative Tribunal on 08.02.2000 which is beyond the period of limitation provided by the Act, 1980.

13. The point of limitation was elaborately discussed in the case of Md. Nazimuddin vs Government of Bangladesh and ors reported in 17 BLC (AD)10 where two of us were sitting. It is clear that the appellant's case filed before the Administrative Tribunal was barred by limitation, as observed in the decision referred by the learned Deputy Attorney General. Therefore, as the case was filed beyond the period of limitation, the order of the Administrative Tribunal was without jurisdiction, and to that extent the Administrative Appellate Tribunal was correct in setting aside the order of the Administrative Tribunal. Thus, effectively the Administrative Appellate Tribunal has endorsed and upheld the order passed by the appellate authority dated 12.08.1999. We now have to consider how far the decision of the appellate authority, i.e. the Government, is sustainable.

14. We find from section 7 of the Police Officers (Special Provisions) Ordinance, 1976 (the Ordinance) that a police officer on whom a penalty has been imposed may appeal to the appropriate appellate authority within 7 days. Section 7 provides as follows:

"7. A police-officer on whom a penalty has been imposed under section 6 may, within seven days of the receipt of the order of punishment, appeal against the order to the appellate authority concerned specified in column 3 of the schedule, who shall, within forty-five days of the date of receipt of the appeal, communicate to the appellant his decision which shall be final."

15. Thus, according to provision of section 7, the appellate authority shall communicate its decision to the appellant within 45 days. We may also refer to a further provision of the said Ordinance, namely section 7A which provides as follow:

"7A. Notwithstanding anything contained in section 7, the Government may, upon an application made to it by an aggrieved police-officer or on its own motion, within one month from the date of making of a decision by an appellate authority under that section,-

(a) revise such decision, if made by an appellate authority other than the Government;

(b) review such decision, if made by it as an appellate authority."

<u>16. In the facts of the instant case it appears that since the appellate authority, which according to the schedule of the Ordinance in the case of inspector, is the Government, did not communicate its decision within the stipulated 45 days, question of review in accordance with section 7A(b), does not arise.</u>

<u>17. We cannot ignore the fact that the appellate authority decided upon the appellant's appeal after a lapse of 10 months, which is not contemplated under the relevant provisions of the Ordinance. We find that the order passed by the appellate authority was passed beyond the period specified by the Ordinance, and as such is not legally valid and is of no legal effect.</u>

<u>18. According to the provisions of the second proviso to section 4(2) the appellant was bound to file the case before the Administrative Tribunal within eight months of his preferring the appeal before the appellate authority. The decision of the appellate authority having been communicated beyond the period specified under the Ordinance, it cannot be subject of the application before the Administrative Tribunal. The appellant in his application before the Administrative Tribunal did impugn the order of the departmental authority dated 06.10.1998, albeit beyond the statutory period of limitation. The Tribunal erred in considering and allowing the application in respect of the appellate authority's order dated 12.08.1999, as that was an invalid and ineffective order having been passed beyond the period specified by section 7 of the Ordinance.</u>

19. It is not clear from the judgment of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal whether the delay in filing the appeal by the Government was agitated. However, the appellant in his concise statement has adverted to the fact that the decision of the Administrative Tribunal was dated 12.10.2002 and the appeal before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal was filed on 23.4.2003 which is beyond the period of six months stipulated in section 6(2A) of the Act, 1980. In this regard the Administrative Appellate Tribunal observed as follows:

"At the out set of hearing the appeal, the learned Advocate for the respondent submits that the appeal is not maintainable as the original A.T. case was filed beyond the statutory period of limitation as given under section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980."

20. It appears to us that such a submission is a non-sequitur, and it is more likely that the respondent was questioning the period of limitation in filing the appeal before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal.

21. Be that as it may, it appears to us that the appeal before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal was beyond the period of limitation, and was, therefore, barred.

22. In the facts and circumstances discussed above, we may conclude that the judgment of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal requires interference, as being barred by limitation. The application before the Administrative Tribunal was also barred by limitation. The decision of the appellate authority being out of time is not valid in law and is of no legal effect.

<u>23. The order of punishment of reduction in rank of the appellant passed by the departmental authority, therefore, stands. Since the application before the Administrative Tribunal was not within time, the point regarding lack of consultation with the Public Service Commission before passing the impugned order of reduction to a lower rank cannot be agitated at this juncture.</u>

<u>24. In the result the appeal is disposed of. The order of the Administrative Tribunal as well as the judgment and order of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal are set aside. The order passed by the Government, being the appellate authority, is hereby held as not valid in law and is of no legal effect. The order of the concerned departmental authority sentencing the appellant to a lower rank for a period of two years is upheld. The appellant will receive all the service benefits that accrued to him, apart from the period of two years of punishment ordered by the departmental authority.</u>

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sarker, J:- The Rule issued calling upon the opposite party nos. 1-3 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 26.07.2012 passed by the Chairman of Election Appellate Tribunal and Additional District Judge, Netrokona in Election Appellate Tribunal Case No. 09 of 2012 reversing those dated 03.06.2011 passed by the Election Tribunal and the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Netrokona in Election Tribunal Case No. 10 of 2011 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in a nutshell, can be stated thus, the present petitioner being applicant filed an Election Tribunal Case No. 10 of 2011 in the Court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar and Election Tribunal, Netrokona contending inter alia that on 02.07.2011 the Union Parishad Election of No. 03 Thakurakona Union Parishad under Netrokona Sadar Upazila, Netrokona was held. In that election the present petitioner and the opposite party no. 1 along with other member candidates contested for the post of member. The petitioner and the opposite party No.1 are voters of the same village. There is 1(one) center for ward no. 08 consists of 3(three) villages namely Sotorsree, Kagzipara and Latibpur and the election center was established in Sotorsree Government Primary School. In that election the opposite party no. 2 and 3 were the presiding and the pulling officers in the same center of Sotorsree Government Primary School who collusively being influenced and dominated by the opposite party no. 1 conducted the election fraudulently and declared the opposite party no. 1 an elected member in the ward no. 8 against the present petitioner showing 7(seven) votes more. The further case of the present petitioner is such that the presiding officer illegally cast false votes in favour of opposite party no. 1 and the voters who in fact were not present to cast their votes and were engaged in separate election centers showing them present collusively cast their votes illegally and despite the opposite party no. 1 as former member suppressed two material information’s regarding his age and defaulter in paying the electricity bill; he was shown eligible for the post of member and declared elected therein. During vote counting, fraud was practiced by the presiding officer and pulling officers and the engaged agent of the present petitioner although raised objection but that was illegally over ruled. 

3. The contrary case of the opposite party no. 1 in short, is thus that no collusion or suppression or forgery was done during casting of votes and counting of the same and conducting election in the respective center. The presiding officer was totally impartial in the election and he conducted the election fairly and rightly. No allegation or objection was raised from any corner or any agent of the candidates and after counting of the votes while it was found that the opposite party no. 1 obtained 7(seven) votes more than that of the petitioner he was declared rightly an elected member of the concern Union Parishad election. The further case of the opposite party no. 1 is such that nothing was suppressed by him during submission of the nomination paper and there is no illegality in acceptance of his nomination paper by the concern authority. He was not a defaulter regarding payment of electricity bill or his age was not suppressed any where and accordingly he was legally declared member in the election after counting of the votes. 

4. The learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Netrokona and Election Tribunal after taking evidence in the case vide his judgment and order dated 03.06.20011 allowed the Election Case and declared the petitioner a member of ward no. 8, No. 03 Thakurakona Union parishad. Being aggrieved the defendant-appellant-opposite party No.1 preferred an appeal before Election Appellate Tribunal and District Judge, Netrokona being 'Election Appellate Tribunal Case No. 09 of 2012 which was heard and disposed of by the Election Appellate Tribunal and Additional District Judge, Netrokona and the learned appellate tribunal by the impugned judgment and order allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and order passed by the election tribunal and Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Netrokona in Election Case No. 10 of 2011. 

5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order the applicant respondent-petitioner has preferred this revisional application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule. 

6. During hearing of this revisional application Mr. Md. Abu Hanif, the learned advocate appeared on behalf of the petitioner while Mr. Khalequzzaman Masud with Mr. Ahmed Sohel, the learned advocates appeared on behalf of the opposite parties. 

7. The learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the judgment and order of the appellate tribunal is not proper in law as the learned Appellate Tribunal and Additional District Judge failed to apply his judicial mind regarding statement of the plaintiff witnesses and the documents marked as exhibits. The learned appellate Tribunal also failed to consider the corrupt and illegal practice of the opposite parties during election and casting of votes including counting of the same. The learned advocat6 further submits that the election tribunal during disposal of the original election application after proper assessment of evidence and other materials on record allowed the application on contest rightly but subsequently during disposal of the appeal the appellate tribunal having failed to assess the evidence of the witnesses and other materials arrived at an erroneous view that the allegation which is raised from the side of the applicant not proved. Without rebutting the findings of the election tribunal the appellate tribunal reversed the judgment illegally. The learned advocate also submits that under Section 59 of the Election Rules, 2010 the Election Tribunal is empowered to declare anybody elected in thee post applied for and there is no infringement of law from the side of the learned tribunal during passing the judgment and order. There is no ambiguity in the judgment of the election tribunal as the allegation which was raised from the side of the applicant was proved beyond reasonable doubt by sufficient evidence. The difference of 7(seven) votes with that of the opposite party no. 1 was collusive and forged. The learned advocate lastly submits that the witnesses who deposed in support of the applicant proved the allegation which was raised by the applicant in his application. But the learned appellate tribunal without proper sifting of evidence and appreciation of law decided the merit of the appeal against the present petitioner which has resulted an error of law occasioning failure of justice. 

8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party no. 1 opposing the Rule controverted the grounds mentioned from the side of the petitioner and submits that the allegations which were brought by the election application not at-all proved by any cogent credible evidence rather those were disproved on record and the learned appellate tribunal rightly after proper -assessment of evidence and appreciation of law decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the appellant after rebutting the findings of the tribunal reversed the judgment and order passed by the Election Tribunal which is based on surmise and conjecture. The learned advocate for the opposite party further submits that in the original case in fact there is no exhibited paper (document) which deserve consideration of the court and in absence of proof in the trial court no proper was marked exhibit and there is no scope to consider the papers which is not proved under the purview of Evidence Act. There is no document of proof including the voter list showing that the names of the persons which were mentioned by the applicant in his election petition in fact did not cast their vote in the election and inspite of that after counting their votes the presiding officer illegally has shown 7(seven) votes more than that of the applicant in the election which was found after counting of votes in the election. There is no collusion or illegality and practicing fair play in the election the presiding officer at the close of counting of the votes declared the opposite party no. 1 an elected member. In support of the contention the learned advocate has preferred 3(three) decisions of this Court and our Apex Court reported in 37 DLR 169, 39 DLR 140 and 3 MLR (AD) 212. Lastly; the learned advocate submits that there is no written complain or objection from the side of the applicant on the election, rather it was fictitious and rightly the oral allegation was not considered by the concerned authority. The applicant after adducing competent credible evidence was totally failed to prove his case and the appellate tribunal after proper consideration of all the materials on record passed the impugned judgment and order which deserve no interference of this Court. 

9. Heard the learned advocates of both sides, perused the case record, papers on record, deposition of the witnesses and all other connected documents. 
10. On perusal of the case record it transpires that admittedly the election of the concern No. 03 Thakurkona Union Parishad was held on 02.07.2011. The dispute raised on the election of ward no. 08 concerning one post of member. , It was alleged in the election application by the present petitioner that in the said election the applicant obtained 613 votes and the opposite party no. I obtained 620 votes which was collusive and fraudulent. The difference shown between the petitioner and the opposite party no. l is 7(seven) votes for which the opposite party no. 1 was declared elected in the post of member. The allegation set forth is such that a numbers of voters of the concern vote center was engaged in their election duties and they were on duty in separate vote center which is a remote place from the disputed center but inspite of that their votes were counted during counting of the votes which were taken collusively by the presiding officer of the center. In fact the opposite party no. 1 obtained less votes than that of the applicant but practicing fraud and collusion with the presiding officer and pulling officers of the disputed vote center the number of votes were shown higher. To substantiate the aforesaid allegation of the applicant he examined 5(five) witnesses and on the contrary the opposite party no. 1 also adduced 5(five) witnesses in support of his pleading to prove that no collusion or forgery was done and the election of the disputed center was free, fair and credible. 
11. On careful scrutiny over the case record it further transpires that the applicant Md. Rupon Uddin as witness no.1 deposed before the tribunal. In his deposition he states at a stage that the difference between he and the elected candidate is 7(seven) votes but more than 7(seven) votes were taken collusively by practicing fraud and the voters who actually did not take part in casting their votes, their votes were shown to have been cast by the presiding officer of Sotorsree Vote Center which is the disputed center of the case. During cross-examination the applicant Rupon Uddin Akonda admits at a stage that the written objection which was submitted by his agent is not in the record. He further admits that he personally did not file any objection. He expressed his inability to state the name of any voter whose vote was taken collusively after practicing fraud. He further admits that at the time of counting of the votes his agent was present. The witness no. 2 for the applicant is one Sajeda Akhter who is a member of Anser and she states in her averment that on the day of election she was engaged in election duty in a vote center other than the disputed center and one Sufia, Sajeda, Fatema, Halima were on duty with her those who belong to village Sotorsree. This witness further states in her examination-in-chief that her co-villager -Rahim, Mojibor and Jan Miah were also engaged as Ansers on duty and they were on duty for the whole day and as a result of which they did not cast their votes in their center Sotorsree. During cross-examination this witness Sajeda states that, there is no paper showing their alleged duty and she is not in the know about the voters who cast their votes in different centers. She also cannot say whether Rahim and Mojibor cast their votes in Sotorsree center. She admits that she is an unsummoned witness. The witness no. 3 for the applicant is Mintu Miah who is another Anser of the locality and states about his duty in other centers. At a stage of his cross-examination like P.W. 2 this witness also expressed that there is no paper showing that he was engaged on duty other than the disputed center Sotorsree. This witness is also an unsummoned witness. The witness no. 4 for the applicant Jahangir Alam is the agent of the applicant-petitioner. This witness during his .deposition before the tribunal states at a stage that he was present at the time of vote counting and none raised any objection excepting he and there is nothing black and white to prove the same. The last witness for the applicant is Md. Monjurul Hoque. This witness states in his examination-in-chief that he is a voter of Sotorsree center in which after 11.00 a.m. there was a quarrel. One Rafiqul Islam gave false vote and after 11.00 a.m. the election was not fair. During his cross-examination this witness states at a stage that he heard about his above mentioned false vote and did not find to give false vote in the center. He cannot say from whom he has heard about casting or giving of false votes. Vis-a-vis; the opposite party no. 1 as witness no. 1 deposed in support of his case and his other witness O.P.W. 2 is his agent of the disputed center, Md. Abdus Salam Khan O.P.W.. 3 is a voter of the disputed center, Md. Abdul Hamid Khan and other voters of the disputed center are Md. Nurul Amin (O.P.W. 4) and Md. Shahjahan Khan (O.P.W. 5). All these voters who deposed before the tribunal states in support of free, fair and credible election in the disputed center Sotorsree at which they gave their votes. The learned Election Appellate Tribunal in his findings after assessment of evidence on record in it's true perspective rightly opined that the complainant Rupon Uddin Akonda along with his 4(four) other witnesses although deposed to support the pleading of the applicant but none of them appears to be cogent, witness and moreover; from their evidence it is not proved that any collusion or unfair play was done or held in the disputed center which is the ward no. 08, Sotorsree vote center. No evidence is noticed showing as to how and in what manner who practiced the alleged fraud or collusion in the said election and there was any false counting of votes in the center. Further more; there is no ingredient by which the allegation raised can be substantiate. Beside this; the election authority also was convinced that the election was free, fair and credible and accordingly the election result was notified in the Bangladesh Gazette. 
12. Scrutinizing the relevant documents specially exhibit 2 series the voter lists of the concern vote center no where it is noticed that the allegation raised from the side of the applicant against some names of the voters were shown to have cast their votes in the said election and there is nothing on record to justify that the persons who deposed in favour of the applicant were shown present in the center and their votes were cast by the election officials. It is also not supported by any documentary evidence that the person who was declared elected in the said election was not qualified or competent at the relevant time for submitting the nomination paper. There is nothing black and white to substantiate the claim of the applicant that the opposite party no. 1 was a defaulter in payment of Electricity bill, and that he was not competent to submit his nomination paper nor eligible for becoming a candidate in the election. Besides this; it is also not sustainable or can be held that the learned election appellate tribunal during-disposal of the appeal was not lawful or justified in passing the impugned judgment and order and there has been gross illegality or irregularity in deciding the merit of the appeal. Apart from this; on careful scrutiny over the connected documents no where it is marked or found that there has been any misreading or non-reading of evidence or non-consideration of material facts from the side of the election appellate tribunal causing miscourage of justice or resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. Under Section 102 of the Evidence Act the burden of proof lies on the applicant who alleges fraud, which is categorically denied by the opposite party. But in the instant case no such convincing evidence lead to prove any element of fraud and no such document is produced from the side of the applicant in which there exist any material of fraud, collusion or unfair role.' 
13. It is a fact that neither the election tribunal nor the election appellate tribunal recounted the votes of the concern Union Parishad Election of the disputed center but it does not mean that in absence of recounting of votes because of the election of the disputed center has been materially or substantially affected. In the instant case we have come across from the papers on record that the tribunal does not feel any necessity for recounting of the votes and the decision was given purely on the papers submitted in consultation with the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties. In fact there is no substance to draw such inference that there is a need for interference is limited. Only in case of gross illegality or non-consideration of material facts including non-reading or misreading of evidence this court can interfere with the 
judgment and order of the appellate tribunal. But I have already referred to above that no such illegality is noticed or there is no misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts by which it can be held that the appellate tribunal committed any wrong in passing the impugned judgment and order. 

14. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and evidence referred to above I'm constrained to hold such a view that the Rule have got no substance to succeed. 

15. In the result; the Rule is discharged. 

16. The impugned judgment and order dated 26.07.2012 passed by the Chairman of Election Appellate Tribunal and Additional District Judge, Netrokona in Election Appellate Tribunal Case No. 09 of 2012 reversing those dated 03.06.2011 passed by the Election Tribunal and the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Netrokona in Election Tribunal Case No. 10 of 2011 is hereby affirmed. 

17. However, there will be no order as to costs. 

18. Communicate the judgment and order at-once to the court concerned for information and necessary action. 

19. Send back the Lower Court's Record immediately.

End.
