full_judgment:
Mr. Moyeenul Islam Chowdbury, J :-This Rule Nisi issued upon the respondents as to why the impugned public advertisement for only Grade-II and Grade-III Engineers and Ship Surveyors as published in "The Daily Observer" dated 21.03.2005 as in Annexure-C should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect and why a direction should not be made to the respondents to include Marine Engineers with Class-I Competency Certificates in Grade-1 in conformity with provisions of the Recruitment, Examination and Certification Rules, 2001. 

2. The case of the petitioner as set out in the Writ Petition, in short, is as follows:

The petitioner is a citizen of Bangladesh and obtained the Certificate of Competency as Class-I Marine Engineer in 1993 from the United Kingdom. He served as Chief Engineer in a number of ocean-going merchant ships of the Bangladesh Shipping Corporation. From 01.11.1999 to 30.03.2003, he worked for the Lloyds Registry of Shipping, U.K. The Lloyds Registry of Shipping is an internationally recognized supervisory organization of large merchant ships and survey of ships for fitness and sea-worthiness. Currently, the petitioner is at the final stage of his course for MBA from Royal Road's University in British Columbia, Canada. He has all the requisite qualifications for appointment as Engineer and Ship Surveyor (Grade-I).

However, Bangladesh is a party to the International Convention on Standards of Training, Certification and Watch-Keeping for Seafarers (STCW), 1978. The STCW Convention is administered by the International Marine Organization (IMO). From time to time, the IMO examines and reviews the organizational set-up and professional competence of Member States. Anyway, as per the Inland Steam Vessels Act, 1917 and the Merchant Shipping Act, 1923, there were provisions for examinations and issuing Competency Certificates to Marine Engineers, Ship Mates and Ship Drivers. Those provisions were complied and circulated by the then Government of Bengal under the captain- "Bengal Marine Manual, 1928". According to the said Bengal Marine Manual, the Director General of the Department of Shipping is authorized to hold examinations and issue Certificates of Competency to Ship Surveyors, Engineers and Engine Drivers in conformity with the requirements of the IMO and the STCW Convention, 1978. 

The Government of Bangladesh promulgated the Inland Shipping Ordinance, 1976 to implement, inter alia, the provisions of the Inland Steam Vessels Act, 1917 and the Merchant Shipping Act, 1923 and the International Conventions. In view of Section 82 of the Inland Shipping Ordinance, 1976, the Government framed the Recruitment, Examination and Certification Rules, 2001. In Rule 7, there is a provision for Examination Board and in Rule 7(4), it is provided that the Chief Examiner must be a Marine Engineer with Class-I Competency Certificate who shall also be the Chairman of the Board of Examiners to hold examinations and issue Competency Certificates to Drivers and Engineers who are meant for work in the Inland and International Shipping Lines. Over 8,000 Bangladeshi Seaman/Seafarers certified by the Board of Examiners are working in foreign shipping lines. Every year a large number of Bangladeshi take the said examination for service both inside and outside the country. Bangladesh being a land-locked country on three sides, opening to the sea and utilization of the opportunity of access to the sea are a vital strategic importance thereto. 

By the SRO No.39-Law/86 dated 23° January, 1986 as published in the Bangladesh Gazette on January 25, 1986, the Department of Shipping (Engineer and Ship Surveyor of Inland Ships) Recruitment Rules, 1980 were amendment providing for three Grades of Engineer and Ship Surveyor. For appointment as Grade-I Engineer and Ship Surveyor, Marine Engineer with Class-1 Certificate of Competency and minimum 5 years of actual post-certificate experience; as Grade-II Engineer and Ship Surveyor, Marine Engineer with Class-II Certificate of Competency with 5 years of post-certificate actual experience or Degree in Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering from a University recognized by the Government with minimum 5 years of post-degree certificate experience and as Grade-III Engineer and Ship Surveyor, Degree in Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering from a University recognized by the Government with minimum 3 years of post-degree experience are required. However, two posts of Engineer and Ship Surveyor in Grade-I fell vacant. The Director General of Shipping by his letters dated 25.05.04 and 25.08.04 requested the Ministry of Shipping to take steps to recruit two Marine Engineers with Class-I Competency Certificates to fill in the vacancies. But because of the impact of the Pressure Groups of the Department of Naval Architecture of the BUET and the graduates of the BUET in Naval Engineering the Government asked the Bangladesh Public Service Commission to recruit two Engineers and Ship Surveyors in Grade-II and Grade-III only. This was deliberately done to eliminate the scope for recruitment of any Marine Engineer with Class-I Competency Certificate. The petitioner holding the degree of Marine Engineer with Class-1 Competency Certificate from the United Kingdom and having long experience in the line would not feel inclined to apply for and be considered for appointment as a Grade-II or Grade-III Engineer and Ship Surveyor. He is personally aggrieved by the public advertisement dated 12.03.2005 issued by the Public Service Commission. But more importantly, the greater public interest would be served in having Marine Engineers with Class-I Competency Certificates in Grade-I. They would be competent to hold examinations and issue certificates to Seamen and Drivers who would be acceptable under the International Conventions. Secondly, Bangladesh ships would need fitness certificates in order to play in international waters and be eligible for Marine Insurance from reputed International Marine Insurance Companies. Thus there is a vital public interest that the posts which fell vacant due to retirement of Marine Engineers with Class-I Engineers and Shi Surveyors with Class-I Competency Certificates as mandated by the Department of Shipping (Engineer and Ship Surveyor of Inland Ships) Recruitment Rules, 1980 as amended by the SRO No.39-Law/86 dated 23' January, 1986. Under the circumstances, the petitioner has made this Writ Petition as a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in order to protect the national interest as against the narrow private interests of a few individuals. 

3. The Bangladesh Public Service Commission's public advertisement No. BPSC/Unit- 1/Misc.-2/2004/8-9 dated 12.02.2005 was published in the Daily Observer on 21.03.2005. The petitioner bonafide believes that this advertisement for appointment of only Grade-II and Grade-III Engineers and Ship Surveyors was made malafide so as to prevent the Marine Engineers with Class-I Competency Certificates from applying and thereby harm the national interest. The impugned advertisement by the Public Service Commission was made in colourable exercise of power. Hence the Rule. 

4. The Rule has been opposed on behalf of the respondent Nos.1 and 5 by filing two separate Affidavit-in-Opposition. 

5. The case of the respondent No.1 as set out - in the Affidavit-in-Opposition, in short, runs as under 

The petitioner is neither an officer nor a member of the staff of the Department of Shipping, So he is not affected in any way by the notification dated 12.03.2005 made by the Public. Service Commission. The respondent No.4 (Director General of the Department of Shipping) is legally authorized to ensure the safety of river passengers and transportation of goods on behalf of the Government. The Inland Shipping Ordinance, 1976 is administered by the respondent No.4. He appoints the Examiners of the Board of Examiners as per law. The Chairman of the Board must be a Marine Engineer, Grade-II and Grade-III Engineers and Ship Surveyors will not conduct any examination. They are to survey Inland Ships according to their job descriptions. At the instance of the respondent No.4, the Public Service Commission legally made the impugned advertisement for recruitment of. Grade-11 and Grade-III Engineers and Ship Surveyors according to the qualifications prescribed by the relevant rules. The petitioner is personally interested in the matter, but by way of smart trick, he has filed the Writ Petition in the name of Public Interest Litigation. That being so, the Writ Petition is not maintainable. Hence the Rule is liable to be discharged with costs. 

6. The case of the respondent No.5 as stated in his Affidavit-in-Opposition, in brief, is as follows: 

The Writ Petition is not maintainable inasmuch as the petitioner has filed the same not for any public interest, but for the selfish ends of the Marine Engineers holding Competency Certificates. He has filed the Writ Petition in the grab of a Public Interest Litigation to espouse the case of a coterie. Nowhere in the Writ Petition he has stated that he has approached the Court on behalf of any poor or disadvantaged or vulnerable segment of the population. It has been preferred with a malafide intention to resist appointment of any Naval Architects-cum-Marine Engineers to the posts of Engineers and Ship Surveyors. The posts of Engineers and Ship Surveyors are filled in by recruitment of either Marine Engineers or Naval Architects-cum-Marine Engineers. Needless to say, the Writ Petition has been filed not for vindication of any public interest, but for furthering to coterie interest of Marine Engineers only. So the petitioner is not entitled to any relief under Article 102 of the Constitution.

The Government of Bangladesh did not promulgate the Inland Shipping Ordinance, 1976 to implement, inter alia, the provisions of the Inland Steam Vessels Act, 1917 and the Merchant Shipping Act, 1923 and the International Conventions. The provisions of Section 38 of the Inland Shipping Ordinance, 1976 have no manner of application so far as the posts of Engineers and Ship Surveyors are concerned. Section 38 of the Ordinance deals with the appointment of the Examiners or the Board of Examiners for issuance of Certificates of Competency, The Examiners or the Board of Examiners so appointed will be entitled to remunerations prescribed by the Government while Engineers and Ship Surveyors are appointed under the Department of Shipping (Engineer and Ship Surveyor of Inland Ships) Recruitment Rules, 1980 with the pay-scales specified in the said Rules. 

It is not correct to say that due to the impact of the Present Group constituted by the Department of Naval Architecture of the BEET and the graduates of the BUET in Naval Engineering, the Government asked the Bangladesh Public Service Commission to recruit two Engineers and Ship Surveyors in Grade-II and III only. It may be mentioned that the post of Grade-II Engineers and Ship Surveyor is still open to the Marine Engineers with Class-I and Class-II Competency Certificates. Be that as it may, there are 4 posts of Engineer and Ship Surveyor in the Department of Shipping. Two Engineers and Ship Surveyors have already retired from Grade-I. There is one Engineer and Ship Surveyor working in Grade-I and II. The post of Graded is required to be filled in by way of promoting the Engineer and Ship Surveyor working in Grade-II and the process of promotion is underway at the moment. For this reason, there is no scope to make direct recruitment to the post of Grade-I according to the amended Recruitment Rules of 1980. 

In any case, the posts of Engineers and Ship Surveyors of all the 3 Grades are relative to Inland Ships. As such, the statement made in the Writ Petition that the Bangladeshi Ships would need certificates of fitness and sea-worthiness in order to ply in international waters and be eligible for Marine Insurance reputed International Marine Insurance Companies is relevant at all. The writ petition has not bee field by way of any public interest litigation. The petitioner is personally interested in his appointment as engineer and ship surveyor in Grade-I as per the amended Recruitment Rule of 1980. He is an interloper. So the Rule is liable to be discharged with costs. 

7. At the outset, Mr. Abdur Rab Chaudhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that to all interest and purposes, it is a Public Interest Litigation, though the petitioner is personally interest in his Appointment as Grade-I Engineers and Ship Surveyors. as per the Department of Shipping (Engineer and Ship Surveyor of Inland Ships) Recruitment Rules, 1980 as amended up-to-date and he has ventilated the grievances of all Marine Engineers with Class-I Competency Certificates and if Engineers and Ship Surveyors are appointed in Grades-II and III as advertised by the Public Service Commission, then our national interest will be jeopardized and this is why, his standing before the High Court Division cannot be questioned. 

Mr. Abdur Rab Chaudhury next submits that under the provisions of the Inland Shipping Ordinance, 1976 and the Rules framed under the SRO No.298/Law dated 30th October, 2001, the appointment of a Marine Engineer with Class-I Competency Certificate is required to conduct examinations and issue certificates to Engineers and Drivers for both Inland and International Shipping and by the impugned advertisement, no steps have been taken for recruitment of qualified Marine Engineers with Class-I Competency Certificates to the detriment of the national interest and as such, the impugned advertisement is without lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

Mr. Abdur Rab Chaudhury further submits that Bangladesh being a Member of IMO and the STCW Convention, it is imperative to comply with the internationally accepted qualifications in the matter of recruitment of Engineers and Ship Surveyors, failing which, the holding of examinations and the issuance of Competency Certificates to Seaman and Ship Drivers would not be acceptable to the IMO and the STCW Convention countries to the great prejudice of our national interest. 

8. On the other hand, Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.5, submits that the petitioner has not come up with the Writ Petition pro bono publico; rather he has filed it with oblique motives in order to serve the insular and. partisan interest of a cotorie of Marine Engineers and against this backdrop, he cannot claim any standing before the High Court Division. 

Mr. Mahmudul Islam next submits that the Department of Shipping (Engineer and Ship Surveyor of Inland Ships) Recruitment Rules, 1980 as amended by the SRO No.39- Law/86 dated 23' January, 1986 unmistakably deals with the recruitment of Engineers and Ship Surveyors in Grade-I, II and III for Inland Ships only and in that view of the matter, the IMO and the STCW Convention have nothing to do with Inland Shipping and in such posture of things, Mr. Abdur Rab Chaudhury has no legs to stand upon. 

Mr. Mahmudul Islam also submits that since the Department of Shipping (Engineer and Ship Surveyor of Inland. Ships) Recruitment Rules, 1980 as amended provide for the recruitment of Engineers and Ship Surveyors in all the 3 Grades in Inland Ships, the contention of Mr. Abdur Rab Chaudhury that the Inland Shipping Ordinance, 1976 and the Rules framed thereunder govern their recruitment is devoid of any substance. 

Mr. Mahmudul Islam further submits that Mr. Abdur Rab Chaudhury has committed a mistake by making an averment in the Writ Petition that the Engineers and Ship Surveyors of all the 3 Grades as contemplated by the amended Recruitment Rules of 1980 are mandated to issue certificates of fitness and seaworthiness of vessels and since the above-mentioned Rules of 1980 are meant for recruitment of Engineers and Ship Surveyors of Inland Ships, the holding of examinations and issuance of Competency Certificates to Seamen and Ship Drivers would not be acceptable to the IMO and the STCW Convention countries without having any Internationally accepted qualifications do not arise at all. 

9. Mr. Md. lqbal Hossain, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing onbehalf of the respondent'No.1, has adopted the submissions made by Mr. Mahmudul Islam. 

10. We have heard the submissions of Mr. Abdur Rab Chaudhury and the counter-submissions of Mr. Mahmudul Islam and perused the Writ Petition and the Affidavits-in-Opposition and the relevant Annexures annexed thereto. 

11. To being with, we are to resolve a very pertinent question as to whether the Writ Petition is a Public Interest Litigation or a Private Interest Litigation. 

In Black's Law Dictionary (Sixth Edition), 'public interest' is defined as follows: 

"Public Interest- Something in which the public, the community at large, has some pecuniary interest, or some interest by which their legal rights or liabilities are affected. It does not mean anything so narrow as mere curiosity, or as the interests of the particular localities, which may be affected by the matters in question. Interest shared by citizens generally in affairs of local, State or national Government…………..”  

In this connection, a reference may be made to the decision in the case of Janata -Dal. Vs. H.S. Chowdhury and others reported in AIR 1993 (SC) 892. In that decision, the Indian Supreme Court held: 

"Lexically the expression PIL means a legal action initiated in a Court of law for enforcement of public interest or general interest or in which the public or a class of the community have pecuniary interest or some interest by which their legal rights or liabilities are affected .... Thus, the concept of PIL which has been and is being fostered by judicial activism has become an increasingly important one setting up valuable and respectable records specially in the arena of 1 constitutional and under-represented." 

With regard to the question of injury to Public Interest or what is termed as "public injury" as distinguished from "private injury", Bhagwati, J. of the Indian Supreme Court observed in the case of S.P. Gupta Vs. Union of India reported in AIR 1982 (SC)149: 

"The view has therefore been taken by the Courts in many decisions that whenever there is a public wrong or public injury caused by an act or omission of the State or a public authority which is contrary to the Constitution or the law, any member of the public acting bonafide and having sufficient interest can maintain an action for redressal of such public wrong or public injury."

 In the self-same case, Justice Bhagwati also observed: 

"It is a fascinating exercise in the Court to deal with Public Interest Litigation, because it is a new jurisprudence which the Court is evolving, a jurisdiction which demands judicial statesmanship and high creative ability. The frontiers of public law are expanding far and wide and new concepts and doctrines which will change the complexion of the law and which were so far embedded in the womb of the future, are beginning to be born." 

12. PIL needs a self-imposed judicial restriction, especially when the grievance exposed does not adversely affect the large number of citizens who on account of innumerable reasons, like poverty, etc., cannot approach the Court to ventilate their cases. Before the public interest jurisdiction is invoked, the Court is ordinarily expected to be satisfied that there is some element of public interest, that the transaction impugned involves malafides, and that there is a need for balancing the consequences of the public good with the act of the State. PIL should not ordinarily be permitted as an adventurous freak in the Court. This view finds support from the decision in the case of A.P. Dalit Maha Sabha Vs. Govt. of Andra Prodesh reported in AIR 1999 (AP) 452. 

In the case of Ashok Kumar Pandey Vs. The State of West Bengal reported in AIR 2004 (SC) 280, the Indian Apex Court held 

"Public Interest Litigation which has now come to occupy an important field in the administration of law should not be 'Publicity Interest Litigation' or 'Private Interest Litigation' or 'Politics Interest Litigation' or the latest trend 'Paise Income Litigation'. If not properly regulated and abuse averted, it also becomes a stool in unscrupulous hands to release vendetta and wreak vengeance as well. There must be real and genuine public interest involved in the litigation and not merely an adventure of a knight errant or poke one's nose into for a probe. It cannot also be invoked by a person or a body of persons to further his or their personal causes or satisfy his or their personal grudge and enmity. Courts of Justice should not be allowed to be polluted by unscrupulous litigants by resorting to the extraordinary jurisdiction. A person acting bonafide and having sufficient interest in the proceeding of a Public Interest Litigation will alone have a locus standi and can approach the Court to wipe out violation of fundamental rights and genuine infraction of statutory provisions, but not for personal gain or private profit of political motive or any oblique consideration ... Public Interest Litigation is a weapon which has to be used with great care and circumspection and the Judiciary has to be extremely careful to see that behind the beautiful veil of public interest, an ugly private malice, vested interest and/or publicity-seeking are not lurking. It is to be used as an effective weapon in the armory of law for delivering social justice to the citizens... The Court has to be satisfied about (a) the credentials of the applicant; (b) the prima facie correctness or nature of information given by him; and (c) the information being not vague and indefinite. The information should show gravity and seriousness involved." 

The Indian Supreme Court sounded a red alert and a note of severe warning that the Court should not allow its process to be abused at the instance of a mere busybody or a meddlesome interloper or wayfarer or officious intervener. It goes without saying that only a person acting bonafide and having sufficient interest in the proceeding of a PIL will alone have a locus standi and can approach the Court on behalf of the indeterminate number of people. 

In our jurisdiction, the decision in the case of Dr. Mohiuddin Farooque Vs. Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Irrigation, Water Resources and Flood Control and others reported in 49 DLR (AD) l may be adverted to. In that decision, our Appellate Division observed in paragraphs 46 and 50 

"46. Article 102 therefore is an instrumentality and a mechanism, containing both substantive and procedural provisions, by means of which the people as a collective personality, and not merely as a conglomerate of individuals, have devised for themselves a method and manner to realize the objectives, purposes, policies, rights and duties which they have set out for themselves and which they have strewn over the fabric of the Constitution. 
…………………………
………………………

50. The High Court Division will exercise some rules of caution in each case. It will see that the applicant is in fact, espousing a public cause, that his interest in the subject-matter is real and not in the interest of generating some publicity for himself or to create mere public sensation, that he is acting bonafide, that he is not a busybody or an interloper, that it is in the public interest to grant him standing and that he is not acting for a collateral purpose to achieve a dubious goal, including serving a foreign interest," 

So it leaves no room for doubt that the petitioner in a PIL should not be a busybody or an interloper, and he should espouse a public cause for the benefit of the vulnerable or disadvantaged segment of the population. Over and above, he must act bonafide and in the greater public interest and he should not seek his own interest or the interest of a coterie for a collateral purpose. 

13. In the present Writ Petition, the petitioner claims himself to be duly qualified for appointment as Engineer and Ship Surveyor in Grade-I as envisaged by the amended Recruitment Rules of 1980. In other words, he has espoused his personal cause along with that of Marine Engineers with Class-1 Competency Certificates only. For all practical purposes, he has asserted the cause of a coterie so as to serve its own parochial interest. Mr. Abdur Rab Chaudhury has failed to pinpoint any illegality or legal flaw in the impugned public advertisement made by the Public Service Commissioner vis-à-vis the Schedule of the Recruitment Rules of 1980 as substituted by the SRO No.39-Law/86 dated 23rd January, 1986. According to the submission of Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the impugned advertisement was made in absolute compliance with the substituted Schedule of the Recruitment Rules of 1980. To put it differently, according to Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the mandate of law was meticulously followed in the impugned advertisement and in this perspective, it cannot be found fault with by any quarter.

14. It transpires that the impugned order advertisement was made by the Public Service Commission in accordance with the substituted Schedule of the Recruitment Rules of 1980. It also appears that those Rules of 1980 hold the field in the matter of recruitment of Engineers and Ship Surveyors of Inland Ships. Since no illegality or legal flaw can be pointed out by Mr. Abdur Rab Chaudhury in the impugned advertisement, we are at one with Mr. Mahmudul Islam that the impugned advertisement was made by the Public Service Commission in complete compliance with the amended Recruitment Rules of 1980. 

15. We have already observed that the petitioner has espoused his personal cause as well as the cause of the coterie of Marine Engineers only. It is an indisputable fact that he dose not represent a vast multitude of down-trodden or oppressed or vulnerable or disadvantaged people. From a plain reading of the Writ Petition, it leads us to hold that in the grab of a PIL, he has come up therewith for his personal and group benefit. That being the position, we have no hesitation in holding that the Writ Petition is not a PIL. As a matter of fact, it does not fulfill any of the criteria as mentioned above. Further, wee have already held that the Inland Shipping Ordinance, 1976 and the Rules framed thereunder do not operate in the matter of recruitment of Engineers and Ship Surveyors of Inland Ships. The certificates of fitness and sea-worthiness from various International entities like the STCW Convention and the IMO can be obtained for ocean-gong vessels only. So the question of comparison between the competency of Engineers and Ship Surveyors of Bangladesh and that of Engineers and Ship Surveyors of other countries of the world is out of the question. In our view, the Government is the best judge as to the recruitment of Engineers and Ship Surveyors of Inland Ships either in Grade-I or in Grade-II or in Grade-III and the requirement of recruitment in Grade-II and Grade-III in the impugned advertisement was accordingly made. 

16. In this context, it may be pointed out that as per the Recruitment Rules of 1980 as amended on 23rd January, 1986, the appointment of a person as Engineers and Ship Surveyors in Grade-I must be made firstly by promotion who have at least five years' service in Grade-II and in default of a suitable candidate, then by direct recruitment. It has been clearly, categorically and unambiguously stated in the Affidavit-in-Opposition filed on behalf of the respondent No.5 that the appointment of an Engineer and Ship Surveyor in Grade-I by way of promotion is under process. This being the scenario, no exception can be taken to the impugned advertisement to recruitment of Engineers and Ship Surveyors of Inland Ships in Grades-II and III.

It is the admitted position that the petitioner has not challenged the vires or constitutionality of the Recruitment Rules of 1980 as amended up-to-date. By the way, it may be noted that the substituted Schedule of the said Recruitment Rules of 1980 by the SRO No.39-Law/86 dated 23rd January, 1986 was challenged in Writ Petition No.2597 of 2001 and the High Court Division on hearing discharged the Rule. As against the judgment and order passed in Writ Petition No.2597 of 2001, Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1910 of 2002 was taken, but in vain. This being the state of affairs, we hold that the petitioner of the instant Writ Petition has no case at all. Of course, Mr. Abdur Rab Chaudhury has candidly conceded that if the Court finds that it is not a PIL, then he has no case whatsoever. 

17. From the foregoing discussions and in the facts and circumstances of the case, we find no merit in the Rule. The Rule, therefore, fails. 

18. Accordingly, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Soumendra Sacker, J.:- The Rule have been issued calling upon the Opposite Party No.1 to show cause as to why the judgment and order No.01 dated 08.03.2012 passed by the learned District Judge, Chittagong in Civil Revision No.44 of 2012 summarily rejecting the same and affirming the judgment and order dated 31.10.2011 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 1 Court, Sadar, Chittagong in Election Tribunal Case No.21 of 2011 shall not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders be passed as to. this court may seem fit and proper. 

2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in a nutshell, can be stated thus, the Petitioner was a candidate for the post of Chairman, No.01 Juldha Union Parishad, Upazilla-Patia, District, Chittagong. The election of the said Union Parishad for the post of Chairman was held on 28.06.2011 and the petitioner was elected as Chairman of the said Union Parishad. The concern Gazette Notification was published on 28.09.2011 and the petitioner took oath in the post of Chairman of the said Union Parishad. The present opposite party No.1 subsequently on 27.10.2011 being plaintiff filed an Election Tribunal Case being No.21 of 2011 bringing an allegation that the election was not fair and proper. Subsequent to the filing of the Election Tribunal Case the opposite party No.1 filed an application for amendment of the Election Petition on 31.10.2011 and the learned Tribunal after hearing allowed the application, Thereafter the plaintiff-opposite party No.1 filed an application on 14.02.20(2 to accept the Ballot paper and other election related documents and accordingly the learned Tribunal allowed the same. The present petitioner challenging the said order of the learned Election Tribunal preferred Civil Revision being No.44 of 2012 in the Court of learned District Judge, Chittagong and the learned District Judge, Chittagong after hearing the petition rejected the Civil Revisional Application summarily by the impugned judgment and order dated 08.03.2012. 

3. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and order of the learned District Judge, Chittagong the petitioner instituted the present Civil Revision under Section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the Rule with an interim order of Stay. 

4. Mr. Md. Mizanur Rahman, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the Petitioner while none appeared on behalf of the, opposite party despite the matter is posted in the daily cause list of this court for days together with the names of the learned Advocates and the matter was transferred to this Bench by the Hon'ble Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1027 of 2012 on le July, 2012 and there was a direction upon this Bench to dispose of the Rule within 4(four) weeks from the date of receipt of this order. 

5. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned Election Tribunal as well as the learned Revisional Court i.e. the learned a District Judge, Chittagong committed gross illegality in disposing the amendment application and the subsequent Civil Revision being No.44 of 2012. The learned Advocate further submits that the Election Tribunal passed the order allowing the amendment application and called for all the votes, books and other related documents from the defendant Nos.2 and 3, which is not proper and legal and as such committed an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The present petitioner being aggrieved challenging the order of the learned Election Tribunal preferred the Revisional Application before the learned District Judge, Chittagong but the learned District Judge without proper appreciation of law and realizing the subject matter of the original election dispute rejected the petitioner's Revisional Application summarily and thus committed error in law in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

6. Heard the learned advocate for the petitioner, perused the revisional application preferred under Section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure including all other connected papers along with the impugned order of the learned District Judge, Chittagong. 

7. On perusal of the connected papers it transpires that the plaintiff-opposite party filed the election complaint petition before the learned Election Tribunal, Chittagong region, Chittagong on 27.10.2011. In the said election dispute application it was the specific case of the plaintiff therein that the disputed vote center is No.7, Paschim Juldha Government Primary School and he prayed for declaration before the Tribunal that the election held in the aforesaid center is illegal, forged, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiff. He also prayed for re-election in the said vote center. Within the Schedule of the plaint it was clearly stated that the disputed vote center is No.7, Paschim Juklha Government Primary School. In Schedtile no. 1(kha) of the plaint the said vote center was specified. After filing of the election complaint application the plaintiff filed an application for amendment on 31.10.2011 under Order 6 Rule 17 along with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the election complaint. In the said application the plaintiff stated that inadvertently in his Plaint there has been omission and in his proposed amendment he raised allegation like the previous allegation upon the vote center Nos.1-6, 8 and 9. For the aforesaid 8(eight) vote centers all the materials relating to election were called for and sought for re-counting of the votes. 

8. On careful scrutiny over the order of the learned Election Tribunal it appears that the Tribunal vide his order No.02 dated 31.10.2011 allowed the application for amendment as sought for in toto. It is obvious to note that the present petitioner who was the opposite party of the election complaint petition being aggrieved by the order of the Election Tribunal preferred a Civil Revision challenging the propriety and legality of the order passed by the learned Election Tribunal before the learned District Judge, Chittagong. The learned District Judge, Chittagong by the impugned judgment and order dated 08.03.2012 rejected the Civil Revision summarily on the plea that under the purview of Section 61 Sub-section (3) of the Union Parishad Nirhachon Parichalona Manual the aggrieved party may file an appeal against the order before the Election Tribunal within 30 (thirty) days from the order and decision of the Election Tribunal and as because the Election Tribunal case is governed by the special law under the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ordinance, 1983 there is no scope to entertain the revisional application, 

9. In this context; on going through the Local Government (Union Parishad) Election Rules, 2010 it is evident that Section 61 Sub-section (3) contemplates the final decision as well as the order of the Tribunal and it relates the decision of the Election Tribunal which is passed after taking evidence from the respective parties on conclusion of pre-emptory hearing. Apparently the learned District Judge, Chittagong was misconceived and failed to appreciate the actual position of law. 

10. It is a fact that it is a special law and the Election Tribunal is not a Civil Court constituted under the Civil Courts Act, 1887. Powers which an Election Tribunal exercises as a Civil Court under the Civil Procedure Code while trying an election case does not empower such Tribunal to give retrospective effect to an amendment when such amendment has the effect as if a fresh election petition has been filed on the date of amendment

In this context; the learned counsel for the petitioner referred a decision of a Division Bench of this Court reported in 38 DLR 435 in the case of Hosne Zaman Sarker Vs. Election Tribunal and others wherein it was held that, it is well settled that although rule 48 of the Union Parishad Rules 1983 provides that the Tribunal shall have all the powers of a Civil Court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 and shall be deemed to be a Civil Court within the meaning of Sections 480 and 482 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1898. It is not a Civil Court constituted under the Civil Courts Act, 1887. The power of an Election Tribunal deciding an election petition under Section 27 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ordinance, 1983 it that of a statutory tribunal with limited jurisdiction The provision of Rule 47 of the Union Parishad Rules that the Code of Civil Procedure shall, as nearly as possible, be followed in trying election cases, does not mean that the Tribunal has the power of making an amendment of the election petition so as to made it relate back to the date of filing of the said petition. In other words, even though Tribunal is not a civil court exercising all the powers under the Code of Civil Procedure, it may still exercise the powers of amendment of pleadings, but it has no authority to give the amendment a retrospective effect from the date of filing of the election petition. 

11. On careful scrutiny over the related papers along with the order of the learned Election Tribunal it is apparent from the face of the papers that the amendment as sought for by the plaintiff-opposite party has been given a retrospective effect from the date of filing of the election petition and as such I am constrained to hold such a view that the said amendment has no doubt the effect of filing a fresh election petition. Such amendment cannot be entertained but the learned Election Tribunal illegally allowed the application for amendment which is not sustainable in law. 

12. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and discussions referred to above I have the every reason to inclined such a view that the Rule have got much substance to succeed. 

13. In the result; the Rule is made absolute. 

14. The impugned judgment and order passed by the learned District Judge, Chittagong in Civil Revision No.44 of 2012 affirming the order dated 31.10.2011 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, 1a Court, Sadar, Chittagong and Election Tribunal in Election Tribunal Case No.21 of 2011 allowing the application for amendment of the election petition is hereby set-aside. 

15. The stay order granted earlier by this Court at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated. 

16. However, there will be no order as to cost. 

17. Communicate the judgment & order at-once to the court concerned for information and necessary action. 

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Akram Hossain Chowdhury, J:-On an application under Article 102 of the 
Constitution. this Rule nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned notice dated 23.04.2012 issued under Section 3 or the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 (to he called Ordinance, 1982) arising out of L.A. Case 
No. 07/2011-12 proposing to acquire the land owned by the petitioners shall not he declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 


2. The facts leading to this rule, as averred in the writ petition are that the petitioner 
No.1, Rahima Khatun and one Harun-or-Rashid who became the owner and possessor of the land measuring 30 decimals appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.90. corresponding to S.A. Khatian No. 154 and B.S. Khatian No. Ill, previous Dag No. 152 and at present Dag No. 450 under J.L. No. 46, Mouza-Dotola Gobindopur, P.S. Chandina, District-Comilla, by way of purchase vide sale deed No. 9907 dated 21.10.1975 executed by one Bidhu Bhushan Acharya. Then they filed application before the Revenue Officer for mutating their name in respect of the aforementioned land but at the point of time it reveals that the aforesaid land was wrongly inserted in the list of vested property. Eventually, on their prayer the V.P. Case No. 38 of 1997 and 77 of 1998 were started and heard together on 05.07.1999 and after hearing of the said V.P. cases the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue). Comilla was pleased to pass an order releasing the land from the list of vested property (Annexure-D to the writ petition). Thereafter the aforesaid Harun-or-Rashid sold out his portion of land to the petitioner No.2, Qari Md. Asmat Ali, vide sale deed No. 7200 dated 08.09.2002. By this way the petitioner Nos.1 and 2 became the owners of the aforesaid land by way of purchase and thereby they were possessing the same without interruption from any quarter. Then the petitioners for their better enjoyment executed an agreement between them for amicable partition in respect of the land in question and thereby they are peacefully possessing the same by erecting their sami pacca houses thereon and are Irving there with their family members from long before. 

3. However, all on a sudden the petitioners have been received the impugned notice dated 23.04.2012 (Annexure-A) showing their homestead land has been proposed to be acquired for the purpose of extension of an Agro based industry namely "Chandina Farmland and Cold Storage Limited". Having learnt about that notice (Annexure-A) the petitioners collected the Memorandum and Articles of Association of the above named company; from which it revealed that the said company is a private limited company registered under the Companies Act, 1994. Then the petitioners jointly filed an application before the respondent No. 4 on 07.05.2012 (Annexure-0) with a prayer not to acquire the land in question on the ground that the land is homestead and the petitioners are living thereon and they have no other land to live. It was further stated that if the land is acquired for the purpose of enlargement of a private limited company the petitioners will be suffered from irreparable loss and injury and they will be thrown out from their homestead. 

4. Upon received the said application the respondent No.4, the land acquisition Officer issued a letter dated 13.05.2012 (Annexure H) directing the petitioners to appear before the respondent No. 1 i.e. the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla with the necessary papers and documents to redress their grievances, Accordingly the petitioners attended the said office of the respondent No.1 and agitated the same grievances as raised in their objection (Annexure-G). But unfortunately the respondent No.1 in a most arbitrary and unlawful manner informed the petitioners that there is no other alternative but to acquire the land in question as the local administration is under tremendous pressure from the local member of Parliament, In the said compelling circumstances the petitioners were constrained to file this writ petition challenging the impugned notice dated 23.04.2012 (Annexure-A) and thereby obtained the present rule. 

5. The respondent No.1 & 3 by filing an affidavit-in-opposition controverted the material allegations made in the writ petition and contended inter-alia that the land as proposed to be acquired has been taken under consideration for acquisition for the purpose of establishment of an Agro based industries for the benefit of general people of the locality and that was done for the public interest also; as there will be an opportunity of employment of thousands of workers and staffs who will be involved in the food processing works for exporting the same in abroad. It further asserted by the respondents that the Managing Director of the Chandina Farmland and Cold Storage Company Limited forwarded a letter of requisition to the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla vide their memo No. Cha.Fa.0.189/12 dated 25.03.2012 in order to acquisition of 0.30 acres of land of B.S. Plot No. 450, situated under Mouza- Dotola Gobindapur to use the same for the purpose of different infrastructures in response to the need of the extension work of the said Chandina Farmland and Cold Storage which have been engaged in service of the food - processing works and exporting the same regularly to the abroad. Al the same lime there is a Master Plan awaiting to be executed to the aim and view of extension of the said industries in order to storage food grain of the locality and also to undertake production of export oriented goods in large scale in the long run. 
6. In response to the said proposal of the Chandina Farmland and Cold Storage Limited the District Land Acquisition and Allocation Committee have taken a decision in a meeting held on 08.04.2012 and after threadbare discussions the committee found there is no legal impediment to acquire the proposed 0.30 acres of land from plot No. 450 and accordingly the acquiring authority initiated the L.A. Case No. 7/2011-12 arcl thereby notice under Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982 was served upon the petitioners and other concerned parties of the locality. The notices were also duly served upon the original owners of the land, namely Parimal Chandra Acharia. Gupal Chandra Acharia. Srinath Bhowmic and others on 24.04.2012. Thereafter in presence of the members of the requiring organization, officials of the government authority and also the petitioners and upon holding spot inquiry the list of structures trees and plants standing thereon were made on account and thereby the valuation of the land, structures and trees were assessed, properly. Then the notice recipients namely (I) Nilofa Begum and (2) Rahima Khatoon subMitted their objections under Section 4(1) of the Ordinance and accordingly the said objections were heard and disposed of observing that since the project is mainly engaged in producing exportable food items and exports the same in abroad regularly and now the agro based organization in need to be extended in order to undertake production of its large scale exportable items and upon consideration of the said public and national interest the authority concerned rejected the objections raised by the aforesaid two objectors. Thereafter the proposal of acquisition was forwarded to the Divisional Commissioner for his consideration under Section 5(I) of the Ordinance. 1982 and accordingly the Divisional Commissioner sent back the proposal to the local authority with his comments vide memo No. 665 dated 27.06.2012 and the process of acquisition is still in continuation; and thus, the attempt of the petitioners' seeking relief under Article 102 of the Constitution in challenging the notice issued tinder Section 43 of the Ordinance is barred by Section 44 of the Ordinance 1982. 

7. When the matter appeared in the list for hearing for a couple of days, one of the day, on 30.04.2015 Mr. Mukunda Chandra Debnath, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the respondents issued the impugned notice dated 23.04.2012 under Section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 to acquire the petitioners homestead land which is in violation of the provisions and spirit of the ordinance, 1982. He further submits that the respondents with a mala-fide intention issued the notice of acquisition for the benefit of the requiring body who is a Private Limited Company though it is an agro based industries but its ownerships belongs to a private limited company whose shares are owned by the private persons and the acquisition process as initiated is neither for a public propose nor in public interest. As such, the impugned acquisition notice was being served by the respondents to acquire the petitioners homestead is to be declared void ahinitio. He also submits that -the right to enjoyment of the property is the fundamental right of every citizens of Bangladesh which has been guaranteed by our constitution. However by issuing the impugned notice in violation of the relevant laws the respondents have infringed the fundamental right of the petitioners and if so the proposed acquisition is held the petitioner will he thrown out form their homestead. Therefore he prayed for making the rule absolute by declaring the impugned acquisition notice issued by the respondents is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

8. On the other hand Mr. Mahbubey Alam. the learned Attorney General appearing with 10 Mr. Bishowjit Roy and Mr. Md. Ekramul Hoque, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the respondent Nos. 1 and 3 submits that the land in question was proposed to be acquired for public purpose: as because the proposed industries wherein thousands of people of the locality are supposed to be employed. He further submits that the local harvests mainly potato and other food grains are produced in the said locality in a large scale and if the proposed cold storage he established the agro based crops and harvests production will be protected and the local farmer and inhabitants of the locality will he benefited at large. Therefore, he emphasis on his submissions that the proposed acquisition notice was served for public purpose as well as in public interest. The learned Attorney General referring to a decision, the ease of Razab Ali and others -Vs- Province of East Pakistan and others, reported in 12 DLR-524, submits that though by the proposed acquisition process the requiring body being a private company will have to be benefited but ultimately it will serve it large number of public of the locality by protecting their agro products and also by creating an scope of employment of thousands of people of the locality. As such, the acquisition as proposed was made for a public purpose and is valid under the law. 

9. On our query, is there any agreement executed by the requiring body with the acquiring authority as mandated under Section 15 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance. 1982 before serving notice tinder Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982? The learned Attorney General referring to a decision the case of Mrinalendu Pal -Vs- Divisional Commissioner and others, reported in 2 = BLC(1997)- 495 submits that since the petitioner failed to agitate their grievances in this regard in filing their objection before the acquiring authority under Section 4 of the Ordinance or in their writ petition, the respondents are in a position having no opportunity to controvert the same. As such, the said argument cannot be agitated at this stage of hearing of the rule. The learned Attorney General lastly submits that having though the above two established decisions, more so, our apex Court in the case of Abdus Salam -Vs-Government of Bangladesh reported in 5 MLR(AD)-184 has decided if the acquisition notices issued for public purpose it cannot be challenged under Article 102 of the Constitution. The present petitioners being failed to maintain the legal requirements as enunciated in 2 BLC Case they cannot challenge the notice issued under Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982 at this stage for non-compliance of proposition of Section 15 of the said Ordinance. The learned Attorney General mainly emphasis to his submissions on the point that the property in question as being proposed to be acquired for a public purpose as well as in public interest, therefore the notice issued under Section 3 of the Ordinance cannot be said it is null and void. Furthermore, he referring to Section 44 of the Ordinance, 1982 submits that the law itself debarred any party to file any suit or any application in respect of any order passed or any action taken or to be taken in pursuance of any power conferred under this ordinance. Thus, he urges for discharging the rule. 

10. Heard the learned Advocates of the respective parties, perused the writ petition, affidavit-in-position and the annexure as annexed thereto. It appears from the impugned notice dated 23.04.2012 issued under Section 3 of the Ordinance. 1982 which is annexure-A to the writ petition; the said notice was issued in the following manner: 
“যেহেতু নিম্নোক্ত তফসিল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তি কৃষি ভিত্তিক শিল্প প্রতিষ্ঠান চান্দিনা ফার্মল্যান্ড এন্ড কোল্ড স্টোরেজ লিঃ এর বর্ধিত করন প্রকল্পের জন্য জনকল্যান মূলক উদ্দেশ্য এবং জনস্বাতে প্রয়োজন সেহেতু এক্ষনে ১৯৮২ সনের স্থাবর সম্পত্তি অধিগ্রহন ও হুকুম দখল অধ্যাদেশ (১৯৮২ সনের ২নং অধ্যাদেশ) এর ৩ ধারার সিদ্ধান্ত অনুযায়ী এতদ্বারা সংশ্লিষ্ট সকলের অবগতি জন্য নোটিশ জারী করা হইল যে উক্ত সম্পত্তি সরকার কতৃক অধিগ্রহনের প্রস্তাব করা হইয়াছে।
উক্ত সম্পক্তিতে স্বার্থবান কোন ব্যক্তি এই নোটিশ জারীর ১৫(পনের) দিনের মধ্যে প্রস্তাবিত সম্পত্তি অধিগ্রহনের বিরুদ্ধে নিম্ন স্বাক্ষরকারীর নিকট আপক্তি দায়ের করিতে পারেন।

11. It further appears from the annexure, those have been annexed to the respondents affidavit-in-opposition. particularly from Annexure-1 series, it shows that the Board of Investment which is being under the office of the Prime Minister, in approving the project "Chandina Farmland and Cold Storage Limited" vide its letter dated 20.04.2011 specifically mentioned and requested the respondent No.1, the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla to submit a full report with its opinion in acquiring 2.23 acres of private land in favour of the aforesaid project other than contrary to the acquisition of the land such as homestead, roads or high ways, school, college, mosque, madrasha, temple or other  religions structures and having any legal disputes or suits involves thereon. The Deputy Commissioner, Comilla then following such directives of the Board of Investment, vide its Memo dated 28.04.2011 asked the Assistant Commissioner (Land), the respondent No. 3 herein, to sent a report after holding spot investigation to the said 2.23 acres of land as proposed to be acquired for the purpose of Chandina Farmland and stating in the report in detail' whether there remains any homestead or other religious structures and legal disputes or suits as contrary to the acquisition. Accordingly, in response to that letter of respondent No. 1, the respondent 3 vide its memo dated 09.05.2011 submitted a report categorically mentioning therein that the land in question though was recorded as vested property but ultimately under the V.P. Case No. 38 of 1997 and 77 of 1998, the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla vide its memo No. ৭২৫/১(৩)কুম/ভিপি dated 30.08.1999 released 0.30 acres of land in favour of the petitioner Rahima Khatun and one Harunur Rashid and on the said 0.30 acres of land they are residing there by erecting their houses. The respondent No.3 in the said report specifically mentioned "প্রতিবেদন পযালোচনায় আরো দেখা যায় যে সংশ্লিষ্ট প্রতিষ্ঠান কর্তৃক আবেদীত ৪৪৮ (এস এস ১৫৯) দাগের ০.৬১ একর ভূমি নিয়ে দেওয়ানী ১১৩/২০১০ নং মামলা চলমান থাকলেও বসতবাড়ি রাস্তাঘাট স্কুল কলেজ মসজিদ মাদ্রাসা মন্দির গীর্জা বা অন্যকোন স্থাপনা নেই এবং আবেদীত ৪৫০ (এস এ ১৫২) দাগের ০.০৩ একর ভূমিতে বসতবাড়ী ব্যতিত রাস্তা অন্যকোন স্থাপনা নেই।” (Under lined to emphasis). 

12. Upon going through the above spot inquiry report of the respondent No. 3 (Annexure-I series), it reveals that the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Chandina intelligently made his report stating that in 0.61 acres of land though there is a suit being No. 113 of 2010 is pending but there is no homestead or religious structures, simultaneously in respect of 0.30 acres of land (i.e. the land in question) other than homestead there is no roads or high ways. School, Mosque, Mdrasha, Temple and other religious structures remains thereon. It is very interesting that on the prayer of the requiring body, "Chandian Farmland and Cold Storage Limited", the Board of Investment in approving the said project by their letter dated 20.04.2011 categorically asked the respondent No. 1 to submit a report mentioning as to the proposed private land may not contrary to the acquisition having there remains any homestead, religious structures and soil or legal disputes. However, it shows from the report dated 09.05.2011 submitted by the respondent No.3, on the query of respondent No. I. that a suit being No. 113 of 2010 is pending relating to the proposed 0.61 acres of land and on the 0.30 acres of land as proposed to be acquired, the petitioner No.1 Rahima Khatun and one Harunur Rashid are residing with their family members by erecting their houses thereon for long time. Having such assertions though have been made in the spot investigation report but disregarding such spot inquiry report and disobeying the query of the Board of Investment the present respondents proceeded with the acquisition proceedings vide L.A. Case No. 7/2011-12 by issuing the impugned notices under Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982 and proposed to acquire the petitioners' homestead land and also is going to take further action under Section 5 of the Ordinance. 1982 which is very much contrary to the letter of the Board of Investment dated 20.04.2011 and also as of the letter of respondent No. I dated 28.04.2011 who requested the respondent No. 3 to submit a spot inquiry report re-iterating the anxiety of the Board of Investment as to whether the proposed private lands are in contrary to the acquisition. 

13. Moreover, in acquiring land for any person other than the government the Section 15 of the Ordinance, 1982 imposed a precondition of agreement before serving notice under Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982. For proper disposal of the rule we may reproduce or quote here the said Section IS of the Acquisition & Requisition of Immovable Property Act, 1982, which runs as follows: 

"15. Transfer of acquired land to the requiring person other than the Government- (I) When any property is proposed to be acquired for any person other than the Government, such person shall enter into an agreement with the. Government in such form us may be prescribed before a notice under section 3 is published. 
(2) When the property in respect of which an agreement has been entered into with a person under Sub-section (I) is acquired under section II, the Government shall, on the performance by such person of his part of the agreement, transfer the property to the person by executing a deed in such from as may be prescribed and in accordance with the law for the time being in force." 

14. From the above provisions of law it transpires that the acquiring authority i.e. the government in acquisition of a property in favour of the requiring body who is a private person or a private entity other than the government, the said requiring body shall have to execute an agreement with the government before issuance of the notice under Section 3 of the Ordinance. But on our query either the petitioner or the respondents failed to show us any of such agreement as has been executed by the requiring body with the acquiring authority; though admittedly the requiring body is firmly found as a private limited company whose shares are belonging to some private persons. 

15. In the case of Sankar Gopal Chatterjee and others -Vs-Additional Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka Division and others reported in 41 DLR( I 998)-326, his Lordship Mr. Justice Mustafa Kamal on a similar point of issue in deciding the case categorically observed in that Judgment at paragraph-9- "The provision of Section 15 is not directory but mandatory. Before the Deputy Commissioner acquires the jurisdiction to publish a notice under Section 3 an agreement with the non-government requiring body is a sine qua non for the exercise of such power. It is a condition precedent. It cannot be whittled down by any device." 

16. In relying to that decision of 41 DLR case our Appellate Division in the case of Malik Mehdi Kabir and another -Vs-Rabitatal-Alam-al-Islami and others reported in 63 DLR(AD)-109 in deciding  the case at Paragraph- 17 of that judgment, their Lordships categorically observed: 
"Section 15 is a mandatory provision of law to be complied with by the requiring body before the acquiring authority proceeds for acquisition of the land if such acquisition is made not for public purposes of the Government". 

Their Lordships also observed at paragraph-15 of that judgment: 

"The purpose for entering in to such agreement is to initiate the process of acquisition so that the person on whose favour the land will be acquired gets possession from the Government on payment of compensation. The obligation of the requiring body under the agreement is to deposit compensation money within time specified therein and the obligation of the acquiring authority is to acquire the land after performance of formalities and then to handover possession to the requiring body. If the latter does not deposit the compensation money within the specified time, the acquiring authority will not be able to pay the compensation to the affected person under Section 10 and if the compensation is not paid the Deputy Commissioner has no power to take possession from the affected person. The payment of compensation is a precondition for taking over possession of the land. Thus there is no scope on the part of the acquiring authority to complete the process of acquisition as per provisions of the Ordinance unless the requiring body deposits the compensation money as per agreement." 

17. In reliance to the above two decisions we are unable to accept the submissions advanced by the learned Attorney General referring to the decision reported in 2 BLC-495 and the decision reported in 12 DLR-524 which does not overcome the query of this Court; as it appears that the judgment reported in 12 DLR-524 was passed before enactment of the Ordinance, 1982 and also before coming into force of Section 15 of that Ordinance. In acquisition of a property in favour of the requiring body who is a private person other than the government, the mandatory provision of agreement is to be executed by the requiring body before issuance of notice under Section-3 as mandated by Section 15 of the Ordinance-1982. Which is not a factual aspect to be rebut but a legal proposition and that should be maintained by the respondent government who being the acquiring authority and they are bound to follow the requirement of law enunciated in the statute and they should have to follow the same before issuance of the notice under Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982. However, in the present case we do not find any such agreement executed by the requiring body though admittedly the acquisition process was started though L.A. Case No. 7/2011-12 in favour and for the benefit of a private limited company. 

Of course, there is no doubt that the purpose of acquisition was for the public purpose and of public interest also, as the local people and farmers of the locality will be benefited by the expansion of Chandina Farmland and Cold Storage Limited and there will he an opportunity of employment of thousands of people. 

18. But it is unfortunate that the acquiring authority i.e. the present respondents disregarding the spot inquiry report and the mandatory Provisions of Law proceeded with the acquisition process by infringing the petitioners' fundamental right of housing: though the petitioner or the respondents failed to show before this Court any of such agreement as to he executed by the requiring body with the acquiring authority before serving notice under Section 3 of the Ordinance as provided by Section 15 of the said Ordinance. 1982, since having admittedly the requiring body „, is a private limited company. 

19. In the premises and the discussions made herein above, we find merit in the rule and thus, the rule succeeds. 

20. In the result the rule is made absolute. The impugned notice dated 23.04.2012 issued under Section 3 of the Ordinance, 1982 arising out of L.A. Case No. 7/2011-12 proposing to acquire the petitioners' land is declared without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

21. Communicate the judgment and order at once.

End.
