“এমতাবস্তায় ১ও২ নং বিবাদীর বানোয়াট কাগজপত্রে আল্লাহর নামে উতসর্গীকৃত সম্পত্তির স্বত্ব স্বার্থ ও দথল বা অধিকার নষ্ট হইতে পারে না। যেহেতু সি-এ-রোল এ মোতওয়াল্লী সূত্রে অত্র এস্টেটের নাম শুদ্ধভাবে লিপিবদ্ধ রহিয়াছে।


In paragraph No. 8 of the plaint, the plaintiff stated further as follows: 
“এই ব্যাপারে বাদী সেটেলমেন্ট অফিসার ঢাকার আদালতে ইস্ট বেঙ্গল এস এ টেনেন্সি এক্ট ৫০ ধারা অনুযায়ী মোকদ্দমা দায়ের করিলে উক্ত নবাব কোর্ট অব ওয়ার্ড এর নামীয় সিএ রোল ২৭/০৪/৭৫ ইং তারিখে সংশোধিত হইয়া ফয়জুন্নেছা বিবি ওয়াকফ এস্টেটের নামে সি এ রোল সংশোধিত হয়।”

12. From the aforesaid statements made in the plaint it is crystal clear that the Waqf Estate had only superior interest in the land in suit as Jaminder, because the C.A. Roll prepared in the name of Jaminder for payment of compensation as per C.A. Roll. So the suit is barred by section 3 of the SAT Act, 1950. It is also found from the aforesaid statements of the plaint that the way estate had given alleged lease to the plaintiff the vacant and in lieu of yearly rents which is prohibited by section 26/A of the Nom Agricultural and Tenancy Act and also by section-75/A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 Since by dint of lease of the land no right is L created in favour of the lessee in the lease hold land the plaintiff, a tieless person cannot disturb or interfere with the ownership and possession of defendant No. 9 in the suit property, who acquired title through S.A. and R.S. recorded owner.

13. In the plaint as well in the deposition. Mutwalli specifically staled that the Waqf, Estate had rent receiving interest in the suit property which was acquired by the Government by operation of Section 3 of the SAT Act, 1950 after paying compensation thereof as per compensation assessment roll. P.W.I has exhibited the aforesaid documents like projabili property gazette, compensation payment gazette as exhibit-11 and 18. So, the plaintiff in no circumstances can now change his averments stating that the suit property was not projabili property. 

14. It has already been stated earlier that in the plaint the plaintiff claimed he and the previous plaintiffs Nos. 3-11 are joint lessee of the nonagricultural suit land under the Ainuddin Haider and Faizunnessa Waqf Estate by dint of a lease dated 13.10.1988 and exhibited the said notarized lease deed as exhibit-7. Plaintiff on 16.07.2006 in his amended' plaint stated that Ainuddin Haider and Faizunnessa Waqf Estate had only 'rent receiving interest and he and other 8 persons took lease of the suit land from Waqf Estate but in the next amendment' petition, he wants to introduced the facts that the Waqf Estate is owner of the suit land which is totally.. contradictory of the previous statement. The amendment can only be allowed for determining the real question in controversy bur amendment as sought for in the present petition will widen the controversy. Since the plaintiff cannot invite another person to be added as plaintiff because the Waqf Estate has already been added as defendant in its own motion: It cannot he added in different position as plaintiff. Moreover, by way of amendment the plaintiff cannot take away the right of the defendant accrued through the plaint.

So, if the story of lease is abandoned as prayed for in the petition of amendment of the plaint then he will not have anything to stand. In that case, he would be right less person in the suit land. A right less person can not come to the court with the plaint for disturbing another person in possession of the suit land, even if he has no title. 

15. Now we refereed to certain decision on this subject. In the case of Anwara Begum Chowdhurani-Vs-Nur Jahan Begum and others, 27 DLR (AD) 109 it is held as: 
On the other hand, Mr. M. A. Rouf, appearing for the respondents argued that in deciding this point, the general scheme of the Act is to be taken into consideration. The general scheme of the Act is that for the purpose of taking over all interests that are liable to be acquired under the Act, preparation of record-of-rights is to be made and after final publication of the record-of-rights, assessment of compensation of the acquirable interests is to be made and finally published. It, however, seems that an exception has been made with regard to rent-receiving interests and special provisions for acquisition of the interests of certain rent-recovers have been made in Chapter II of Part 11 of the Act. According to the provisions of this Chapter, rent-receiving interests can be acquired by publication of Notification under section 3 of the Act even before the general provisions of the Act are given effect to, that is, before preparation of the record-of rights and preparation and publication of the Compensation Assessment roll. It may also be pointed out that according to the provisions of section 3 of the Act, before introduction of the sub-section (2a) M section 3 by way of amendment. Notification under section 3 was to be published with re3ference to particular estates, talks, tenures, holdings and tenancies and in respect of all rent-receivers whose properties were under the management of court of Wards Act, 1879. Sub-section (2a) was enacted and introduced in section 3 of the Act by Ordinance No.III of 1956. This provision namely, sub-section (2a) empowers the Government to publish Notification under section 3 in respect of rent-receivers by name or by reference to areas wherein they have interests or in such other manner as the Government might determine. It is after this amendment that general Notification dated 2nd April, 1956 were issued District-wise in regard to all rent-receiving interests which thereafter vested in the Government with effect from 14.4.56 in terms of those Notifications. So, Mr. Rout submitted that it was futile to argue that these interests. which were the subject-matter of the general Notifications, contained even after 14th April. 1956 and that they did not vest in the Government. His contention was that in the instant case the rent-receiving interests of the raiyat legally vested in the Government which became the proprietor by virtue of acquisition of the said interests. Accordingly from 14.4. 56 the Government alone became entitled, under the law, to receive the rent. The previous rent-receivers became divested of the right to receive rent and consequently they disappeared from the sense. On this point reference was made to subsection (4)(e) of section 3 which runs thus:

"all tenants holding lands in such estates, taluks tenures, holdings or tenancies directly tinder the rent-receiver specified in the notification under sub section (I), shall become tenants directly under the Provincial Government and shall pay rent at the existing rate, in respect of the rent-paying lands so held by them to the Provincial Government and not to anybody else." 'The next contention urged by the learned Counsel for the appellants was that in the absence of any specific provision in the Act conferring the right of pre-emption to an upgraded under-raiyat as a raiyat, no right of preemption tinder section 26F of the B.T. Act can be available to such a raiyat under the said Act and that in claiming pre-emption in the instant case the respondents sought to take advantage of two laws, i.e. section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and section the respondents firstly claimed that tinder the state Acquisition and Tenancy Act and section 26F of the B.T. Act. It was pointed out that the respondents firstly claimed that under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act the status of the under -raiyat was raised to that of a raiyat after acquisition of the rent-receiving interests of the latter and accordingly secondly, they sought to obtained pre-emption of the raiyati interest under section 26F of the B.T Act. It was, therefore, submitted that the respondents should not be allowed to take advantage of both the laws according to convenience only to suit their purpose, i.e., the upgrading of the under -raiyat to the status of a raiyat under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the relief by way of pre-emption under the B.T. Act. He accordingly urged for dismissal of the applications for pre-emption of the disputed land. This contention of the learned Counsel does not appear to be tenable inasmuch as the right which became available to the respondents was not their, own creation. The said right was created by a statute. It is an unending fact that the rayati interests in the present case, in view of the under raiyat there under, was a rent-receiving interest within the meaning of the Act. The rent-receiving interests of the raiyat, as already stated, vested in the Government. The Government became the proprietor by virtue of acquisition of the said interests. Thereafter the rent-receiving raiyat was divested of his right and consequently disappeared from the field. Naturally the under-raiyat was automatically upgraded as a raiyat under the Government, there being no intermediate interest in between. Part V of the Act not having come into operation at the time the transfers in the instant case were made and the applications for pre-emption having been filed when the B.T. Act was in force, the right to claim preemption could be exercised under the law in force." 

"Having considered the contentions of the learned Counsel with reference to the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act as well as the relevant provisions of the B.T. Act, we arc inclined to hold that the view expressed in the case of Mubsher Ali that after the Notification issued under section 3 of the Act, the status of the under-raiyat became upgraded to that of raiyat, was correct and the impugned judgment of the learned Single Judge of the High Court, being based upon that view, calls for no interference."

16. In the ease of People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet and others-Vs-Sri Sri Madan Gopat Jew Bigraha and others, 33 DLR (AD) 13 it is held as:-
"It is to be observed that prayers as set out in the plaint clearly challenge the notification made under section 3 of the Act as null and void and as such all consequences following there from on the acquisition of the Debuttor property were also challenged and so an injunction was sought for. It is to be further observed that it is now well settled on the authority of Jalil Ahmed Vs. The Province of East Pakistan. 19 DLR 106 decided by a Special Bench and affirmed by the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Tanvir Ahmed Siddiky Vs. The Province of East Pakistan 1968 20 DLR (SC) 144 PLO 1968 S.C. 185. That on the Act. All rent receiving interests including that of Debuttor and Waqf estate stood acquired and all non-retainable khan land also stood vested in the Government. This part of the proposition was overlooked by the Courts below. 
There is another fact which needs top be noted that in the year 1963 notifications under section 43 of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act have been published acquired of all interests other than those already acquired under section 3 of the Act completing all acquisition proceedings under the Act. All the notifications have been published in the Official Gazette covering all districts of Bangladesh. Another fact that requires to be noted is that President's Order No. 90 of 1972. The Bangladesh (Legal Proceedings (Third) Order 1972, was 
Kamrul Ahsan Shelim & Ors 2313LTOLC1))2015 promulgated on 3rd August, 1972 long after the observation made in some of the decisions of the High Court. Dacca on the retention by the Mutwalli or Shebait of an estate on account of non-preparation of the compensation assessment roll. This enactment has been promulgated long after all the acquisition proceedings were completed and long after the observations of the High Court made regarding the non-preparation of the compensation assessment roll. The enactment made in President's Order No. 90 of 1972 clearly states that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force. on the commencement of this Order all suits, appeals applications and other legal proceedings pending or continuing or deemed to be pending or continuing in any court against the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in which the legality or validity of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 1950 or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance. 1956 or of any other law making any amendment in the said Act or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question shall abate, and all orders, including orders of injunction and other interlocutory orders passed in such suit, appeals applications and other legal Proceedings shall cease to have any effect; and; and no court shall entertain and no person shall bring fresh suit, appeals application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question. 

The directive in the law is therefore clear that on the costing into operation of this Order, notwithstanding any other earlier view of law on the subject, a pending proceeding or a proceeding which is sought to instituted challenging or calling in question the acquisition of any property under any of the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act shall abate and no proceedings shall be instituted in any Court. 

To revert back to the prayer made the plaint, it is manifest that the plaintiff respondent in clear language challenged the notification of 2nd April, 1956 as null and void and claimed immunity of the Debuttor estate from acquisition. All other prayers a consequential prayers following therefore. The plaint, as it stands cannot but abate being hit by President's Order No. 90 of 1972." 

17. In the case of Promode Ranjan Saha and others-Vs-Government of Bangladesh and another. 33 DLR (AD) 53 it is held as:- "There can be no denying the fact that Plaintiffs sought to challenge the acquisition of their Hats and Bazars made under the general notification dated 2.4.56 issued under section'3(l ) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, and so it is directly hit by President's Order No. 90 of 1972, which gives a clear mandate of law that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law of the time being in force, on the commencement of the Order, all suits. appeals applications and other legal proceedings pending or continuing Or deemed to he pending or continuing in any Court against the Government of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh which the legality of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 E.B. Act No. XXVIII of 1951), or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (EB. Ordinance No. III of 1956) of as other law making any amendment in the said Act or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question shall abate, and all orders, including orders of injunction and other interlocutory orders passed in suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceeding shall cease to have any effect; and no Court shall entertain and no person shall bring any fresh suit. appeal, application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question." 

18. In the case of Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate and others-Vs-Resheda Begum and others, 14 MLR (AD) 401 it is held as: "Learned Advocate appearing for the leave petitioner, when confronted with the aforesaid gazette notifications dated 24.03.1952 and 29.02.1956, as to acquisition of rent receiving interest and the vesting of lands of the leave petitioners, including the case lands, found it difficult to substantiate the locustandi of the leave petitioner in challenging the draft records of right prepared in the names of the respective writ petitioners in respect of their respective case lands prepared during the Mohanagar Survey. Further with the publication of the gazette notifications dated 24.03.1952 and 29.02.1956 the leave petitioner ceased to have any right, title and interest and possession in the case lands, because of acquisition. And vesting of said lands in the Government. The learned Additional Attorney General could not deny the granting of the ground rent payment receipts, copy of which have been annexed to the affidavit-in-opposition, admitting the writ petitioners as tenants under the Government. 

On plaint reading of the Rule 42A, quoted above, it appears that the settlement officer is empowered to pass order only on receipt of an application or on receipt of an official report, for correction of an entry in the record of right, procured by fraud, before final publication thereof. Thus the said Rule cannot be applicable in the instant case inasmuch as the record of right as prepared is in accordance with the past records of right prepared during S.A. Operation and R.S. Operation and there being no change as to the names as appearing in the said records of rights the question of fraud in recording the entry of names in the recent record of right prepared after the Mohanagar Survey does not arise. Apart from that after final publication of the record of right after the S.A. Survey the only - mode for correction of the same was through Civil Court and thus subsequent to preparation of S.A. record of right, the R.S. record of right was prepared and alter final publication thereof the mode for correction of any wrong entry appearing in the R.S. record was through Civil Court and without moving the Civil Court no correction in those records of right is lawful or permissible and as such the draft record of right in the instant case having been prepared following the preparation of the S.A. and R.S. records in accordance with law. the attempts of the leave petitioner for correction under Rules-30 and 31 of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955 have failed. The plaint reading of the application dated 14.07,2002, quoted above, allegedly tiled under Rule 42A of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955. ex-facie appears to be a vague application inasmuch as the said application do not contain any specific allegation of any such of fraud and it is the settled principle of law that an application, not having disclosed any act of fraud it its body, is not entertaining and liable to be rejected. Without 'correcting the S.A. Khatian and R.S. Khatian as prepared in respect of the case lands in accordance with law earlier the leave petitioner cannot get its name entered in the recent record of right prepared during Mohanagar Survey allegedly only on the basis of C.S. Khatian." 

"Thus we are of the view that the leave petitioner had no locus-standi to challenge the draft Mahanagar Survey Khatian as prepared in the names of the respective writ petitioners, at-least after publication of the gazette notifications dated 24.03.1952 and 29.02.1956." 

19. Now we may look into Order VII Rule II of the Code of Civil Procedure which is as follows:-"
(a) where it does not disclose a cause of action; 
(b) where the relief claimed is undervalued, and the plaintiff, on being required by the Court to correct the valuation within a time to be fixed by the Court fails to do so
 (c) where the relief claimed is properly valued, but the plaint is written upon paper insufficiently stamped, and the plaintiff, on being required by the court to supply the requisite stamp-paper within a time to be fixed by the Court, fails to do so; 
(d) Where the suit appears from the statement in the plaint to be barred by any law. 
It has been decided by all the courts of this sub continent that any of the sub Rule under Order VII Rule 11 can apply only on reference to the plaint. On a reading of the plaint if it is found plaint attract any of the provision of aforesaid sub Rule of I I of Order VII then the plaint shall be rejected. We have already seen that plaintiff in his plaint has made averments which is sufficient for invoking sub rule (d) of Rule I I of Order VII. 

20. From the aforesaid facts disclosed by the plaintiff mentioned herein above provision of section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and President's Order 90 of 1972 also stands a bar to proceed with the -suit. Sub Section (1) of section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act runs as follows:-Section (1) At any time after the  commencement of this Act, it shall be lawful for the Government to acquire, by notification in the official Gazette, with effect from such date as maybe specified in the notification hereinafter referred to as the notified date, 
(i) all interests of such of the rent-receivers as may be specified its the notification, in their respective estates, minks tenures holdings or tenancies, as the case may be, in any district part of a district or local area, and 
(ii) All interests of all rent-receivers whose properties are, for the time being under the management of the Court of Words under the Court of Words Act. 1879, in their respective estates, taluks, tenures, holdings or tenancies, as the case may be including all their interests in all sub-soil and rights to minerals in such estates, taluks, tenures, holdings or tenancies. 
(2) Subject to the provisions of sub-sections 4, 5, and 6 of section 20, the. Government may also. simultaneously with or at any time after the publication of a notification under sub-section (I) in respect of the interests of any rent-receiver on any estate taluk, tenure. holding or tenancy acquire, by notification in the official Gazette, with effect from such date as may be specified in the notification (hereinafter referred to as the notified date), all or any of the lands in his khas possession of which he shall not he entitled to retain possession under the said section and so much of the lands in his khas possession as has been acquired under this sub-section and has not vested in the Government under clause (a) of sub-section' (4) shall vest absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances." 
Section 3 of sub section 2 of President's order No. 90 of 1972 also look into as:

 Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law of the time being in force, on the commencement of the Order, all suits, appeals applications and other legal proceedings pending or continuing or deemed to be pending or continuing in any Court against the Government of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh which the legality of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 E.B. Act No. XXVIII of 1951). or of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1956 (E.B. Ordinance No. of 1956) of as other law making any amendment in the said Act or of the acquisition of any property made under any provision thereof is challenged or called in question shall abate, and all orders, including orders of injunction and other interlocutory orders passed in suits, appeals, applications and other legal proceeding shall cease to have any effect; and no Court shall entertain and no person shall bring any fresh suit, appeal, application or other legal proceedings in which the legality or validity of any such law or acquisition is challenged or called in question." 

21. Mr. Narul Amin learned Advocate, referred to an unreported decision of the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court. i.e. the case of Salahudin Khan and others-Vs- Md. Abdul Hai Bahar and others, Civil Appeal No. 149 of 2008, in which, the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Bangladesh on the question of rejection of the plaint was of the opinion that: 

"The only claim of the defendants on which they sought to dismiss the suit was that the plaintiff No. I company was not properly represented and the other plaintiffs being neither Directors of the company nor its Share-holders had right to represent the company. In the plaint. it was categorically stated that after the death of Sirajul Islam Khan, Managing Director of the company, plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 being his son and wile became the directors of the company and as such they were entitled to redeem the mortgaged property. The plea taken by the defendants in the application that none of the said plaintiffs have got 5000/ shares to become the director of the company nor the company approved them to the Shareholders of the company are purely question of fact which shall have to be thrashed out on the basis of the evidence of the produced by the parties at the tie of hearing of the suit, particularly the suit being at the stage of peremptory hearing. Considering all statements made in the plaint as well, as in the application, it appears to as that none of the situations as contemplated in Order VII, rule 11 of the Code was attracted. It a true that the provisions of rule 11 are not exhaustive in the matter of rejection of plaint and in exceptional situation a plaint can be rejected under section 151 of the Code even if it does not come within the mischief of this rule, but such situation is absent in the instant ease. It is also a fact that the application for dismissal of the suit was filed after about 9(nine) years from the date of filing of the suit when the same was at the stage of peremptory hearing. The very filing of the application at such a belated stage particularly when the suit was fixed for peremptory hearing does not show bonafide on the part of defendants. It appears to as that the application was filed just to delay the disposal of the suit. In the above context, the learned Joint District Judge while rejecting the application lightly observed that on issue as to the maintainability having already been framed, the same shall be decided along with other issues, the learned District Judge rightly affirmed the said view of the learned Joint District Judge, but the learned Judges of the High Court Division totally failed to consider the above discussed factual and legal aspect of the case as well as observations of the Court below." 

22. This unreported decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondent on the facts of the given case as we see is not applicable because (i) it appears that plaintiff is lessee whose lease has expired, he has no legal title to the suit property; (ii) the law is clear that if the suit land became projabili property as per President's Order No. 90 of 1972, no suit can proceed; (iii) as per section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950 the lessor of the plaintiff has no title as his rent receiving interest has been vested in the Government and in all purpose; (iv) application for rejection of the plaint has been filed within 2 months from the date of impleading of defendant No.9 in the plaint; (v) in absence of lessor lessee has no legal right or title to maintain a suit for declaration of title. - Since the plaint as we see is barred by law, the suit can not proceed. We find substance in the rule. 

23. In the result, the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. 

24. Plaint of Title Suit No.04 of 2012 is rejected. 

25. Send down the lower court records. 

26. Communicate this order at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ruhul Amin, J: This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment and order dated October 23, 2002 of a Division Bench of the High Court Division passed in Writ Petition No.2597 of 2001 discharging the Rule. The writ petition was filed impugning the amendment of the schedule (published in the Gazette on January 23, 1986) of the Department of Shipping (Engineer and Ship Surveyor of Inland Ships) Recruitment Rules, 1980 and the Memo No.E-1(1)/Part-6/3224 dated 27.3.2001 giving current charge of the post of Chief Engineer and Ship Surveyor, Department of Shipping to the respondent No.5 (Engineer and Ship Surveyor Department of Shipping). 
2. The writ petition was filed stating, inter alia, that on February 5, 1994 Public Service Commission made an advertisement calling application for appointment in two posts of Engineer and Ship Surveyor, that the post of Engineer and Ship Surveyor was divided into three Grades i.e. Grade-I, Grade-II and Grade-III, that in the advertisement the qualification and the experience for being eligible to apply as well as for appointment were mentioned against respective grade, that in the said notification scale of pay of the respective grade was also mentioned, that in the light of the advertisement the writ-petitioner, the respondent No.5 and others submitted their applications for being appointed as Engineer and Ship Surveyor and in due course interview was held and recommendation was made for the appointment of the respondent No.5 in Grade-I and in respect of the writ-petitioner recommendation was made for appointment in Grade-II and thereupon notification was made as to appointment of the writ-petitioner and the respondent No.5 and on January 18, 1995 writ-petitioner. joined as Engineer and Ship Surveyor in Grade-II, that on March 28, 2001 Chief Engineer and Ship Surveyor, Department of Shipping went on leave preparatory to retirement and thereupon by the order dated March 27, 2001 the. respondent No.4, Director General, Department of Shipping made recommendation as to respondent No.5 for holding current charge of the post of Chief Engineer and Ship Surveyor in spite of writ-petitioner being senior to the said respondent No.5, that the writ-petitioner on May 7, 2001 represented to the respondent No. l, Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Shipping for consideration of writ-petitioner's case for promotion to the post of Chief Engineer and Ship Surveyor, Department of Shipping but without making decision thereof the respondent No.4 did take step for making recommendation in respect of the respondent No.5 for promotion in the post of Chief Engineer and Ship Surveyor, that in 1980 when the Department of Shipping (Engineer and Ship Surveyor of Inland Ships) Recruitment Rules, 1980 were framed there was no gradation and the qualification as regard the post of Engineer and Ship Surveyor of Inland Ships was one of the three alternatives mentioned in the schedule but on January 23, 1986 the schedule of the Department of Shipping (Engineer and Ship Surveyor of Inland Ships) Recruitment Rules, 1980 was amended and the post of Engineer and Ship Surveyor of Inland Ships was classified as Grade-I, Grade-II and Grade-III fixing qualification and experience for the respective grad6, that in 1995 respondent No.2, Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Establishment appointed a committee to scrutinize the recruitment rules for the purpose of making Unified Recruitment Rule of the Department of Shipping, that respondent No.2 asked the respondent No.1 to propose Unified Recruitment Rule for the Department of Shipping and the respondent No.1 prepared a -set of Unified Recruitment Rule and forwarded the same to the respondent No.2 and in the proposed Unified Rule the post of Engineer and Ship Surveyor was eliminated, that although recommendation was made as back in 1995 but the Unified Rule has not yet been finalized. 

3. It is the contention of the writ petitioner that making gradation of the post of Engineer and Ship Surveyor of Inland Ships by amendment of the schedule of the Recruitment Rules, 1980 was violative of equity clause as in Article 27 and 29(1) of the Constitution and that the classification so made between the Graduates in Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering and the Marine Engineers with class-1 certificate with competency is highly unreasonable as the same is not based upon any material, substantial and real difference and the classification so made is not logically correct, natural and intrinsic, nor even the said classification is founded upon any intelligible difference, that the gradation so made and the classification for the respective grade is highly discriminatory and that the classification so made is also capricious, fanciful and patently unjust, that giving current charge of the post of Chief Engineer and Ship Surveyor, Department of Shipping by the office order dated 27.3.2001 to respondent No.5 is violative of the writ-petitioners right to protection of law guaranteed by Article 31 of the Constitution and also violative of the equality provision guaranteed under Article 27 and 29(1) of the Constitution, that treating the respondent No.5 senior to the writ-petitioner is violative of the Article 31 of the Constitution and also violative of Article A(II) of the General Principles of Seniority adopted by the Government by Memo No. I /16/69D-2 dated 31.12.1970, that the recommendation made by the respondent No.4 for giving current charge of the office of the Chief Engineer and Ship Surveyor to the respondent No.5 who is junior to the writ-Petitioner was violative of the equality clause as in the Constitution. 

4. The Rule was opposed by the respondent No.5 by filing affidavit-in-opposition stating, inter alia, that the writ petition so filed is not maintainable being barred by limitation, estoppel, waiver and acquiescence since the writ-petitioner challenged the amended schedule which was made on January 23, 1986 and as under the said Rule the writ-petitioner was appointed in Grade-ll because of his qualification and he joined in Grade-11 on January 18, 1995 while the respondent No.5 joined in Grade-I on December 26, 1994, that had the writ-petitioner been aggrieved because of his appointment in Grade-II he ought to have challenged the legality of the amended Rule immediately after he noticed his appointment in Grade-II and having had not done so the petitioner being guilty of latches in filing the writ petition only in 2001 same was bad for latches and delay, that the writ petition for all practical purposes being related to the claim for grade and promotion the same is not maintainable and that the matter of promotion is exclusively matter for adjudication by the Administrative Tribunal, that in the advertisement made by the Bangladesh Public Service Commission in 1994 for filling up two posts of Engineer and Ship Surveyor therein qualification and experience with the pay scale against the respective grade were specifically mentioned, that writ-petitioner having and had accepted his appointment in Grade-II and having had joined in the said grade subsequent to the date of joining of the respondent No.5 the writ-petitioner's contention that the respondent No.5 is junior to him is not tenable, that the writ petition has been filed for the speculative purpose of creating a dispute and to delay the promotion cif the respondent No.5 who is fully eligible for promotion on a regular basis, that writ petitioner having had filed an application for promotion to the Grade-I upon completion of 5 years-service in Grade-11 same clearly shows that the writ petition was filed for malafide purpose of delaying the promotion due to the respondent No.5 and the writ-petitioner cannot make any claim as he is not in the feeder post or in the range of promotion, that for the redress of his grievance against giving current charge to the respondent No.5 the writ-petitioner was required to move the Administrative Tribunal and that the redress so sought as regard the giving of current charge to the respondent No.5 is not available in the writ jurisdiction. 

5. The Rule was also opposed by respondent No.4, i.e. Director General, Department of Shipping by filing affidavit-in-opposition denying the material averments made in the writ petition and stating, inter alai, that claim of the writ-petitioner that he topped list of selected candidates is not correct, that from the statement of the writ-petitioner it is evidenced that he was not considered for appointment in Grade-I nor he was appointed in Grade-I post of Engineer and Ship Surveyor and writ-petitioner's application for consideration for promotion to Grade-I after completion of 5 years of service in Grade-II clearly shows that the writ petition has been filed for malafide purpose of delaying due promotion to the respondent No.5, that writ-petitioner was appointed in 1995 in Grade-II as Engineer and Ship Surveyor, that for the redress of writ-petitioner's grievance against the order giving current charge to the respondent No.5 of the post of Chief Engineer and Ship Surveyor, Department of Shipping he was required to approach the Administrative Tribunal, that the writ-petitioner had challenged the legality of the amendment of the Recruitment Rules, 1980 by the Gazette Notification dated January 23, 1986 although he was appointed under the said amended Rule in Grade-II and he upon accepting the appointment in Grade-II joined therein in January 1995 as such he is estopped from questioning legality of the amendment of the Rule made in 1986. Moreover writ-petitioner having been appointed in 1994 in Grade-II as Engineer and Ship Surveyor, joined in 1995 and had he been aggrieved by the said amendment he ought to have challenged the legality of the amended Rule immediately after his appointment and that having had not done so the writ petition so filed challenging legality of the amendment made in 1986 suffers from latches and negligence and as such the same is liable to be dismissed. 

6. The High Court Division on the findings that in the background of the materials on record the petitioner can neither claim to be senior to the respondent No.5 nor can claim for promotion to the post of Chief Engineer on the ground of seniority, that there is hardly any scope for deciding the question whether the qualifications/degrees as the writ-petitioner and the respondent No.5 holding are equal or one is higher to the other, that the concerned authority in the light of the Rule of 1980 as had given preference to the degree of Marine Engineer with Class-I certificate of competency and that being the requisite qualification which the writ-petitioner had not the appointment of the respondent No.5 in Grade-1 cannot be questioned by writ-petitioner, that amendment made in 1986 in the Rule of 1980 was not made to favour anybody or to deprive anybody in any respect and as such the amendment cannot be considered malafide and writ-petitioner has no reason to challenge the amendment of the schedule of the Department of Shipping (Engineer and Ship Surveyor of Inland. Ships) Recruitment Rules, 1980 discharged the Rule. 

7. We have heard the learned Counsel for the petitioner and the learned Counsel entering caveat for the respondent No.5 as well as perused the materials on record. The learned Counsel for the petitioner more or less reiterated the grounds urged before the High Court Division. The learned Counsel also submits that High Court Division was in error in not taking into consideration of the fact, that in the proposed amendment of 1997 the Graduates in Naval Architecture and the Marine Engineering (qualification the writ-petitioner had not at the material time) have been recommended for the same grade i.e. Grade-I and thereby the writ-petitioner and the respondent No.5 have been treated equally. Suffice it to say the proposal has not been made final and that being so the claim of the writ-petitioner being equal to respondent No.5 is misconceived one. The learned Counsel for the petitioner has also contended that there has been violation of the Article 27 and 29(1) of the Constitution. The argument so made is also not well founded since at the time when the advertisement was made qualification and experience for the respective grade was very much in the Rules in 1980 and was also very much in the advertisement and that the undenied position was that the writ-petitioner had not the qualification for being appointed in Grade-I and that he had only the qualification for being appointed in Grade-II and as such the appointment of the writ-petitioner in Grade-II was quite legal and in accordance with law. The contention that the writ-petitioner was senior to the respondent No.5 is also not correct since writ-petitioner joined in Grade-II in January 1995 while the respondent No.5 joined in Grade-I in December 1994. The writ-petitioner has challenged legality of the order dated 27.3.2001 giving current charge of the post of Chief Engineer and Ship Surveyor, Department of Shipping to the respondent No.5, but the same being the matter relating to condition of service the relief sought in the writ petition in respect of the said order dated 27.3.2001 was not available to him since the subject matter of the said order i.e. giving of current charge was the matter for adjudication by the Administrative Tribunal. 

8. In the background of the materials on record we are of the view that High Court Division was quite correct in holding that amendment of the schedule of Department of Shipping (Engineer and Ship Surveyor of Inland Ships) Recruitment Rules, 1980 was not made to favour anybody or to deprive anybody. 

9. In the light of the discussions made hereinabove we find no substance in the petition.

10. Accordingly, the petition is dismissed. 

End.

বিচারপতি শেখ মোঃ জাকির হোসেনঃ- অত্র রুলটি উদ্ভব হইয়াছে নওগাঁর বিজ্ঞ সাব জজ, বর্জা৷নে যুগ্ম 6জ্যা৷ জজ,
তৃতীয় আদালতের দেওয়ানী ১৮৩/১৯৯৬নং আপীলে প্রচারিত ১৯/০৮/২০০১ তারিখের রায় এবং ২৩/০৮/২০০১ তারিখের স্বাক্ষরিত ডিক্রীর বিরুদ্ধে, যে রায় ও ডিক্রীমূলে নওপঁ1 ৫জ্যাষ্কর মান্দার সহকারী জজ,… দ্বিতীয় আদালতেরদেওয়ানী ৬১/১৯৯২নং মোকদ্দমায় প্রচারিত ২৭/০৬/১৯৯৬ তারিখের রায় এবং ০৩/০৭/১৯৯৬ তারিখের স্বাক্ষরিত তিক্রীপরিবতনি পূর্বক আপীল মঞ্জুর হইয়াছে এবং বিচারিকআদালতের রায় ও ভিক্রী রদ ও রহিত পূর্বক মূল মোকদ্দমায়ডিক্রী হই'য়াছে।

২ ৷ রপ্সটি নিস্পত্তির স্বার্থে মােকদ্দমার সংক্ষিপ্ত ঘটনা এইযে, দরখাস্তকারীদ্বয় বাদী হিসাবে দেওয়ানী ৪৬/১৯৮৮নংমোকদ্দমায় প্রচারিত ১০/০৭/১৯৯২ তারিখের রায় ও ডিক্রীভাহাদের উপর কার্য্যকর নহে মর্মে ঘোষনার নিমিত্তে নওপঁ৷সদরে বিজ্ঞ সহকারী জজ, দ্বিতীয় আদালতে দেওয়ানী৬১/১৯৯২নং মোকদ্দমা দায়ের করেন ৷ আরজির সংক্ষিপ্তবিবরণ এই যে, ১নং বিবাদী নালিশী তফসিল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তিবাবদে একখন্ড ডিক্রী হাসিল করিয়াছে উক্ত সম্পত্তির মালিকছিল ২নং বিবাদী-বাংলাদেশ সরকার…১ ও ২নং বাদীগণ উক্তএলাকার এক ভূমিহীন সম্পত্তি 1 সরকারী সম্পত্তি পরিয়াথাকার কারণে তাহারা সেখানে বাড়িঘর নির্মাণে বসবাস শুরুকরিয়া সরকারের নিকট নালিশী সম্পত্তি পত্তন পাইবার জন্যএক দরখাস্ত আনায়ন করে 1 বাদীপক্ষের দরখাস্ত মোতাবেক২১৬/৮৮-৮৯নং বন্দেবেস্ত কেইস মূলে কমিটির সুপারিশবিবচনাক্রমে বাদীপক্ষকে নালিশী সম্পত্তি ৯৯ বৎসরের জন্যচিরস্থায়ী বন্দেন্বস্ত প্রদান করে ৷ বন্দে৷বন্তের মতানুসারেবাদীপক্ষ-সরকার বরাবরে কবুলিয়তি দলিল সম্পাদন করিয়াদেয় ৷ তৎপর হইতে বাদী নালিশী জোত সম্পত্তি দখল ভোগপরিচালনা করিয়া আসিতেছেন 1 ১নং বিবাদী একজন ধুরন্দরমামলাবাজ লোক 1 বাদীর নালিশী জােতে সর্বপ্রকার স্বত্বআছে মর্মে অবগত থাকা স্বত্বেও কতিপয় ণ্…’যাগসাজসীকাগজপত্র প্ৰন্তুতে এক মিথ্যা ৪৬/১৯৮৮নং মোকদ্দমা সরকারের বিরুদ্ধে আনায়ন করিয়া বাদীকে পক্ষভুক্ত না করিয়া একখন্ড যোগসাজসী ডিক্রী হাসিল করিয়াছে। তৎপর ১০/০৭/১৯৯২ তারিখে উক্ত ডিক্রীর বৃনিয়াদে নালিশীসম্পত্তি হইতে বাদীপক্ষকে বেদথল করিবে মর্মে হুমকি প্রদর্শন করিলে বাদীপক্ষে আর মোকদ্দমার কারণ উদ্ভব হয়। বাদী উক্ত ডিক্রী রদ করিবার জন্য অত্র ডিক্রী রদের মোকদ্দমা আনায়ন করিয়াছে।
৩ 1 অপরদিকে ১নং বিবাদীপক্ষ লিখিত জবাব দাখিলপূর্বকবাদীপক্ষের আনিত মোকদ্দমার বিরোধিতা করিয়া বর্ণনা করেযে, অত্র মোকদ্দমা বর্জা1ন আকারে চলিতে পারে না ৷ অত্রমোকদ্দমা দোৰারা দোষে বাব্রিত ৷ অত্র মোকদ্দমা তামাদিআইনে বারিত 1 প্রকৃত বর্ণনায় ১নং বিৰাদীপক্ষ বর্ণনা করেনযে, নালিশী সম্পত্তি বাবদে সরকারের নামে তুংভােবে আর…এস… খতিয়ান প্রস্তুত হইলে ১নং বিবাদী তাহা অবগত হইয়া২-৫নং বিবাদীপক্ষের বিরুদ্ধে ৪৬/৮৮নং ও/সি মোকদ্দমাআনায়ন, ভৈয়পক্ষের সাক্ষ্য প্রদান সমাপন অস্তে দোতরফাসূত্রে রায় ডিক্রী হইঁয়াছে ৷ মােকদ্দমা লেক্যেলীণ সময়েসরকারের নালিশী সম্পত্তি পত্তন দেওয়ার কোন অধিকার ছিলনা বা নাই ৷ উক্ত পত্তন দেওয়া হইয়া থাকিলে তাহাএখতিয়ার বহিভূঁত ৷ বাদীপক্ষ নালিশী সম্পত্তি দখলন্…ভাগকরেন না ৷ উক্ত নং মোকদ্দমায় ২নং ৰিবাদী কােনক্রমেইপক্ষাভাব দোষেৱ কথা অবতারনা করে নাই ৷ বাদীপক্ষেরকােনরূপ কাগজণত্র আদালতে দাখিল করে নাই ৷ বাদীপক্ষে…বদাবী মতে কবুলিয়ত দলিলসহ ৰিবাদীর ডিক্রীর পরে সৃষ্টিহওয়ায় তাহা দ্বারা ১নং ৰিবাদীর 8৬/১৯৮৮নং মােকদ্দমাবারিত হ্ইবেনা ৷ কাংআঁ নালিশী সম্পত্তি বাবদে তবিতিমোকদ্দমায় বাদীপক্ষকে পক্ষ করার কোন কারণ নাই ৷ ফলেবাদীপক্ষের আনিত মিথ্যা মোকদ��দমা খরচাসহ ডিসমিসহৃইঁবে 

8 ৷ বাদীপক্ষ তাহাদের মােকদ্দমা প্রমাণের জন্য ৩ জন সাক্ষী এবং কিছু দালিলিক সাক্ষ্য আদালতে উপস্থাপন করেন ৷ দালিলিক সাক্ষ্যগুলো ‘প্রদর্শনী' ১-১(ক)… ২, ৩(গ), ৪ এবং ৫। হিসাবে চিহিড্ড হয় ৷ অন্যদিকে ১নং বিবাদীপক্ষে তাহাদের মোকদ্দমা প্রমাণের জ্যাৰু ৩ জন মৌখিক সাক্ষী এবং যে সকল দালিলিক সাক্ষ্য উপস্থাপন করেন তাহা 'প্রদর্শনী' এ-এ(১)এ(২) এবং (বি) হিসাবে চিহ্নিত হয় ৷ অতঃপর উভয়পক্ষের আর্জি-জবাব, মৌখিক এবং দালিলিক সাক্ষ্য এবং বিজ্ঞ কৌশুলীদের বক্তব্য শ্রবণসহ মূল্যায়ন পৃর্বক বিজ্ঞ বিঢারিক আদালত মােকদ্দমাটি ১নং ৰিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে দােতরফা সূত্রে এবং অন্যান্য বিবাদীদের বিরুদ্ধে একতরফা সূত্রে ডিক্রী প্রদান করে এবং তর্কিংক্ক ৪৬/১৯৮৮ ও, সি  েকদ্দমার রায় ও ডিক্রী দ্বারা বাদীপক্ষ বাধ্যকর নয় মর্মে ঘোষিত হয় ৷ উক্ত রায় ও ডিক্রীর বিরুদ্ধে বিবাদী-আপীলকারী হিসাবে নওপঁষ্কর বিজ্ঞ জেলা জজ আদালতে ১৩০/১৯৯৬নং স্বত্ব আপীল দায়ের করেন ৷ যাহা বিচারের জন্য… নওগাঁর বিজ্ঞ সাব জজ বর্তমানে যুগ্ম জেলা জজ তৃতীয় আদালতে বদলী হয়। অতঃপর বিজ্ঞ যুগ্ম জেলা জজ নিম্ন আদালতের রায়, উভয়পক্ষের বিজ্ঞ কৌশুলীদের যুক্তিতর্ক শ্রবণসহ তাহা মূল্যায়ন পূর্বক বিচারিক আদালতের রায় ও ডিক্রীকে রদ ও রহিত মর্মে আপীলটি মঞ্জুর করেন ৷ অতঃপর উক্ত রায় ওডিক্রীর বিরুদ্ধে সংক্ষুব্ধ ও অসম্ভষ্ট হইয়া বাদী-প্ৰতিবাদী-দরখাস্তকারী হিসাবে দেওয়ানী কার্যবিধির ১১৫(১) ধারার বিধান অনুযায়ী রিভিশনের দরখাস্ত দায়ের করিলে অত্র রুলটি  উদ্ভব হয় ।

৫। রুলটি শুনানীকালে দরখাস্তকারী পক্ষে বিজ্ঞ কৌশুলী বাবু এস. এন গোস্বামী সঙ্গে বিজ্ঞ কৌশুলী জনাব আশরাফুল আলম রুলের স্বপক্ষে নিবেদন করেন যে, দরখাস্তকারীপক্ষ নালিশী সম্পত্তি ২নং অপরপক্ষের নিকট হইতে ব্লেজিট্রি দালিল মূলে ৯৯ বৎসরের জন্য স্থায়ী বন্দেশ্ববস্ত নিয়া তথা বাড়ীঘর নির্মাণ করিয়া ভোগ দখলে আছেন ৷ যদিও নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে বন্দে1বস্ত নেওয়ার পূর্বেই খালি থাকা অবস্থায়দৱখাস্তকারী-বাদীপক্ষ উক্ত সম্পত্তি ভোগ দখলে ছিলেন। বিস্তু ১নং অপরপক্ষ অত্র দরখাস্তকারী বাদীদের পক্ষভূক্ত না করিয়া কথিত 8৬/১৯৮৮নং ও… সি মােকদ্দমা দায়ের পূর্বক দরখাস্তকারীষ্বাদীপক্ষের অজ্ঞাতে কথিত যােগসাজসী ডিক্রীহাসিল করিয়াছেন ৷ বিজ্ঞ কৌশুলী আরো নিবেদন করেন যে, ২নং অপরপক্ষ উক্ত মােকদ্দমায় হাজির হইয়া লিখিত জবাবদাখিল পূর্বক বর্ণনা করেন যে… নালিশী সম্পত্তি বাদী-দরখাস্তকারীদের রেজিষ্ট্রকৃত দলিলমূলে স্থায়ী বন্দেত্ববস্ত প্রদান করারতথা তাহারা বাড়ীঘর নির্মাণ করিয়া বসবাস করিতৈছেন। বিস্তু তথাপিও বাদী-দরখাস্তকারীদের কথিত ৪৬/১৯৮৮ ও… সি মােকদ্দমায় পক্ষভূক্ত করা হয় নাই বিধায় মােকদ্দমাটিচরম পক্ষভাব দুষ্ট এবং কথিত রায় ও ডিক্রী এই বাদী দরখ1স্তকারীদের উপর বাধ্যকর নয়; বিস্তু বিজ্ঞ বিচারিক আদালত বিষয়টি অনুধাবন করিলেও বিজ্ঞ আপীল আদালত তাহা ভ্রমে পতিত হইয়া তর্কিত রায় ও ডিক্রী প্রদান করিয়াছেন 1 বিজ্ঞ আপীল আদালত রায় প্রদানের পূর্বে কথিত 8৬/১৯৮৮নত্ ও… সি মােকদ্দমার নথি তলবপূর্বক তাহা বিচার বিশ্লেষণ করা উচিত ছিল 1 কিন্তু উক্ত মোকদ্দমাৱ কাগজপত্র পর্যালোচনা ব্যতিত অনুমানের উপর ভিত্তি করিয়া যে রায় ও ডিক্রী প্রদান করিয়াছেন তাহা রক্ষণীয় হইতে পারে না বিধায় ৪৬/১৯৮৮নং ও. সি মোকদ্দমায় নথি তলবপূর্বক তাহা বিচারবিশ্লেষণ সহ… মোকদ্দমাটি নিস্পত্তির স্বার্থে নিম্ন আপীল আদালতে পুনঃবিচারের জন্য ফেরত (রিমান্ডে ) পাঠানোর নিবেদন করেন।

৬ ৷ অন্য দিকে অপরপক্ষে কেহ রুলঢি শুনানীকালে প্রতিবাদবরাের জন্য হাজির নাই যদিও মূল ১নত্ অপরপক্ষ বিজ্ঞকৌশুলীর মাধ্যমে হাজির ইেয়াছেন এবং বিজ্ঞ কৌণ্ডলীরনামসহ রিভিশনঢি শুনানীর জন্য একাধিকবার দৈনিককার্যতালিকায় মুদ্রিত ইেয়াছে 1 দরখাস্তকরীিপক্ষের বিজ্ঞকৌশুলীর বক্তব্য শ্রবণসহ আপীল আদালতের রায় এবংনথিতে সংশ্লিষ্ট অন্যান্য কাগজপত্র পর্যালোচনা করিলাম_ যাহাহইতে সুস্পষ্ট প্রতিয়মান যে, বাদী-দরখাস্তকারী ৪৬/১৯৮৮নংও…সি মােকদ্দমায় পক্ষ্তূক্ত নয় বিধায় তাহড়াতে প্রদত্ত রায়ডিক্রী তাহাদের উপর বাধ্যকর নয় মর্মে তাহা চ্যালেঞ্জেরনিমিত্তে একটি মােকদ্দমা কিন্তু বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন বিচারিক আদালতযদিও বাদী-দরখম্ভেকারীর পক্ষে রায় ডিক্রী প্রদান করিয়াছেনকিন্তু বিজ্ঞ আপীল আদালত বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন বিচারিক আদালতেরঅভিমতের বাহিরে ভিন্ন অভিমত পোষণ করিয়া আপীলটিমঞ্জুর করিয়াছেন 1 সেখানে বিচারিক আদালতের অভিমতেরবিরুদ্ধে জ্যি অভিমত পোষণ করার ক্ষেত্রে কথিত৪৬/১৯৮৮নং ও…সি মোকদ্দমা কাপজপত্র পর্যালোচনা করাউচিত ছিল বলিয়া আমার অভিমত ৷ কিন্তু বিজ্ঞ আপীলআদালত ৪৬/১৯৮৮নং ও…সি ণ্…মাকদ্দমার কাণজপত্রপর্যালোচনা ব্যতিত বিজ্ঞ বিচারিক আদালতের অভিমতেরবাহিরে কিসের ভিত্তিতে সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণ করিয়া ৰিচারিকআদালতের অভিমতকে (রিভার্স) পরিবর্তন করিলেন তাহাবোধগম্য নয় বিধায় বিজ্ঞ আপীল আদালতের কথিত৪৬/১৯৮৮নং ও…সি মোকদ্দমায় কাগজ পর্যালোচনা পূর্বক আপীলঢি দেওয়ানী কার্য্য বিধির আদেশ ৪ ১ নিয়ম ৩১ এরবিধান অনুসরণ পূর্বক পুনঃশুনানী সাপেক্ষে নিস্পত্তির সুযোগপ্রদান করা উচিৎ বলিয়া আমার অভিমত I

৭ I অতএব, ফলাফল, রুলটি চূড়ান্ত (Absolute) করা হইল এবং ৰিজ্ঞ আপীল আদালতের রায় ও ডিক্রী রদ ও রহিত পৃর্বক উপরোক্ত নির্দেশনায় অ্যা…লাকে আপীলঢি নিস্পত্তির জন্য রিমান্ডে প্রেরণ করা হইল।

৮ 1 রায়ের কপিসহ নিম্ন আদালতের নথি যথাশীঘেই ফেরত প্রেরণ করা হউক৷
End.
