full_judgment:
Mr. Mohammad Fazlul Karim, J.- The Civil Appeal Nos.143 and 144 of 2004 arising out of Civil Petition Nos.1624 of 2003 and 688 of 2003 respectively by leave, are directed against the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division dated 09.11.2003 passed in Writ Petition No. 5951 of 2003 disposing of the case against the impugned judgment and order dated 21.05.2003 in Writ Petition No. 1978 of 2003 discharging the same. In both the writ petitions the vires of Sections 5 and 6 of Druta Bichar Tribunal Ain, 2002 was challenged together with the notifications issued under the said Act being SRO No.233-Ain/2003 purporting to transfer Companigonj Police Station Case No.11 dated 12.08.2001 under Sections 147/148/149/448/324/326/307/302/380/347/ 34 of the Penal Code corresponding to G.R. Case No.1003 in Writ Petition No.5951 of 2003 and SRO No.38-Ain/2003 purporting to transfer Bandar Police Station Case No.30 dated 19.04.1993 under Sections 147/148 /149/302 of the Penal Code to Druta Bichar Tribunal, Chittagong in Writ Petition No. 1978 of 2003. 

2. The Government of Bangladesh filed the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.36 of 
2004 against the impugned direction in the judgment and order dated 09.1 L2003 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.5951 of 2003 directing the writ-respondents-petitioners in the leave petition, to pass necessary order within 2(two) weeks from the date of receipt of the order for trial of the Companigonj Police Station Case No. 1 1 dated 12.08.2001 arising out of G.R. Case No.1003 of 2001 /Sessions Case No.11 of 2003 by Druta Bichar Tribunal setting up at any place in the Headquarter at District Noakhali and if it is not done the writ-respondents were directed to modify/ amended the notification dated 02.08.2003 (Annexure-B to the writ petition No.5951 of 2003) deleting the aforesaid Companigonj Police Station. Case Np.1.1 dated. 12.08.2001 appearing at serial No:79 of the list Annexure-B within 3(three) weeks from the date of receipt of the order. This Court granted leave in the aforesaid leave petition by the order dated 18t" April, 2004 and thereupon Appeal No.145 of 2004 was registered. 

3. The writ-petitioner in Writ Petition No.5951 of 2003 moved the High Court Division stating, inter-alia, that the petitioner is the elected Chairman of Basurhat Pourashava, Upazila-Companigonj, District-Noakhali. He is the younger brother of former State Minister for Youth and Sports Affairs, Md. Obaidul Kader, who was elected as a Member of Parliament being nominated by Bangladesh Awami League in 1996. The petitioner and other accused-persons worked in favour of Mr. Obaidul Kader, a nominated candidate of Bangladesh Awami League in the last parliamentary election held on October 01, 2001 and incurred anger and displeasure of the leaders of the ruling BNP-Jamat Four Party Alliance and because of satisfied against the writ-petitioner under the provisions of Druto Bichar Tribunal Ain, 2002. Accordingly, the vires of Sections 5 and 6 of the Druta Bichar Tribunal Ain, 2002, (the Ain), have been challenged together with the notification being under S.R.O. No.233-Ain/2003 dated 02.08.2003 issued under the said Ain as malafide, discriminatory, arbitrary and violative of the fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 27, 31, 32 and 35 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, and the same was issued with the ill motive and purpose to create scope to "pick and choose" policy against the accused for transferring Companigonj Police Station Case No.11 dated 12.08.2001 corresponding to G.R. No.1003 of 2001 to the Druta Bichar Tribunal, Chittagong from the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Noakhali. 

4. The facts leading to the case, as stated by the writ-petition, are that on 12.08.2001 one Didarul Islam, son of Md. Mostafa, of Village-Rampur, Police Station Companigonj, District-Noakhali, a local leader of B.N.P. lodged an First Information Report with the Companigonj Police Station against 97 persons including the petitioner under Sections 147/ 148/ 149/324/326/307/ 302/379/427 of the Penal Code, alleging, inter-alia, that on 12.08.2001 at about 9 a.m. while BNP leaders and workers were in a meeting in their party office, accused-persons being armed with fire arms attacked them and fired shots at them and consequently, one Alamgir died on the spot and 9 others were injured. Police upon a perfunctory investigation submitted charge sheet No.21 dated 26.02.2002 against 49 accused including the writ-petitioner under Sections 147/148/149/448/324/326/307/302 /380/427/34 of the Penal Code. It was stated that after submission of charge sheet, the Cognizance Court No.3, Noakhali accepting the charge sheet taking cognizance sent the case record to the Court of Sessions Judge, Noakhali for trial and the learned Sessions Judge, Noakhali, transferred the case to the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Noakhali for trial, where the case was pending for framing of charge. Meanwhile, Additional Sessions Judge also discharged 4 (four) accused persons from the case under Section, 265C of the Code of Criminal Procedure by order dated 24.05.2003, fixing the date on 16.06.2003 for framing of charge and thereafter, it has been fixed on 26.08.2003 for framing of charge. All the accused hail, from Companigonj 'Upazila, DistrictNoakhali but the Government issued the notification for transferring the case to the Druta Bichar Tribunal, Chittagong with the malafide intention to harass and to deprive them of fair and impartial trial. Accused are very poor and some of them are physically very ill and are quite incapable to go to Chittagong from Companigonj, Noakhali to attend the Druta Bichar Tribunal, at Chittagong and the untold inconvenience, misery and the heavy costs in going to Chittagong and returning to Companigonj would be unbearable on the part of the accused petitioners and that would be repugnant to the scheme of fair trial guaranteed under Article 35 of the Constitution. It was stated that the Druta Bichar Tribunal Ain, 2002 (Act XXVIII of 2002) has been enacted on 15' December, 2002 with retrospective effect from 24th October, 2002. Instant case being Companigonj Police Station Case No.11 dated 12.08.2001 lodged on 12.08.2001, long before enactment of the impugned Act the instant case does not fall within the ambit of Section 1 of the Act, and there is no scope of giving retrospective effect for application of Act XXVIII of 2002 since the same has not been specifically provided for in the said Act. It was further stated in the writ petition that the State being a party in the case, it cannot and should not decide which sorts of cases would go to Druta Bichar Tribunal. The laws of the land should be uniform. One set of accused persons under the same sections within the jurisdiction cannot be tried by different Courts, and the matter is totally contrary to the provisions of Articles 27 and 31 of our Constitution. The provisions of Sections 5 and 6 of the Druta Bichar Tribunal Ain, 2002 confer unbridled and arbitrary power upon the Government to transfer case to Druta Bichar Tribunal under the said Act without recording any reason and without adhering to the principles of natural justice and there is no guideline in the Act, as to when and under what circumstances, this power of transfer could be exercised. 

5. The leave petitioners in Civil Petition No.688 of 2003 stated that the subject-matter of the case under reference being S.T. Case No.542 of 1999 is under Sections 147/148/302 of the Penal Code pending in the Court of Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong corresponding to G.R. Case No.507 of 1993 arising out of the Bandar Police Station Case No.30(4)1993 under Sections 147/148/ 149/302 of the Penal Code. The said criminal proceeding was in the process of trial in accordance with the provision of law of the land but due to the political connection of the informant the case has been listed in Gazette dated 5" February 2003 published by the respondents at the instance of present ruling party ignoring and 
(M. natal Karint,1)207  disregarding the provisions of the Constitution. Petitioners are facing the legal consequences of the case by way of facing the trial and enjoying the privilege of bail but respondents violating the Constitutional provision provided under Article 35 of the Constitution included the case in the list of Druto Bichar Tribunal case on the basis of the so-called power given under Druto Bichar Tribunal Act, 2002. The impugned Act was published in the additional gazette dated 24th October, 2002 and the impugned order of transferring the concerned criminal proceeding to Druto Bichar Tribunal, Chittagong was published in the additional gazette dated 5" February, 2003. The impugned Act and the impugned order are violative of the fundamental right of equality before law guaranteed by Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution, the fundamental right in respect of trial and punishment guaranteed under Article 35 of the Constitution, the impugned Act and order are also inconsistent with fundamental right and not sustainable in law and thereby liable to be declared void. The impugned Act and the order are also contrary to the provision of supremacy of the Constitution guaranteed by-Article 7 of the Constitution. By way of passing of the impugned Act and issuing the .impugned order the respondents acted contrary to the provision of right of life and personal liberty enshrined in the Constitution and as such the impugned Act and the impugned order of transfer are unconstitutional and void. 

6. The High. Court Division, however, upon hearing the Rule, disposed of the Rule in Writ Petition No.5951 of 2003 with the direction as stated above and summarily rejected Writ Petition No.6047 of 2003. The writ petitioners in Writ Petition Nos.5951 and 6047 of 2003 against the judgment of High Court Division filed Leave Petition Nos. 1624 and 688 of 2003 and the Government and others filed Leave Petition No.36 of 2004 against direction in Writ Petition No.5951 of 2003. 

7. Besides these appeals, subject matter of respective civil petitions of all other cases have taken up together as the reasons involved therein are similar and accordingly, are taken up for hearing together and disposed of by this single judgment. 

8. Leave was granted to consider the contention "Mr. A.F.M Hassan ,the learned Attorney General of Bangladesh appearing for the petitioner in Civil Petition-No.36 of 2004 submitted that an under trial prisoner, is also entitled to get speedy trial without being languishing in jail without trial for an indefinite period and it is a fundamental right of an under-trial prisoner to get speedy trial and thus the High Court Division erred in law in granting stay against the spirit of law and intention of the legislature in enacting the Act No.28 of 2002. The learned Attorney General further submitted that section 5 and 6 of the Act 28 of 2002 having been challenged in writ jurisdiction and the said two sections have been found to be the valid law and the decision to that effect has been reported in 55 DLR 636, as such, High Court Division ought not to have granted stay of proceedings while is ruing the rule challenging the vires of certain provisions of the law. The learned Attorney General farther submitted that the High Court Division committed illegality in directing the Government to establish Druto Bichar Tribunal under sections 4 of the Druto Bichar Tribunal Act, 2002 inasmuch as the authority to establish forum for administrating the criminal justice lies with the Government both under section 9 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as well as under section 4 of the Druto Bichar Tribunal Act, XXVIII of 2002 and that thus has exceeded its jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. The learned Attorney General submitted that the High Court Division committed illegality in directing to delete Companygonj Police Station Case No. 11(8)01 appearing as item. No. 79 in the gazette notification under SRO No.33-Ain/2003 dated 2nd August, 2003 transferring the case to Druto Bichar Tribunal, Chittagong inasmuch as the High Court Division has itself having held the law regarding transfer to be valid one and not ultra-vires, the directions to delete i.e. thereby stopping transfer is not in conformity with the law as well as the judgment itself and the order of deletion is without jurisdiction. 

Mr. Amir-ul-Islam, and Mr. Abdul Beset Majumder, learned Counsel appearing for the respondent submitted that Sections 5 and 6 of the Druto Bichar Tribunal Ain is ultra-vires to the Constitution as it tends to destroy the fundamental structure of the Constitution allowing the executive authority to intrude into the area of judicial organ of the Republic including that of the High Court Division having exclusive domain as provided under Article 110 of the Constitution and Section 526 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to transfer a case pending before an ordinary Court of law thereby destroying the balance of the Constitution violating the independence and separation of judiciary protected under the Constitution as basic structure of the same.

The learned Counsel further. submitted that the impugned Ain and the order is violative of Article I/O, read along with Article 35 and Article 22 allowing exclusive domain to transfer a pending case on the ground of general public importance. The learned Counsel submitted the impugned is Violative  of Article  27 read along with Articles 31, 32 and 35 of the Constitution: The learned Counsel further submitted that the impugned Ain in Sections 4, 5 and 6 are inherently discriminatory between the persons similarly situated allows the executive authority la  exercise unfettered and unguarded discretion inasmuch as the Ain does not provide any guideline in determining and deciding which cases are to be transferred or not, nor provided  any criteria :and yardstick nor provides any transparent policy, a neutral hoard or independent  authority Making such determination there by arbitrary "pick and choose leading to discriminatory application allowing the executive authority unfettered and Unguarded exercise of discretion resulting in abase of power which is inherent "in the 'Ain' itself' The learned Counsel further submitted that there being lib guideline as-to geographical proximity; access to  the Court specifying' the area without any rational qualification or nexus leading to arbitrary exercise of power under the impugned Ain' for fortnation of the Court under the impugned Ain the formation of the Courts for the whole Country only under Section 4 causes' eat' hardship and harassment and the same is ultra vires anal Violative of Article 110 of the Constitution."

9. Mr. Salahuddin Ahmed, learned Additional Attorney General appearing for the appellants: in Civil; Appeal. No.145 of 2004 submitted that an under trial prisoner is also entitled to get speedy trial without being languishing in jail without trial for an indefinite period and it is a fundamental right of an under trial prisoner to get speedy trial and that the Act XXVIII of 2002 providing for speedy trial by Tribunal is legal and proper-OW Sections 5 and 6 of the AO XXVIII of 2002 haying been challenged in writ jurisdiction and the said two Sections have been found to be valid law and the decision to that effect has been reported in 55. DLR. 63d and as such, the High Court Division ought not, to have granted stay of proceedings issuing  the Rule challenging the yires of certain the law that the Court. Division committed illegality in directing   the Government to establish Druto 13ichar Tribunal under Section 4 of the ,Druto Bichar Tribunal Act 2002 inasmuch as the authority to establish forum for administrating the criminal - justice lies with the Government both under Section 9 of the Code of Criminal Procedure well as Under Section 4 of the Drum BicharTribunal Act, XXVIII of 2002 and 'thus' has exceeded' its jurisdiction tinder Article102 of the Constitution. 

10. The learned Additional Attorney General submitted that the High Court Division committed illegality in directing  to delete companygonj Police Station Case No.11(8)01 appearing  item No in in the Gazette Notification in SRO Ain/2Q03 dated 2nd. August, 2003 transferring the case to Druto Bichar Tribunal, Chittagong inasmuch as the High Court Division has itself haying held the law regarding, transfer to be valid one and mot ultra-vires, the directions ,to delete thereby stopping transfer, conformity with, the law as well as the judgment itself and the order of deletion is without jurisdiction; that trial before a speedy tribunal is under the identical Code of Criminal Procedure as in a Court of Sessions trying Sessions cases by application of evidence act with right of appeal before identical appellate forum of the Supreme Court, the High Court Division had no speedy mode and manner of trial terminating in conviction, sentence or judgment or acquittal as the case may be and that in the purview of speedy tribunal's jurisdiction only specified nature of grave cases viz murder, rape, fire arms, narcotics are triable and that. in such purview of jurisdiction said offences are tried in consonance with principles of natural justice guaranteeing right of fair trial under the existing law of dispensation of criminal justice by Court of Sessions without interference to a citizen's right to get fair trial as guaranteed under the Constitution. 

11. The learned Additional Attorney further submitted that pursuant to the provision of Article 35(3) of the Constitution the accused having a right to speedy trial, the Government in its anxiety to arrange such speedy trial, enacted the law and that there is no bar in the Constitution in transferring any case to the Special Tribunal so formed by the Ain and that regarding the objection as to applicability of the Ain with retrospective effect; that there is no difference in the matter of awarding punishment and only the procedure being provided, the enactment giving its effect retrospectively for speedy trial and disposal of specified cases in the of justice cannot be regarded as a bad law. Referring to Section 6 of the Ain the learned Additional Attorney General submitted that there is sufficient guideline in making orders to transfer the cases inasmuch as the 
Government in the public interest may transfer cases of grave nature viz murder, rape, arms, explosive substance and drugs and as such, it cannot be said that there is no guideline in the Ain. 

12. In order to appreciate the submissions we refer Sections 5 and 6 of the Ain which run as follows; 

“৫ এখতিয়ার সরকার সরকারী গেজেটে প্রজ্ঞাপন দ্বারা যে মামলা দ্রুত বিচার ট্রাইবুনালে স্থানান্তর করিবে শুধু সেই মামলাই এই ট্রাইবুনালে বিচার করিবে।
৬.  মামলা  স্থানান্তর সরকার সরকারী গেজেটে প্রজ্ঞাপন দ্বারা জনস্বার্থে হত্যা, ধর্ষন, আগ্নেয়াস্ত্র, বিরোস্পক দ্রব্য এবং মাদকদ্রব্য সংক্রান্ত বিচারাধীন কোন মামলা উহার যে কোন পর্যায়ে এমত, দায়রা আদালত বা বিশেষ আদালত বা ম্যাজিস্ট্রেট আদালত হইতে বিচারের জন্য দ্রুত বিচার ট্রাইবুনালে স্থানান্তর করিতে পারিবে।”

It appears from aforesaid Section 5 of the Ain that the Tribunal shall hold trial under said Section only those cases mentioned in the Gazette Notification and the provision in Section 6 provides which eases would be transferred by the Government through Gazette Notification to the Tribunal established under the Ain. It is the concurrent finding of the High Court Division that there is, prima-facie. no hide and sick or choose and pick in making the transfer of the cases. 

13. Now let us consider as to whether there is any foul observation or otherwise foul play in the matter of transfer of the cases or any guideline required for the purpose. In Section 6 it has been provided that the Government in the public interest by making notification in the Gazette may transfer the cases involving murder, rape, arms, explosive substance and drugs which are pending before the other Courts. It has been persistently submitted that the aforesaid provisions are violative of Article 27 of the Constitution. Article 27 of the Constitution runs as follows; 

"27. All citizens are equal before law and are entitled to equal protection of law." 

14. The High Court Division found that there is no major departure of the procedure of trial in the cases. Under Section 17 of the Ain it has been provided that provision of the Code of Criminal Procedure so far as they are not inconsistent with the provision of the Ain shall apply to the proceeding of the Druto Bichar Tribunal. There are of course, in Section 9 of the Ain, provisions for application of Chapter XX of the Code of Criminal Procedure in trial of the cases. On perusal of the provision of Chapter XX of the Code of Criminal Procedure the High Court Division did not find that as a result of holding trial under Chapter XX, in the interest of speedy trial of the cases pursuant to the principle of Article 35(3) of the Constitution, there is any chance of prejudice to the writ-petitioners. 
After consideration of the provision of Article 35(3) of the Constitution providing for speedy trial of the criminal case and also after giving its anxious consideration to the submissions made by the learned Counsel of the appellants, the High Court Division is of the view that the impugned enactment and the provisions of Sections 5 and 6 thereof are not liable to be declared as ultra-vires. 

15. To obtain aim and object of the Ain, provision has been made in Section 4(4) of Druto Bichar Ain, 2002 empowering Government to establish Tribunal(s) at place or places and the said provision is as under; 
“৪. দ্রুত বিচার ট্রাইবুনাল স্থাপনঃ ৪ সরকার যে স্থান বা স্থানসমূহ নির্ধারন করিবে সেই স্থানে বা স্থানসমূহের যে কোন স্থানে দ্রুত বিচার ট্রাইবুনাল বসিতে পারিবে এবং উহার কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করিতে পারিবে।”

Under the aforesaid provision the Druto Bichar Tribunal may sit and transact its proceeding at such place or places as the Government decides. 

16. The broad facts of the case as submitted by the accused, are that the Sessions cases ripe for hearing upon framing of the charge and are usually fixed for hearing in the respective Sessions jurisdiction but issuing the notification in question transferring the cases to the Druto Bichar Tribunal to Chittagong for trial resorting to provisions of the Ain and resulting deprivation of fair and impartial trial inasmuch as the movement of the accused beyond the jurisdiction would lead to unnecessary excess cost of transportation, lodging, finding lawyer and engaging of new lawyer in a Court beyond the jurisdiction would be not only costly but also difficult .to provide instructions for the poor public litigants who are not only financially injured but physically jeopardized solely with the malafide intention to harass and deprive them of fair or impartial trial inasmuch as the accused would be frequently incapable to go to Chittagong from Companigonj, Noakhali a separate district far away from the Court to attend the Tribunal at Chittagong leading to untold miseries and inconveniences rather than the heavy costs on the part of the accused which would be repugnant to the scheme of Tribunal granted under Article 35 of the Constitution. 

Though the Druto Bichar Tribunal Ain was enacted on the I' December, 2002 giving retrospective effect from the 24th October.2002 and the learned Counsel has further Submitted that it is although the accessed Charged of the same section of the Penal Code are tried under the  Druto Bichar Tribunal Ain, 2002 (Act. XXXVIII of 2002) but the certain other accused charged of the same offences are being tried in the Sessions Court, the list of the same in gazette dated St" February, 2003 smack political connection of the informant to the utter detriment' of the accused is Violative of the fundamental right of equality before the law guaranteed under Articles 27 and 31of the Constitution and the fundamental right in respect of  trial punishment guaranteed under the Article 35of there Constitution: The alleged transfer inconsistent thereof; is accordingly not sustainable in law. 

17. The object, intended and purpose of „jurisprudence is for expeditious disposal of cases in the matter of investigation, trial, and prompt delivery of judgment which is in .consonance with the provision of  Article 35(3,) of the Constitution providing that an accused of a criminal offence,shall have the right to speedy and public trial by the defendant through an impartial Court or Tribunal established by law.The actual intent and purpose of the provisions besides other element has provided for a right to a speedy Vial and this right is enshrined in the said Article designed for ameliorating the rigour of criminal trial to the detriment to the right of the accused for getting justice and this right is a right which has been preserved arid protected and safeguard under the, provision of law and the Constitution. Any violation of any form amounts negation of justice and leading to hardship' and suffering 'of the accused and expeditions disposal Of Criminal cases has been-preserved demanding that the 
trial should not  be unnecessarily prolonged for ling should not be conducted to the Utter detriment of the parties and should be held expeditious through a speedy -process least the accused is to neither languish in custody for jot's for no fault of him nor there should be delayed justice ultimately resulting in negation Of justice. 
The recent trend, of delay in disposal of criminal cases has created, havoc in the 'adjudication of justice depriving the parties to get fair and impartial justice within a reasonable time and thereby justice is denied due to pilling of huge 'cases awaiting disposal and accumulation of, cases, of any particular category for long resulting in delay in 'disposal of cases and. pilling of huge backlog of cases.

Speedy trial is the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence and law never intended that this process of bringing the offender to bookor justice in, the case should be. delayed or thus denying the parties to the litigant justice due to protracted litigation amounting to denied of justice. Delayed justice also causes unnecessary 'obstruction in the smooth disposal of the 'case by the Court dispensing with justice.
 
Section 6 of the Druto BicharTribunal Ain has made no stringent provision and there is no reason how the time limit for disposal of the case will affect the petitioner or change of ,venue from one' place to another in respect of specified offences could affect the petitioner's right to trial in Court of law of competent jurisdiction for holding trial thereof.  In our Constitution Article 35(3) clearly provides for that a person accused of criminal offence have the right to have the speedy trial in Consonance with the said provision of law and the age old practice, of disposal of Sessions cases in our Country in session within a very shot space of time has been re-iterated in Druto' Bichar Tribunal' Ain keeping intact practice and 'procedure and principle of trial of 'the 'cases of the nature as specified in the said Ain. 

18. If we consider the provision regarding equality before the law or equal protection Under the law we find that in the instant cases there are' sufficient guideline in the Ain-so as to which classes of cases Of the offenders are  triable by the Tribunal. Scrutinizing the provision laid down in Druto Bichar, Ain we do not find that there was  any chance, of discrimination or legislature made no discriminatory treatment in respect Of the same specified offences. The provision made in the Ain in 'Sections 5 and 6 thereof 'provides for trial ,of specified cases by  Druto 'Bichar Tribunal upon transfer of pending cases of the nature from the Court of the learned Sessions Judges set up' for speedy trial in six -Divisions of the Country It is true  to 'be submitted that 1procedure for trial followed for the normal Court of Sessions jurisdiction  are specifically the same in the Druto Bichar Tribunal. The transfer of the cases of the nature specified in the. Ain, have no chance of adversely affecting ,or prejudicing the 'accused but aim and object of the said 'Ain was for disposal of  the cases within a reasonable promptitude' and/o very, shortest possible 'time -in order to avoid any delay in disposal' causing mischievous  of justice to the accused. The 'purpose of the Ain is to -ensure 'speedy/ trial in keeping with The aforesaid-provision and law and the practice and 'procedure of the Court since not-being adhered to recently due to 'the filing of good number of various types' of cases  in the Sessions Court keeping in view with the universally accepted principle of providing speedy trial to the accused. 

Section 5 quoted 'above specified the types of cases to be tried by the Tribunal and Section 6 specifically provides for offences of murder, rape, fire-arms, explosive substances and (lits may he transferred by the Government in the public interest by way of notification, in the' gazette from the Court of Session or Spedial Court or of 'a Court of Magistrate as the case may be. The Ain in our view does not in airy may affect the right of the accused far less offending any fundamental 'right of the accused because Section 1 specifically provides that the Tribunal shall be deemed to be 'Court of Sessions and the provision of the Ain, shall apply in respect of the trial of the cases before the Tribunal. 

On perusal of the said provision ' Of impugned 'Ain in juxtaposition with the normal law of the land we `do not find that any right of the' accused has 'been 'curtailed to get a free fair and impartial trial before a Tribunal. 
Ditto Bichar Tribunal Ain;-2002 provides for the -purpose and intent 'Of 'framing the law; .যেহেতু কতিপয় অপরাধের ত্বরিত বিচারের জন্য দ্রুত বিচার ট্রাইবুনাল স্থাপন করা সমীচীন ওপ্রয়োজনীয় and accordingly the said 'Ain has provided .provision to Apt up, Druto Bichar Tribunal for speedy trial of certain offences. 

19. Certain provisions of Druto Bichar Tribunal. Ain, 2002 namely, SectiOns 7, 8 and 9.. are required to be examined as to whether the  sane provide for any other procedure for trial of the specified Sessions cases before the Druto Bichar Tribunal.
	Section 7 of the Ain Provides that
	“৭। (১) দ্রুত বিচার ট্রাইবুনাল একটি দায়রা আদালত বলিয়া গন্য হইবে।
	(২) দ্রুত বিচার ট্রাইবুনাল তকর্তৃক বিচারকৃত অপরাধের জন্য সংশ্লিষ্ট আইন দ্বারা নির্ধারিত যে কোন দন্ড আরোপ করিতে পারিবে।

Sub-section ( 1) of Section 7 provides that the Druto Bichar Tribunal shall deem to be a Sessions Court; Sub-section (2) of Section 7 provides that Druto Bichar Tribunal could impose any penalty/sentence for the offences specified in the concerned parent Acts. Thus, from the above, we find that the said Tribunal has the power and jurisdiction of a Sessions Court to deal with the accused in the manner provided by the concerned Act i.e. Code of Criminal Procedure and Penal Code. 

Section 8 speaks of the trial of the cases; sub-section (1) provides that Druto Bichar Tribunal shall try a case from the stage of the case was pending before the Sessions Court. Sub-section (2) thereof provides that the deposition of the witnesses before the Sessions Court upon transfer to the Tribunal shall he treated to be the deposition before the Tribunal and the Tribunal could in the interest of justice as necessary take evidence afresh. Thus, there is no change in any trial procedure before the Tribunal upon transfer of the case to the Druto Bichar Tribunal: 

Section 9 provides that the cases since transferred to the Druto Bichar Tribunal shall be carried out following Chapter XX of the Code of Criminal Procedure as far as practicable. Sub-section (2) of Section 9 provides that cases shall he conducted in a summary procedure unless the punishment of any offences of death penalty, imprisonment for life or more than 7 years in that case the provision of Chapter XXII of the Code of Criminal Procedure shall he followed. An accused enlarged on bail by the Sessions Court upon transfer of the case to the Druto Bichar Tribunal could apply for enlargement on bail and the Tribunal shall dispose of the same following the provision applicable for the offences. 

Apart from above, Section 10 has provided for the time limit for completing the disposal of the case. From the above it is crystal clear that the transfer of the case to Druto Bichar Tribunal has in no way affected the right of the parties as provided in the Code of Criminal Procedure excepting the time frame within which the trial has to be completed keeping the view of the spirit of the criminal jurisprudence and a normal practice and procedure that any delinquent entitled to speedy dispose of the case instead of lingering the same for years together in order to secure the ends of justice. 

20. Moreover, the Ain provides a guiding principle taking the provisions in the Ain as a whole which does not affect the right and obligation of the parties in application of the special provision to specified cases of offences mentioned in the Ain inasmuch as we find nexus both the offences of a particular category and the object with which the Ain was promulgated. In that view of the matter the allegation of discrimination is of no avail as there are sufficient justification of the introduction of Druto Bichar Tribunal Ain for specified offences and for speedier trial of those offences. In that view of the matter we can profitably quote a passage from the decision in the case of Kathi Raning-vs-State of Saurashtra reported in AIR 1952 SC 123 which answered the justifiability of such law and nullified the allegation of 'choose and pick' of any particular cases to be tried in the said Tribunal as under.

"The Ordinance, as I have already stated, purported to amend another Ordinance, the objection which was to provide for public safety, maintenance of public order and preservation of peace and tranquility in the State. It was not disputed before us that the preamble of the original Ordinance would govern the amending Ordinance also, and the object of promulgating the subsequent Ordinance was the same as the object of promulgating the original Ordinance. Once this is appreciated, it is easy to see that there is something in the Ordinance itself to guide the State Government to apply the special procedure not to any and every case but only to those cases or offences which have relation to or connection with the main object and purpose of the Ordinance and which for that reason become a class by themselves requiring to be dealt with on a special footing. The clear recital of a definite objective furnishes a tangible and rational basis of classification to the State Government for the purpose of applying the provisions of the Ordinance and for choosing only such offence or cases as affect public safety, maintenance of public order and preservation of peace and tranquility. Thus, the State is expected to select only such offences or classes of offences or class of cases for being tried by the special Court in accordance with the special procedure, as are calculated to affect public safety, maintenance of public order, etc, and the use of the special procedure must necessarily be confined to only disturbed areas or those areas were adoption of public safety measures in necessary." 

In that view of the matter we are of the view that the equal protection clause of the Constitution has not been violated as the Ain is in respect of the offences specified therein and as such, the classification of the said offences is not arbitrary or caprice but bearing a reasonable relation with the objective which the legislation has in view. 

21. Section 6 of the Ain refers to five distinct categories of offences/classes of offences empowering the Government to direct any one or more of cases, offences to be tried by Druto Bichar Tribunal under the Ain. The specified offences, prima-facie, do not contemplate any particular offender or any particular accused in any particular cases. The emphasis is on 'offence' or 'offences' and not in any way calculated to touch any particular accused. Such classification does not refer to or is not directed towards singling out of any particular person or any particular offences but is directed against the offences, group of the offences or classes of offences or classes of cases mentioned in the said provision of Section 5. In that view of the matter it is of no merit to argue that the Ain is designed to pick and choose of any particular offences or any particular accused. 

22. The provision of Druto Bichar Ain has been thoroughly dealt with in the case of Muhibur Rahnian Manik and others-vs-Bangladesh and others reported in 55 DLR 636 and the issues raised therein were also agitated therein and decided by the learned Judges and set at rest in the said illuminating judgment with which we have no reason to differ or to depart from.

23.Sections5 and 6 of the Ain read together do not Other in terms of necessary implication discriminate both a person or classes of persons or purport to deny to any one equality before law or 'equal' Protection of law because the 'Ain does' not make any such law 'derogatory to the aforesaid principle as the Ain- is applicable 'to the trial of offences or classes offences or classes of case's. Keeping' in 'View the constitutional provision as provides Under Artiele35(3), thus by no stretch of imagination it could be alleged any discriminatory intention the part of the Government because there is no departure from the normal procedure excepting that the cases regarding certain categories of cases specified, in Section be transferred to the. Tribunal for expeditious disposal of the same. Even if discretion could be alleged in stick offences or classes of offences or classes as the case may be but the main object is for speedier trial exercised by the Government in exercise of its duty for providing speedy trial of the cases.  

24. In vices of the above C.A Nos, 143 and 144 of 2004 are hereby dismissed and C.A. No.145 of 2004.1s allowed. Accordingly, in the light of the discussion and finding regarding the validity of the Ain itself and on the principle, of law made the body of the judgment  the C.P.'s are accordingly dismissed and the Druto Bichar Tribunal are directed to dispose of the 'aforesaid respective cases speedily and in accordance with law. 

End.

lawyer: Mr. Abdul Momin Chowdhury for the petitioners. Mr. Nikhlesh Datta ... for the opposite party.
parties:
Sananda Mohan Barua and Ors ------ Petitioners.
